On the eve of her wedding, Liudmyla Ryzhak pressed her delicately embroidered dress, laid out a full white tulle skirt and her husband’s traditionally patterned shirt, then hung them on the bedroom door.

After repeated delays caused by the war with Russia, she was only hours away from marrying her partner, a Ukrainian soldier, in a ceremony in the capital.

But as the couple slept, a Russian strike hit a warehouse across the street from their building, sending a blast wave through the apartment and threatening to stop the wedding scheduled for Tuesday morning.

The pair was soon digging their wedding clothes out of the rubble. Ryzhak had to pull her skirt from beneath the debris, shaking off pieces of broken glass.

Strike followed visit by US envoys

The strike came soon after U.S. envoys visited Ukraine on Sunday, a trip that brought a lull in Russian attacks. The assaults then resumed with drones and missiles. Explosions were heard in Kyiv for almost five hours overnight. Strikes continued during the day Tuesday.

Like many others in Kyiv, the couple decided the attacks would not derail their lives and forged ahead with the ceremony. It had taken a long time for her fiance, Leonid Ryzhak, to make it back from the front lines in eastern Ukraine.

“If God gave me a continuation of life, then why should I put it off?” the bride said. “For someone, it ended. And who can guarantee this won’t happen again tomorrow? That tomorrow won’t come for us? At least for now, I have the right to be happy. Both him and me.”

Liudmyla and Leonid awoke from the blast, which blew out the apartment's windows and scattered its furniture. A burned curtain hung in shreds.

Their ears deafened by the explosion, the couple's only immediate thought was the risk of a second strike. They fled to a shelter with Liudmyla’s 6-year-old daughter and two guinea pigs but without the cat, which had hidden in fright and could not be found.

They were lucky: By the time the second strike hit, they were already safe. The apartment was rendered uninhabitable until repairs are made.

A friendship deepened into love

The two met three years ago through mutual friends, coming together as adults who weren’t looking for anything serious. Both had children from previous marriages.

But the friendship deepened. She supported him through his deployments to the front, and slowly the relationship grew into love. Leonid Ryzhak, who serves as part of a team that deploys bomber drones in the Pokrovsk area, arrived in Kyiv for a long-awaited vacation a week and a half earlier, just as near-constant air raid alerts and daytime attacks began disrupting life in the capital.

For six days straight, the couple went to the registry office but could not submit their documents because of constant air raid sirens.

When they finally succeeded, they were assigned Sept. 8. Nobody could have predicted that their apartment would be badly damaged on the same day.

It wasn’t the first time for Liudmyla. She had already lived through one attack, on Aug. 20, when a strike cut the gas lines and shattered windows in her home. She was badly frightened and for a time was afraid to go back.

Eventually, ordinary life pulled her back in: The wedding was coming, and the children had to go to school.

More attacks hit as they wait at registry office

Eventually, the two put on their wedding clothes and headed to the registry office.

Leonid tried to keep their spirits up. What mattered most to him, he said, was for his bride to be smiling.

“It’s fine. We’ll get through it,” he said.

When they stepped outside their apartment, the courtyard looked almost apocalyptic, with a column of black smoke rising behind a brightly colored children’s playground. Neighbors clearing debris stopped to congratulate the couple.

“We should all be celebrated, that we survived,” Liudmyla replied.

The couple arrived at the registry office on time, at 10:40 a.m.

Leonid wore an embroidered vyshyvanka, a traditional Ukrainian shirt, with a pattern that matched the one on Liudmyla’s dress.

In place of black dress pants, he wore army trousers — he couldn’t dig his own out of the rubble — and black sneakers with fluorescent yellow soles and laces, for the same reason. Liudmyla’s white tulle overlay had tiny, barely visible holes that were torn as she pulled it out from the rubble and broken glass.

Shortly after they arrived, a siren sounded: Another attack had begun, and the registry office closed for safety. The couple waited in the courtyard, unsure how long it would last.

Explosions echoed nearby as strikes hit surrounding districts and fires broke out. Almost three hours passed before the alert finally ended, and the couple hurried back inside.

Against all odds, they became husband and wife

Just before entering the hall for the ceremony, they paused, trading nervous jokes.

“I didn’t even get to finish the repairs at home,” Leonid joked about their now-wrecked apartment.

“I’ve never had such a spectacular day,” his bride replied.

The ceremony went ahead as the officiant told them, “Love is when two people become a team.”

Moments later, the two were officially married.

“We’re gaining a new life, because we survived,” Liudmyla said. “You could probably call (it) a new life because it could have ended today, and none of this would happen.”

In a different scenario, “I wouldn’t be wearing this dress. Someone would be picking out something else for me instead, something darker.”

When life gets busy, cookbook author Emma Petersen knows how hard it can be to get a healthy balance with food.

After studying history at Leeds, where she started a food blog, Petersen, now 29, took a law conversion course and won a two-year training contract with a city law firm. “Those sort of courses are like gold dust, and it was always my plan to be a lawyer, earn loads of money and retire early,” she says.

But achieving that six-figure salary required sacrifices. Fitness fan Petersen, who has completed Ironman Triathlons, says: “Suddenly I had no time to cook, was living off Deliveroo, and didn’t have time to train. I started to get depressed.”

The job itself was manageable, but the truth was Petersen couldn’t let her “social media baby” go. “I burnt out because I was juggling being a lawyer with a social media influencer and ended up doing both badly. So I quit the day I qualified.”

Now, Petersen has 813,000 followers on her Instagram account, and she’s following up her Sunday Times bestselling debut cookbook (2025’s Healthyish) with her second offering: Healthyish High Protein. It’s all about hitting your daily protein and fibre targets naturally with easy meal preps and nutrient counts.

She suggests the current craze for adding protein to everyday foods isn’t always necessary, saying: “I’m not anti-protein powder but we should just cook properly. There’s protein in everything from eggs, cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, lentils and tofu… to meat, fish and dairy.” Petersen adds that her recipes use “everyday ingredients in clever ways”, making for a “more natural way” to add protein to your diet.

She points out everyone benefits from more protein and fibre, whether they train or not. “Protein helps repair and rebuild muscles and cells, and fibre slows digestion and helps you feel fuller,” she explains.

Londoner Petersen, who has just moved to the countryside with her fiance Matthew and is in the process of renovating an 170-year-old cottage, shares her top tips on how to make healthy food exciting…

open image in gallery ‘Healthyish High Protein’ is Petersen’s follow-up to her bestselling debut cookbook ( Pavilion )

1. Max out on more

We’ve been taught that eating healthily means eating less – less carbs, less fat, less calories, less sugar. But Petersen says: “A more mentally healthy way would be to add to it to make it more balanced.

“If you have a slice of toast with a smear of butter on it, you’ll be hungry an hour later. But a slice of toast with chia jam and peanut butter gives you healthy fats and carbs.

“It’s not about taking away – it’s adding things that make it a well-rounded meal.”

2. Build your breakfast

Petersen makes her own granola every week. “My recipe for vanilla cardamom and apricot granola can be substituted with whatever store cupboard ingredients you have. No apricots? Use raisins.”

And she explains how easy it is to get your daily nutrition requirement. “The granola has seven grams of protein, and with yogurt and other bits, you’ve got a high protein breakfast.

“It also has five grams of fibre – a fifth of your daily intake – and that’s before adding fresh fruit.”

3. Get stuffed at lunch

Petersen is all about easy lunches, particularly sandwiches and pitas you can stuff with an array of fillings.

open image in gallery Petersen wants healthy eating to feel satisfying rather than restrictive ( Lucy Richards )

Her favourite filling – and a recipe that features in her latest cookbook, is “a chicken salad with yummy pickles and dill, which are all chopped together so it’s spoonable. You can make a big bowl of the filling and keep it in the fridge.

“And if you want to make your own carbs from scratch, I have a two-ingredient bagel recipe – just yogurt and self-raising flour.”

4. Make healthy food tasty

As a massive lifelong foodie, Petersen is on a mission to make healthy food taste good.

“No one’s gonna get excited about a plate of plain steamed vegetables,” she says. “But if you roast them until they’re crispy and then add seasoning, feta and something crunchy like in my cookbook, you’ll eat the whole tray!”

5. Leave room for the ‘ish’

Not everything we eat needs to be nutritionally perfect. “If you’re craving pasta – eat pasta. Don’t try and feed yourself a salad,” says Petersen. She suggests making your pasta a bit more balanced and satisfying.

”Start with what you love rather than overhauling the way that you eat, and then build it from there. Try to be healthy but leave room for the ‘ish’.”

6. Guilt’s out, happy’s in

Everything in moderation, especially moderation. Petersen believes “it’s just about finding that middle ground between food that makes you feel good, and food that makes you feel good eating it”.

She says, “Don’t feel guilty and think, ‘Oh I need to start again tomorrow.’ If you had a Mars Bar and it made you happy – success. It might not have fuelled you, but you must have enjoyable things.”

And she takes her own advice. “Hey, look, what did we do on our first night in the cottage? Did I cook from scratch? No, I got a Chinese takeaway!”

Brothy Thai chicken and rice

open image in gallery A fragrant, 30-minute chicken and rice bowl with plenty of protein and comfort ( Lucy Richards )

“This is what I make when I want comfort food that still feels bright and fresh,” says Petersen. “The broth is gingery and fragrant, and the rice soaks up every bit of that flavour. A simple, 30-minute high-protein meal that never fails to hit the spot.”

Serves: 2

Prep time: 10 minutes | Cook time: 20 minutes

Ingredients:

2 boneless, skinless chicken thighs

1 tbsp Thai red curry paste

1 garlic clove, minced

2.5cm piece fresh ginger, peeled and grated

300ml chicken stock

100ml oat or soy milk

1 tsp soy sauce (GF: tamari) or ½ tsp fish sauce

1 x 250g pouch cooked jasmine rice

¼ red onion, thinly sliced

1 red chilli, thinly sliced

Handful of fresh coriander

1 tbsp cashews, chopped

Salt and pepper

Olive oil, for cooking

Lime wedges, to serve

Method:

1. Pat the chicken thighs dry with kitchen paper/paper towel, then season with salt and pepper.

2. Heat a drizzle of oil in a deep frying pan/skillet or shallow casserole dish over medium–high heat. Add the chicken and cook for 4-5 minutes on each side until golden and cooked through. Remove from the pan and set aside.

3. Reduce the heat to medium and add a touch more oil if needed, then stir in the curry paste, garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, then pour in the stock, oat milk and soy or fish sauce. Stir to combine and let it simmer gently for 5 minutes.

4. Meanwhile, microwave the rice according to the packet instructions. Slice the chicken into strips.

5. Spoon the rice into bowls, top with the sliced chicken and ladle the fragrant broth over the top. Finish with the red onion, chilli, coriander and cashews, and serve with lime wedges for squeezing over.

Tofu doner

open image in gallery Crispy tofu ribbons turn the takeaway favourite into a plant-powered fakeaway ( Lucy Richards )

“Some nights call for a bit of comfort, and this take on a doner kebab hits all the right spots – albeit in a more healthyish way,” explains Petersen. “The thin, crisped ribbons give you that chewy, meaty texture, while the fresh salad and garlicky yogurt sauce pull it all together. Proof that the best fakeaway nights can absolutely be plant-powered.”

Serves: 2

Prep time: 15 minutes | Cook time: 15-20 minutes

Ingredients:

Baking sheet, lined

½ red onion, finely diced

2 salad tomatoes, finely diced

¼ small cucumber, finely diced

1 tbsp finely chopped fresh parsley

1 tbsp finely chopped fresh mint

2 flatbreads (GF: gluten-free flatbreads)

Salt and pepper

Lemon wedges, to serve

For the doner ‘meat’:

2 tbsp olive oil

2 tbsp tomato puree/paste

Juice of 1 lemon

1 garlic clove, minced

1 tsp ground cumin

1 tsp smoked paprika

1 tsp onion granules

½ tsp cayenne pepper

225g extra-firm smoked tofu, pressed

For the garlic sauce:

100g thick 0-5% fat yogurt (DF/VE: soy yogurt)

1 garlic clove, minced

Juice of ½ lemon

Method:

1. Preheat the oven to 220C fan/240C/475F/gas mark 9.

2. To make the doner ‘meat’, whisk together the olive oil, tomato puree, lemon juice, garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, onion granules and cayenne pepper in a large bowl. Season generously with salt and pepper. Using a potato peeler or mandoline, shave the tofu into thin ribbons. Add to the bowl and toss gently to coat.

3. Spread the seasoned tofu out on the lined baking sheet and bake for 15-20 minutes, or until slightly crisp and curling at the edges.

4. Meanwhile, combine the red onion, tomatoes, cucumber, parsley and mint in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper and set aside.

5. For the garlic sauce, stir together the yogurt, garlic and lemon juice in a small bowl. Season to taste.

6. To assemble, warm your flatbreads (optional, but recommended). Spread with garlic sauce, then layer on the salad and the crispy tofu ‘doner’. Drizzle with more sauce and add a wedge of lemon on the side, if you like.

Matcha and strawberry chia pudding

open image in gallery Matcha, chia and strawberries make this an easy make-ahead breakfast with a caffeine kick ( Lucy Richards )

“I love this flavour combination for breakfast, especially as you get a subtle caffeine boost from the earthy matcha to kick-start the day,” enthuses Petersen. “If you’re anti-chia (it’s okay, I get it!), try blending the chia seeds with the milk before chilling; it gives a smoother, more pudding-like texture that might just win you over.”

Serves: 1

Prep time: 5 minutes | Chill time: 4 hours or overnight

Ingredients;

80ml milk of choice

150g fat-free thick yogurt (DF/VE: soy yogurt)

1 tbsp maple syrup, plus extra if you like it sweeter

¼ tsp vanilla extract

1 tsp matcha powder

20g chia seeds

To serve:

2-3 strawberries, hulled and finely diced granola (GF: gluten-free granola)

Method:

1. In a mixing bowl, whisk together the milk, yogurt, maple syrup, vanilla extract and matcha powder until smooth and no lumps remain. Stir in the chia seeds and mix well.

2. Pour the mixture into an airtight jar or container, then seal and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight, until thickened.

3. When ready to serve, give the pudding a quick stir and top with fresh strawberries and a handful of granola. You can serve with an extra dollop of yogurt too, if you like.

Future you: Cool and place in an airtight container, storing in the fridge for up to 3 days.

‘Healthyish High Protein’ by Emma Petersen (Pavilion, £22).

Prince George, 13, arrived for his first day at Eton College yesterday accompanied by his parents, the Prince and Princess of Wales.

Like millions of children heading back into the classroom for the autumn term, the future king will have been feeling nervous. And not too far away, his cousins Prince Archie, seven, and Princess Lilibet, five, were also starting their new schools in the UK, pre-prep and prep, after the Duke and Duchess of Sussex relocated the family from their Montecito home in California – supposedly settling near the Cotswolds.

Meghan, as an American, will need to decode unwritten British school-gate etiquette, which may trigger memories of her life as a senior working royal before Megxit. The truth is, to be back on the school run after a six- to eight-week summer break is a complete shock to the system, whoever you are and wherever you choose to send your children.

open image in gallery Prince George started Eton yesterday ( Reuters )

This is Motherland writ large, with competitive parents, cliquey groups, judgmental stereotypes, and epic dramas all there to be unravelled over the next few weeks during school drop-offs and pick-ups.

I’ve had my fair share – and the summer school holidays have been a welcome break from it all. As I walked down the alleyway into the school playground of my children’s West London primary school, it felt like a tidal wave of parents might wipe me out.

While we’re all busy taking photos of our children, emotions are flying high. Most parents feel panic about how our kids are going to settle in, which only adds to the dread of the dreaded class WhatsApp revving up – a guaranteed hotbed for explosive fallouts.

As soon as I saw the first message for a new class rep and the “polite reminder” for parents to step up to the job like we are being called to fight for our country, I wanted to mute the channel.

I try to pace things by keeping communication to the minimum and legging it back to my car because before you know it, you can be knee-deep in issues that zap your time and energy.

I walked straight back into the drama as my eight-year-old daughter Liberty started Year 4 and found there to be only 13 other children in what is meant to be a class of 30. Her best friend had left without telling us, going to a private school across the road in Kensington – and my daughter was hysterical.

open image in gallery Schoolgate frenemies in BBC sitcom ‘Motherland’: Anna Maxwell Martin as the stressed mum Julia and Lucy Punch as the perfect Amanda ( BBC )

On top of that, other mums are roaming the playground discussing tutoring, which secondary school is best, and how to get your child through entrance exams.

The usual rivalry is in full force with one tiger mum who pretends to be relaxed like a jelly fish parent, fast tracking her daughter into every extra curriculum activity possible, which made me feel like a total failure.

Of course, with the elections of school class councillors next week, some mums are already coaching their children in public speaking - and handing out flyers to vote for them.

I know I need to throw myself into the community spirit - and I have a lot of great mum friends at the school. But things can turn in a second, last year I felt ostracised for not helping to carry trestle tables at the the school’s fun run.

Dr Tara Porter , clinical psychologist and author of 2026’s Good Enough Parenting: How to Stop Beating Yourself Up, and Raise Happy, Self-Reliant Kids says the school gate can be a “tinderbox for competiveness”.

“There are so many diferent aspects of raising children and when we talk to other parents, it’s so hard not to compare, and then start to have a wobble about your own standards,” she tells me.

“When parents start to worry about meeting other people’s standards or how they or their child are doing comparatively, it can pull them away from their relationship with their child - meeting their child where they are as who they are, having fun with them, creating happy memories or good times.”

Over the last generation, she says, there have been many different factors which have combined to super charge this, and tip normal comparison into something unhealthy, verging on competition.

Nowadays parents aren’t just comparing themselves to the parents in their community. There is a whole other world of idealised parenting on social media which raises expectations Dr Tara Porter

“Nowadays parents aren’t just comparing themselves to the parents in their community. There is a whole other world of idealised parenting on social media which raises expectations of what parenting should be like. So it ups the pressure for everybody.”

The education system has also been through several different reforms, with children being assessed at multiple points, even through primary school, which, she says, creates so many opportunities for parents to worry that their children aren’t making the grade.

“They hear that other parents have started tutoring, extra homework, or Kumon Maths, and wonder if their child needs that. Will they be left behind?” she adds.

“This all occurs against the backdrop of fears about the economy, competing for places at the best schools and universities, and how will they ever afford a house. Everything feels like a competition.”

Anita Cleare, parenting expert and author of The Work/Parent Switch, says it’s not always easy to stay sane at the school gate and to not get knocked off track by competitive parenting.

“It’s easy to feel resentful when you hear other parents’ stories about their idyllic summer holidays, but always remember that what you’re getting are the edited highlights of the best bits,” says Cleare.

“All families have their challenges and their bad moments; they just don’t always advertise them. It’s best to assume that behind every glossy parental veneer, there is an equal portion of stress, hair-pulling and far-from-perfect parenting.”

open image in gallery Dr Tara Porter says the school gate can be a tinderbox for competiveness ( Tara Porter )

She also adds that it can take time to find your tribe at the school gate – “the parents who you can be honest with and laugh with and mutually support”.

“One of the key principles of positive parenting is looking after yourself,” she adds. “We are all far less likely to parent calmly and consistently when we are stressed or stretched too thin.”

If you have time to spare, she advises, then you might want to jump into the school community by volunteering or joining the PTA. “But,” she says, “it is fine to step back and conserve your energy so you can be a calm and connected parent at home rather than trying to appear like a super parent to everyone else.”

Catherine Mintague, a UK-based psychotherapist, points out that the school gate isn't just where we drop our children off; it's one of the biggest social arenas many adults step into.

“We're pack animals, wired to seek belonging, so it's no surprise that many parents feel like the playground can be daunting, perhaps even flooded with memories of their own childhood, which can be extremely emotive,” she tells me.

“Playground politics is about our deeply human need to belong. When we feel uncertain, our brains naturally look for where we fit in, and that can lead to comparison, cliques and misunderstandings.”

One important “don’t” is not to forget that your child needs a present parent, not a perfect one. The irony is, she says, that most parents are worrying about exactly the same thing: “Am I doing a good enough job?” Once we realise that, it's much easier to swap comparison for compassion.

News.title: ‘She’s a bit similar to me’: Dame Laura Davies reflects on Charley Hull’s winning Solheim Cup approach
News.content:

As the person with the most Solheim Cup appearances (12) and the most Solheim Cup points (25) in history, you might expect Dame Laura Davies to be rooting for a European whitewash of Team USA when the latest edition of women’s golf’s premier team competition begins in the Netherlands this week. But she’s got the bigger picture in mind.

“I think it will be really close come Sunday,” she says in an exclusive interview with The Independent. “I hope for the galleries and the TV audiences it’s really close.”

But she can’t keep the proud European in her at bay for long. “Then I hope we just nick it down the last two or three matches, that would be the dream,” she smiles. “It’s happened recently a couple of times for Europe, so hopefully it’ll happen like that. If we went on to have a big win, I’d like that too, but ideally, a close run thing with a win for us. And I think it’s definitely possible.”

open image in gallery Dame Laura Davies is hoping for a narrow European win in the upcoming Solheim Cup ( Getty )

The Solheim Cup has had a habit of going down to the wire in recent years. The United States are the current holders, after a relatively serene 15.5-12.5 win in Virginia in 2024, but the three prior editions had seen 14.5-13.5 and 15-13 wins for Europe, plus a 14-14 tie.

The Americans haven’t lifted the cup on European soil since 2015 (a dramatic 14.5-13.5 triumph at Golf Club St. Leon-Rot in Germany, where Team USA roared back from 10-6 behind heading into the final day), so although the bookies have Angela Stanford’s side – led by superstar world No 1 Nelly Korda – as narrow favourites this time, there will be the weight of recent history hanging over the visitors at Bernardus Golf Club near Den Bosch, in the central-southern part of the Netherlands.

Europe will be led by Anna Nordqvist, a player at each of the last nine Solheim Cups, although appearances as a playing vice-captain in 2023 and 2024 have given the 39-year-old Swede a taste of what is required from a leadership standpoint.

open image in gallery Anna Nordqvist captains Team Europe after making nine Solheim Cup appearances as a player ( Getty )

In fact, Nordqvist emotionally announced her shock retirement from playing late last month, so unless she retains the captaincy for 2028, this may be her swansong in competitive golf.

“Her retirement came out of the blue for me,” admits Davies. “I think a lot of people were surprised. I haven’t spoken to anyone that said ‘oh yeah, she’s been talking about that for a while’.

“It’s definitely surprising because she’s still so good but it reaches a point in your career, if you’re not enjoying it, then it’s time to stop. Who knows, maybe she’s just not enjoying it as much as she used to? So it’s probably the right decision for her.”

Losing Nordqvist in a playing capacity is symptomatic of a slight trend for Team Europe, with Georgia Hall missing out after only recently returning from having a baby, the pregnant Madelene Sagstrom being unavailable and Emily Kristine Pedersen having lost form over the past couple of years. That quartet have played 22 Solheim Cups between them, leaving the hosts shorn of some potentially crucial experience.

There are four first-timers on the European side in the form of Lottie Woad, Julia Lopez Ramirez, Nastasia Nadaud and Mimi Rhodes, although given her status as world No 7 and a two-time winner on the LPGA Tour since turning professional last summer, Woad is far from your traditional Solheim rookie.

But if they are to vanquish Korda and co, then Charley Hull will need to lead from the front. The 30-year-old Englishwoman’s endless quest to finally claim a first major may not yet have borne fruit but she is in the form of her life, entrenched in the world’s top 10 and ready to appear at an eighth Solheim Cup.

Davies makes no bones about the fact that Hull will need to shine if Europe are to triumph, even if she’s not a natural off-course leader.

open image in gallery Charley Hull will need to lead from the front if Europe are to triumph this week ( Getty )

“I think she’s a bit similar to me,” admits Davies. “I was not vocal in the team room and from what I’ve seen of it so far, Charley’s not either. But she doesn’t need to be.

“You’ve got a captain. You’ve got three really strong vice-captains, in Caroline Hedwall, Anne van Dam and obviously Mel Reid. So you’ve got all the noise in the team room and all the geeing up of people, although there will be some players that are like that. I don’t think Charley necessarily would be, or has to be. Just get out there and win points, which is what she loves to try and do.

“I think she is probably playing the best golf of her career. But the one thing about Charley, she doesn’t win enough. I’m not talking majors, I just think she’s so good, you can’t believe that she hasn’t won a few more tournaments. That is not a criticism, that’s a compliment. It’s amazing to see how good she is week in week out. Rarely puts in a terrible performance, always pretty solid. The major will come but also, more importantly for me, getting lots of wins in a given season because she deserves that, because her golf is that good.

“I think she really loves the Solheim Cup as well. The fact she’s got 11 teammates is a bonus, but I think she’s more than happy to get out there and try and get some points off the Americans.”

open image in gallery Hull has starred in seven previous Ryder Cups ( Getty )

Hull isn’t the only Solheim veteran that Europe can call on, with Spaniard Carlota Ciganda also appearing for the eighth time, France’s Celine Boutier at her fifth and the hero of 2021 – Ireland’s Leona Maguire – bringing her incredible 70.83 winning percentage in Solheim Cup matches after receiving a captain’s pick.

Davies, who has been part of the European team room at the last couple of Solheim Cups and will be again this year, says that Nordqvist has already given the players a rough idea of who they might be playing with when the action starts on Friday morning.

Nerves will be jangling as practice rounds over the next couple of days determine the exact nature of the final selections but Davies claims there is nothing quite like a Solheim Cup and has urged the players to relish it.

open image in gallery Davies won 25 points in her 12 Solheim Cup appearances ( Getty Images )

“It was the best thing in my career,” insists the four-time major winner. “I played 12 of them over the years [between 1990 and 2011] and loved every one – I lost eight and won four but still, I’ve only got good memories of all of them.

“It’s a pressure packed cauldron of a tournament, but these players, they live for that. It’s great to have 11 teammates and all the other people to help you during that one week, every two years. If any of the players ever come away from it, not having enjoyed it, it’s a real waste.”

Watch every moment of the Solheim Cup live, exclusively on Sky Sports and NOW from Friday 11 September

News.title: If Alexis Mac Allister wants a new contract at Liverpool, he’s got to earn it
News.content:

When the giants from the Spanish capital visit Anfield, Alexis Mac Allister has a habit of commanding attention. In 2024, Real Madrid arrived and departed beaten, with Mac Allister scoring. In 2025, the same happened. And in 2026, as Atletico Madrid prepared to kick off their Champions League campaign, Mac Allister delivered another dramatic intervention. This one did not involve angling a shot or planting a header past Thibaut Courtois.

Mac Allister implied he could have been lining up at Anfield on Wednesday in the colours of Atletico. “There were options to leave this summer,” he said. There may have been more reason to go with the message from Liverpool. “I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract, which of course makes me very, very sad,” he said.

It made Mac Allister the odd man out among the 2025 title-winning midfield. Ryan Gravenberch signed a six-year deal in March. Dominik Szoboszlai agreed a five-year deal in July. Mac Allister was arguably the best of the trio in Jurgen Klopp’s final season, after each joined in 2023. He was excellent in Arne Slot’s title-winning team the following year.

open image in gallery Mac Allister admitted he could have left Liverpool ( Getty )

He noted the difference. “I see Dominik and Ryan renewing their contracts and that’s makes me very happy because they deserve it but at the same time it makes me a little bit sad I didn’t get mine. Of course, there is still time.”

Time, perhaps, to change Liverpool’s minds. Mac Allister’s current deal expires in 2028. He will, though, soon be entering the frame when his transfer value deteriorates and other clubs may start making overtures. Liverpool have lost a series of players on free transfers in recent years and sold others for cut-price fees when their contracts were nearing the end. One interpretation is that the former director of football Richard Hughes has left his successor with another problem.

Another is to argue that, impressive as Mac Allister was in his first two seasons after his £35m move from Brighton, his form last year scarcely merited a new deal. He will be 29 at the end of his current contract. Never blessed with pace, there is the question if he is slowing down as the game is getting quicker, making him a man out of time. If he did not leave in the summer, perhaps it was because the calibre of club he may have wanted to join did not provide a suitable offer.

The World Cup was a reason why Mac Allister started the season on the bench, but with new head coach Andoni Iraola’s use of Florian Wirtz as a No 10 meaning there is only room for two central midfielders, it could have seemed an insight into his thinking.

What can be said is that Liverpool already possess one of the biggest wage bills in world football. They have committed around £650m to signings in the last 15 months. A club who often describe themselves as self-sustaining may have decided their money only goes so far.

Mac Allister has not had a full explanation. “What I got from my agent was that they were not in the position to renew me. It’s really sad because we won the Premier League together, we went through difficult times as well together and I always give my best,” he said. At the same time, there was a recognition he was not at his best last year. “I take responsibility because it was not a good season for me individually and for as a team,” the World Cup winner added.

Nor was it for quite a few others. Now two of last season’s underachievers gone, in Mohamed Salah and Ibrahima Konate; Liverpool did not meet the Frenchman’s contract demands. Perhaps committing to Mac Allister for the long term now may have seemed a reward for recent failure.

open image in gallery Alexis Mac Allister puts in a sliding tackle on Nottingham Forest midfielder James McAtee ( PA )

Mac Allister’s sadness did not prevent him from hinting that he understood Liverpool’s reluctance to give him a deal. “Maybe, it is going to depend on how I perform during these years, like every football player, and they are right to make the decision,” he said.

For now, it may seem Liverpool are in the stronger negotiating position. Mac Allister wants to stay. “I don’t think I have to prove something but I have to show the level I can perform and hopefully that is the case,” he added. “I love this club, I love being here, I love the fans, and as a player it sometimes happens you are in a club for a long time and you don’t really realise where you are. That doesn’t happen to me, I know very well this is an amazing club.”

If he has to persuade his employers, he might have made the right kind of start with Iraola. Mac Allister had a fine World Cup as Argentina reached another final. He came into the Liverpool side for Gravenberch after the draw at Newcastle.

“The important thing for me is he wants to continue here in the footballing side,” said Iraola. “I think very highly [of him] and definitely there is still a lot of time to talk about those contract situations." But the surprise was how much Mac Allister said and what it revealed.

Taking place every September in Berlin, the IFA tech and home show stands for “Innovation for All”. It has been held since 1924, and Albert Einstein once attended. The show usually runs for one week and is also open to the public.

News.title: Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double
News.content:
Enzo Maresca takes charge of his first Champions League game in charge of Manchester City as they have travelled to Portugal to take on Porto at the Estadio do Dragao. These sides last met during the Champions League group stages during the 2020/21 season. Manchester City won 3-1 at home before the two sides drew 0-0 in this stadium.

Manchester City were busy late on in the transfer window, bringing in both Iliman Ndiaye and Enzo Fernandez as they spent nearly £200m on deadline day alone. They come into tonight’s game off the back of three straight Premier League victories to kick off the Maresca era. Maresca has limited Champions League experience as a manager, which came with Chelsea last season. Manchester City have won their opening game of a Champions League campaign in six of the last seven seasons but this will be the first time since 2015/16 that Manchester City embark on a Champions League campaign without Pep Guardiola at the helm.

“It is a hard place to come [Porto],” said Maresca. “They have started really well. In the last 14/15 games in Europe they lost just one, that shows a difficult place to come, but we will try our best and try to win the game. It is a very, very good team. They have different players, but in terms of the team it is very clear in the way they play. They are aggressive without the ball and on the ball, they have a clear style. But we will try our best and try to win the game. The ambition is the same; try to be ourselves and to win games and then we will see.”

Porto, managed by Francesco Farioli, have won every league game so far this season and already sit four points clear at the summit of Liga Portugal. Farioli takes charge of his first game as a manger in the Champions League and the club make their return to the elite European competition after two seasons away.

“We are going to face one of the big favourites to win the competition,” Farioli said. “It will be a game that will demand that we be at our best, and we know that whenever we step onto the Dragão pitch, something special can happen. I am happy to be in the Champions League for the first time at 37 years old. This will be my first game, but we approach every game with the same attention to detail and the same focus. It is easy for the players to be motivated tomorrow [tonight]. But the key will be our strategy and our ability to execute it, individually and collectively.”

Porto were in the Europa League last season, making it to the quarter-finals, where they were knocked out by Nottingham Forest 2-1 on aggregate. The omens would not appear to be on Porto’s side tonight; they have only won two of their last 16 games against English opposition in major European competition.

Team news from Portugal to follow shortly.

News.title: Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start
News.content:
Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he said.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

News.title: Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off
News.content:
Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

News.title: Bird flu threatens French foie gras amid new duck cull
News.content:
The latest cull - like previous ones - was undertaken to protect both animal and human health.

Ducks are killed to stop the spread of the disease between farms, as well as to protect the health of farmers and minimise the risk of the virus mutating.

It is thought foie gras itself does not pose a risk to human health, even if it came from a bird-flu-infected duck, because it is almost always heat-treated before it is sold, which effectively destroys the virus, according to Public Health France.

“The consumption of meat, foie gras and eggs – and more generally of any food product based on poultry – presents no risk to humans,” said a spokesman for the Maine-et-Loire prefecture.

Veterinary experts say ducks are especially problematic regarding H5N1 because they can carry the virus without showing symptoms and have been described as the Chevaux de Troie or “Trojan horses” of bird flu.

It is unclear how the birds in the latest outbreak, located on a farm in Longué-Jumelles, contracted the virus, although it is typically spread by wild birds which shed the virus through their droppings.

It is for this reason that British poultry were forced into lockdown or “flockdown” from late October to April of this year.

This included so-called “free-range” birds, which, as the Telegraph reported in November continued to be described as free-range despite never seeing the light of day under a dispensation given by the Department for Environment, Food, and Rural Affairs (DEFRA).

Ducks reared for foie gras typically spend the first 90 days of their lives being reared in their tens of thousands in barns with very little access to natural light.

Animal rights campaigners say most never see water.

They then are put through a rigorous 12-16 day “fattening up” period where they are force-fed through a tube to significantly enlarge their livers, before being slaughtered.

While France introduced a vaccination programme to protect its duck population from bird flu in 2023, the jabs do not entirely stop the virus from getting into a flock.

Data collected by the French Agency for Food, Environmental and Occupational Health & Safety suggested that between 50 and 55 per cent of the country’s ducks are unvaccinated at any given time, due to a 20-day gap between the first and second dose of the vaccine and waning immunity over time.

The ducks subject to the latest bird-flu cull in Western France had received their first dose of the H5N1 vaccine, but not the second, meaning they were not fully protected, according to the disease monitoring firm Airfinity.

The threat to France’s £2 billion foie gras industry comes amid increasing global competition.

Once the dominant producer, it is now being challenged by China, which has rapidly scaled up its output of the delicacy and now accounts for 45 per cent of global production.

A tin of Chinese foie gras costs roughly £3.70, while a typical tin of French foie gras made from duck liver costs between £10 and £15. French foie gras produced from Geese costs anywhere between £70 and £150.

China is also said to operate a more rigorous poultry vaccination programme, according to an analysis by DEFRA.

It applies to all farmed birds in the country, which has managed to keep outbreaks of bird flu on farms relatively low compared with European levels.

The H5N1 avian flu pandemic has now been running for six years and has decimated flocks of farmed chickens and turkeys across the globe.

In the UK alone, more than five million farmed birds have been culled since 2021, costing an estimated £48 million in farmers’ compensation alone.

Last week, the virus was detected on a mink farm in the US state of Utah.

Minks in captivity have previously been described as pandemic “time bombs”. The size and density of fur farms – where thousands of the animals are crammed together in tight proximity – give invading viruses a perfect environment in which to mutate.

The virus has also done huge damage to wild birds and other animals. In South America alone, more than 600,000 wild seabirds have died since 2022.

Dozens of other mammals have been infected and died across the globe, including foxes, otters, sea lions, bears, and seals.

In June, the virus was found in Australia for the first time – the last continent on earth to record a case – and the government has since launched a vaccination programme to protect the country’s rare species, including birds like orange-bellied parrots and black cockatoos.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 gains the mutations necessary to spread between people, it could trigger a human-pandemic, something that would be of “enormous concern”, according to the World Health Organization (WHO), given the virus’s 50 per cent case fatality rate.

News.title: The Chancellor’s speech, as it happened
News.content:
John Healey failed to rule out tax rises at next month’s Budget in his first major speech as Chancellor.

Mr Healey also sought to blame Liz Truss and her mini-Budget in 2022 for the high borrowing costs being paid by the Treasury.

During a speech in Coventry, the Chancellor said he would be “honest” about the need to control public spending during his time in Number 11.

He was speaking days after the cost of government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007.

It was also overshadowed by Jaguar Land Rover announcing plans to cut 4,000 jobs in the face of “intense competition and ongoing geopolitical uncertainty”.

Read our report on the Chancellor’s speech.

News.title: Maitland-Niles’ last-gasp debut goal salvages Everton’s miserable week
News.content:
At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

Their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Julian Alvarez behaviour speaks volumes as private chat with team-mate emerges
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Julian Alvarez behaviour speaks volumes as private chat with team-mate emerges

A look at the latest headlines surrounding Arsenal as they get set to return to the Champions League on Wednesday night with a trip to Napoli

View 3 Images Julian Alvarez's behaviour at Atletico Madrid has emerged (Image: Cesar Ortiz Gonzalez/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Julian Alvarez's behaviour following a failed move to Arsenal has been revealed, with Lautaro Martinez offering insight into the striker's mindset. The Gunners were pushing for the Argentina international towards the end of the window but he ultimately remained with Atletico Madrid.

‌



With that, Mikel Arteta will rely upon Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres as forward options for the season. This has ultimately been working well, as the Gunners have won all three Premier League games of the 2026/27 campaign.

‌



Now a tricky opening clash away at Napoli is coming up in the Champions League. Arteta's side have travelled to Italy for the fixture as they aim to reach the final once again.

‌



Here, Mirror Football has the latest coming out of the red side of north London.

Alvarez behaviour emerges

Alvarez is said to be back to "new" following his failed transfer saga this summer. The Argentine striker was desperate for a move to Barcelona, with Arsenal also circling, but neither move materialised.

The 26-year-old missed three training sessions in a row, citing illness, and did not travel with the team to face Sevilla. He returned in a 3-0 loss to Athletic Club earlier in September and impressed, despite continued jeers from the Atleti fans.

‌



This effort is now said to have translated in training with AS claiming he is "a new Julian Alvarez." The Spanish news outlet stated that the striker took part in an intense session which focused on pressure, ball circulation and 'stealing.'

View 3 Images Alvarez is reportedly a 'new' man and has got his head down (Image: Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images)

Alvarez reportedly scored during this training session and also put in extra work with a physical trainer to build up his fitness as others stretched. Atleti manager Diego Simeone discussed the striker before last weekend's game, stating that he hopes the failed transfer was "a learning experience."

Simeone said: "Julian Alvarez will be in the squad tomorrow. He's training well, and we expect the best from him, just as we do from all his team-mates. For me, life is full of opportunities, and Julian now has an opportunity. A lot of the time, we spend our lives judging.

Team-mate speaks out

Sports.title: Arsenal in Champions League blow as Naples flight hit by air traffic control outage
Sports.content:
Arsenal in Champions League blow as Naples flight hit by air traffic control outage

The Gunners were unable to catch their flight to Naples ahead of their Champions League game due to a technical issue which forced hundred of flights to face delays and cancellations

View 4 Images The Arsenal team boarded the plane later than expected after delays

Arsenal's travel for their upcoming Champions League game against Napoli has been disrupted due to flight cancellation chaos.

‌



The team were delayed catching their flight to Naples because of air traffic control issues which left thousands of people stranded across the UK.

‌



The technical failure meant the North London team's flight was delayed. Players remained at the club training ground and left later for the airport.

‌



Manager Mikel Arteta was due to speak to journalists at a press conference in Naples on Tuesday evening, alongside defender Riccardo Calafiori, ahead of their opening European fixture of the season.

View 4 Images Passengers at Gatwick Airport's South Terminal in Crawley, West Sussex, after flights were cancelled on Tuesday because of a UK air traffic control issue. (Image: Jordan Pettitt/PA Wire)

However, due to the chaos, the Gunners were not expected to arrive in Naples until around 9.30pm local time (8.30pm UK time).

‌



NATS, which provides air traffic control services to 15 UK airports, has said recovery from a technical issue which forced the cancellation of more than 400 flights “has taken longer than we had hoped” but is “resolved”.

The “system issue” on Tuesday had been resolved by 7.30pm however, thousands remain impacted by the delays and cancellations at UK airports.

Many passengers reported being 'trapped' on planes or 'stranded' at airports due to the issues.

‌



Flight monitoring website Flightradar24 said more than 1,000 flights had been cancelled at UK airports by about 8pm.

View 4 Images Rice boarded the flight on Tuesday after delays

Ryanair said more than 65,000 of its passengers had been disrupted and it had cancelled more than 50 scheduled flights.

‌



British Airways (BA) said it was forced to cancel or divert more than 100 flights on Tuesday which had impacted “tens of thousands of customers”.

The boss of the air traffic control provider, Nats, said he “always” accepts “full responsibility” after a technical issue caused huge disruption to flights.

Nats’ chief executive officer Martin Rolfe said “I always accept full responsibility”.

‌



He said: “I am the CEO of a piece of critical infrastructure, so it is my job to take responsibility for that.

View 4 Images Thousands of people have been left 'stranded' due to the disruption (Image: Ed Easton/Daily Mirror)

“What I absolutely take responsibility for is keeping people safe and delivering the best service we possibly can on a day like today.

‌



“You will understand my focus is entirely about how we actually resolve this issue, get things back to normal, help our airlines, our airport customers and the travelling public.”

Neal McMahon, Ryanair’s chief operating officer, called on Mr Rolfe to resign, saying: “How many more failures do passengers have to suffer before overpaid failure Nats CEO Martin Rolfe accepts responsibility for his repeated mismanagement and resigns?

“Over three years after Nats’ catastrophic 2023 system meltdown, it’s clear that nothing has changed, with UK passengers once again suffering avoidable ATC (air traffic control) delays of up to eight hours today due a critical Nats ATC system failing.”

Article continues below

Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander is due to speak with Mr Rolfe on Wednesday before she addresses MPs in the Commons for the second reading of the Civil Aviation Bill.

Mr Rolfe said airlines would be able to provide the best information on how long the ongoing impact would take to resolve.

Erling Haaland angry with Ayyoub Bouaddi as he sends clear message to Man City chairman

Erling Haaland scored both goals as Manchester City claimed a 2-0 win over Porto in the Champions League on Tuesday night

View 2 Images Erling Haaland had a message for Ayyoub Bouaddi after Man City's win over Porto (Image: Amazon Prime)

Erling Haaland praised new Manchester City signing Ayyoub Bouaddi after the victory over Porto, and jokingly claimed that he was 'angry' with his new team-mate. City claimed a 2-0 win over the Portuguese club in their first Champions League group-stage fixture on Tuesday night.

‌



Haaland scored both goals for City in the second half, with the first coming just after the interval thanks to the Norway international getting on the end of a cross from deadline-day signing Enzo Fernandez.

‌



The striker added his second in stoppage time to become City's third-highest scorer of all time with 167. After the game, Haaland was asked for his verdict on Bouaddi’s performance for City, and went on to jokingly say he was 'angry with his team-mate and describing him as a 'gem'.

Sports.title: Diego Simeone makes honest Julian Alvarez admission ahead of Liverpool clash
Sports.content:
Diego Simeone makes honest Julian Alvarez admission ahead of Liverpool clash

Julian Alvarez has returned to contention for Atletico Madrid over recent weeks following a failed summer move to Arsenal and Diego Simeone has now offered his take on the striker’s situation

View 2 Images Diego Simeone takes his Atletico Madrid side to Liverpool on Wednesday (Image: Getty Images)

Diego Simeone has admitted that Julian Alvarez's situation is still disrupting Atletico Madrid ahead of their trip to Anfield. The Spanish side take on Liverpool in their Champions League opener on Wednesday evening.

‌



The game comes after a tumultuous summer where star forward Alvarez was linked with a move away from the club. Barcelona and Arsenal were interested, with the former lodging a formal bid but Atleti elected not to do business with their Spanish rivals.

‌



Since then, Alvarez, 26, has made two substitute appearances, having also been booed by the club’s fans, while he missed training due to illness. Speaking ahead of the trip to Merseyside, boss Simeone has confirmed that he is not ready to start, while both fellow strikers Jonathan David and Alexander Sorloth are doubts.

‌



"Jonathan arrived very recently and couldn't play the other day [against Athletic Club] due to a problem," said Simeone. "Julian is still developing; I don't see him starting yet, but he'll help us as the game progresses.

"[Sorloth's] recovering. He has this injury that's keeping him from playing. We need him; he's important, whether it's for 90, 60 or 20 minutes. He gives us things we don't have in the team right now. Hopefully, he'll be back soon."

Simeone added: "It's very important for the club that the final is at the Metropolitano. For us, we have to work incredibly hard to be able to aspire to that privileged position.

"I showed him my full support because, apart from the fact that we're teammates, that we play in the same position and are competing for a place in the national team, he's a friend.

‌



"I'm sure the situation he's been through and is still going through isn't easy, but well, the decision lies with his club and his club's president.

"I wish him all the best," Martínez added. "I hope he gets well soon and continues to show what he's shown so far, because he's a brilliant player -- one of the best in the world, too."

Sports.title: Erling Haaland delivers again to help Man City survive Porto scare - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland delivers again to help Man City survive Porto scare - 5 talking points

PORTO 0-2 MAN CITY: A brace from Erling Haaland decided the game for Manchester City once again, as they took maximum points from their awkward Champions League opener

View 5 Images Manchester City are up and running in the Champions League (Image: PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA/AFP via Getty Images)

Manchester City got their Champions League campaign off to a winning start with a hard-fought 2-0 victory over Porto. Erling Haaland netted both goals in Portugal to make it five for the season, having also decided Saturday's win against Coventry.

‌



City returned to the scene of their Champions League final defeat to Chelsea in 2021 with a new man in the dugout. Enzo Maresca didn't have easy time watching his team toil in the the pouring rain, but they earned their fourth successive win under him.

‌



They were left frustrated in the first half, much thanks to the heroics of Diogo Costa. The Porto goalkeeper made a string of impressive saves, including two from Haaland to keep the Premier League giants at bay.

‌



But it didn't take long for City to break through at the start of the second period - and third time was a charm for Haaland, whose header hit the post before nestling in the back of the net. It was then backs to the wall until full-time, as Porto pushed for an equaliser before City's goalscorer supreme struck again.

Here are five talking points from the Estadio do Dragao.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

1. Haaland starts despite Maresca hint

Erling Haaland's daddy issues was the main talking point from Enzo Maresca's pre-match press conference on Monday. The City boss explained how Haaland, now bearing the responsibilities of being a father, will need to be rested at some point this season following a busy 2025-26 campaign which ended in a deep run at the World Cup with Norway, who made it to the quarter-finals.

With deadline-day arrival Iliman Ndiaye now at his disposal, would Maresca rotate his striker? No. The 26-year-old was named in the starting XI alongside £86million signing Ayyoub Bouaddi, who was handed his full debut in midfield next to Enzo Fernandez after a cameo against Coventry.

‌



Will Man City win the Champions League? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 5 Images Erling Haaland isn't being rested yet (Image: PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA/AFP via Getty Images)

2. VAR looks past Guehi incident

With the first half meandering to a close, City were flexing their muscles and causing Porto some discomfort. Marc Guehi did that quite literally when challenging Gabri Veiga for a bouncing ball, drawing blood from the Porto star's head.

‌



Guehi's arm wasn't outstretched but the hosts became incensed after watching replays of the incident on the touchline. Francesco Farioli suggested that the City centre-back had elbowed his midfielder.

Veiga received treatment for a good few minutes, giving VAR plenty of time to assess the collision. But nothing was given, allowing referee Szymon Marciniak to signal for the restart without going to the monitor.

But when Marciniak blew his whistle for half-time, he was greeted by deafening whistles from the home crowd. The Polish official was also swarmed by Porto players as he attempted to get down the tunnel.

‌



View 5 Images Gabriel Veiga took a heavy blow from Marc Guehi (Image: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images)

3. Who else but Haaland?

Need someone to break the deadlock? Call Erling Haaland.

The Norwegian has now scored the first goal in City's last three games. This time he easily beat Jakub Kiwior in the air and headed Fernandez's cross back the way it came, leaving Costa wrong-footed.

‌



It seemed to take an age for the ball to go in, but there was relief when it eventually did. The header marked Haaland's 58th Champions League goal - in just 59 games - taking him clear of Bayern Munich legend Thomas Muller.

View 5 Images Erling Haaland rose highest to give Manchester City the lead (Image: Miguel RIOPA/AFP via Getty Images)

4. No messing from Maresca

After going 1-0 up, City suddenly became vulnerable and sloppiness seeped - or flooded more accurately - into their performance. Their tendency to give possession cheaply away left Maresca furious in his technical area and he made a double substitution shortly after a poor passage of play.

‌



Rayan Cherki, twice the source of his manager's frustration, came off alongside Antoine Semenyo, who had a difficult night. Ndiaye and Elliot Anderson were their replacements as Porto smelled blood.

View 5 Images Enzo Maresca saw the danger coming (Image: PATRICIA DE MELO MOREIRA/AFP via Getty Images)

5. Dodgy Donnarumma

Although Maresca wasn't happy with his outfielders, it was his goalkeeper who nearly made two fatal mistakes. Gianluigi Donnarumma flattened Pepe in the 49th minute, and while the offside flag saved him from giving away a penalty, he was still booked for his challenge.

‌



Shortly after the hour mark, Donnarumma misjudged a pass which was played back to him and got chased down by William Gomes as he hurriedly attempted to clear his lines. Luckily for the Italian, his blocked clearance flew back towards goal but whizzed past the post.

Porto never properly tested the City No.1 in the closing stages, getting caught offside on numerous occasions despite their pace. And when Haaland made it 2-0 with a cool finish inside the penalty area, Maresca could breathe a sigh of relief after two narrow victories in four days ahead of the Manchester derby at Old Trafford this Sunday.

Sports.title: Ex-Liverpool star Curtis Jones has nightmare for Inter Milan on Champions League debut
Sports.content:
Ex-Liverpool star Curtis Jones has nightmare for Inter Milan on Champions League debut

Curtis Jones was allowed to leave Liverpool this summer and made a move to Italian giants Inter Milan but he had a moment to forget as he made his Champions League debut against Real Madrid

View 2 Images Curtis Jones had a nightmare at the Bernabeu (Image: Getty Images)

Curtis Jones was left red-faced on his Champions League debut for Inter Milan after gifting Kylian Mbappe a goal. The ex-Liverpool man joined the Italian giants this summer in a £30m switch from Anfield.

‌



And he had enjoyed a positive start to life with his new employers so far, albeit that came to an abrupt end at the Bernabeu on Tuesday evening. The midfielder’s sloppy pass was picked off by Mbappe as Inter attempted to play themselves out.

‌



Yann Bisseck tried to intervene but missed his challenge completely, allowing Mbappe to skip past him and hammer the ball home for his first Champions League goal of the campaign.

‌



Jones’ howler comes just days after he admitted that boss Cristian Chivu - who is unlikely to be thrilled with his mistake - was a driving force behind his move to Italy.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



He said: "There’s a reason I came here: the phone calls we had, how the team plays, his tactical ideas, and how he works every single day.

"It’s the small things he says, things that might seem minor but end up having a massive impact. Plus, he has immense experience and played at the highest level himself. He’s managed the squad brilliantly. He’s ‘one of us,’ and to me, that’s fundamental."

Jones added: "I just feel at home with the lads. Since the first day, they've been unbelievable and so I can just be myself. Of course I've got a point to prove but I know that if I'm just myself, the lads will like me, the staff and the fans as well.”

‌



Jones almost went some way to atoning for his error midway through the first-half, however, as his powerful effort thumped off of the crossbar.

View 2 Images Mbappe took full advantage of Jones' error (Image: Getty Images)

Fortunately for Jones, he was not the only one left with his head in his hands at the Bernabeu. Goalkeeper Josep Martínez also committed a similar - if slightly worse - howler to hand the home side a 2-0 lead.

‌



The stopper attempted a Cruyff turn in the penalty area when closed down by Federico Valverde. But he got it all wrong, with the Uruguayan midfielder tapping home. Like Jones, he then made up for his mistake with a brilliant double save just before half time.

Jones, Martinez and their Inter Milan teammates will certainly hope for better fortune over the coming weeks. They resume their Serie A campaign this weekend against Udinese before a clash with Roma at the Stadio Olimpico.

Chivu’s side have some time to wait before their next Champions League clash against Club Brugge in mid-October.

Sports.title: Gabriel Jesus reveals brutal Mikel Arteta call days before Arsenal exit was confirmed
Sports.content:
Gabriel Jesus reveals brutal Mikel Arteta call days before Arsenal exit was confirmed

Gabriel Jesus completed a surprise move from Arsenal to Barcelona over the closing days of the summer transfer window and he has now revealed how the move came about

View 2 Images Jesus made the move from Arsenal to Barcelona over the closing days of the window (Image: Getty Images)

Gabriel Jesus has admitted that he was made to train alone at Arsenal in the days leading up to his exit. The Brazilian striker left the Emirates Stadium at the end of the window as he completed a surprise switch to Spanish giants Barcelona.

‌



His move brought to an end an ultimately frustrating period in North London where Jesus won the Premier League, albeit injuries limited him to just 123 appearances over four years.

‌



In discussing his switch, Jesus has admitted that he was forced to train away from his teammates in the build up. Speaking to SportyTV, Jesus said: "So, the truth is, I was training, I did all the pre-season with Arsenal as normal.

‌



“Obviously, I knew already that probably I would not play there or get many opportunities, but nobody told me nothing.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"Well, I am a professional. Obviously I was training with the group. Then, from nothing, they put me to train away from the group.

‌



"Well, I was training, I was doing my maximum to be ready if I have a chance to play at a high level again. Then, obviously, in the last week it was very quick.

"The work with Deco, the president of the club, and my agent was amazing. In one day, it was sure that I would have the opportunity to come (to Barcelona). I said yes, straight away, no matter what and I am so happy to be here."

In the aftermath of Jesus’ move to the Camp Nou, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta had some kind words to say. He said: "Gabi’s gone to Barcelona, which I take the opportunity as well to give him a huge thank you.

‌



View 2 Images Jesus made his Barcelona debut over the weekend (Image: Getty Images)

"He was a massive contributor for us to change the dynamic and the energy in and around this club. I think when Gabi came in he brought this energy, this belief within, this aura, that’s really helped achieve what happened next.

"And now, yeah, he has an amazing opportunity to enjoy one of the biggest clubs in the world, and a beautiful place to live as well, and we are happy for him.”

‌



Jesus, 29, has already made his debut for his new employers, having made a brief cameo in the 5-0 win against Valencia over the weekend. He could potentially make his second appearance on Wednesday evening as Barcelona take on Feyenoord in the Champions League.

In the meantime, Arsenal kick off their latest European campaign against Italian giants Napoli. The Gunners will certainly be aiming to go one further this year, having lost out to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final last term.

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney issues Michael Carrick sack warning and says Bruno Fernandes won't be happy
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney issues Michael Carrick sack warning and says Bruno Fernandes won't be happy

Manchester United have only managed to win one of their opening three Premier League matches, a far cry from the red-hot form which they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season

View 2 Images Wayne Rooney fears for Michael Carrick (Image: The Overlap)

Wayne Rooney has warned Michael Carrick that he needs results now and can't wait for another transfer window to fix Manchester United's problems. The Red Devils legend also criticised United's summer business which saw them fail in their search to bolster their defence.

‌



Carrick's side have mustered just four points from their first three games of the Premier League season, conceding a worrying six goals in the process. United began the campaign with a shock 2-0 loss away to newly promoted Hull before thrashing Ipswich 5-2 at Old Trafford in their second outing.

‌



But off the back of Sunday's late 2-2 draw with Everton, in which the Red Devils threw away the lead twice, Rooney is concerned for his ex-team-mate. "If you're manager of Manchester United you know the pressure which comes with the job and the time now you're not getting much time in the job," the former striker explained on the Stick to United podcast.

‌



"You have to push as hard as you can even harder to get players in because you know you don't want to be sitting here in six months, 12 months' time, saying 'You know what? I should have'.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"Do we want to win the Champions League? Of course we do. But in terms of this process we're going through to try and get back to that, we're going to have to accept we're not quite at that level yet. Arsenal have been through this process over the last five years with [Mikel] Arteta and you've seen the progress each year."

Rooney went on to say: "I know Michael's come out and said he's happy with the players they've got in. I don't think any manager's happy.

"He's going to have to come out and say the right things. Of course… every manager does that. But he hasn't got time to wait for next year. He can't sit there and go 'Well, you know what? I'll wait till next year,' then I'll have my defence sorted. You're getting more and more American owners who want success straight away."

‌



Is Michael Carrick the right man for Manchester United? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Michael Carrick needs to find a solution quickly (Image: Lewis Storey - Danehouse/Getty Images)

Rooney also claimed that United captain Bruno Fernandes won't be happy with the club's decision to only sign three midfielders and a No.2 goalkeeper in the summer window. "There is nothing in there which is saying to me now these players are going to take Man United to the next level," he continued.

‌



"I love Bruno. I think he's brilliant. He must be thinking 'Right, please bring me some help. I'm doing everything I can. Help me'. And I don't think the club have done that with the signings.

"You're not sitting there saying you've got these four players we should be winning the Premier League. You're sitting there saying these players need more help than what they've been getting.

Rooney added: "We're Man United. We've won so many Premier Leagues, Champions Leagues, whatever. The fans will still be thinking that's what we want. But, realistically, they're not there."
