Sports.title: Bowen at the double as West Ham climb top of the Championship
Sports.content:
Captain Jarrod Bowen scored twice as West Ham's 3-2 win over Bolton took them top of the Sky Bet Championship on goal difference and earned a first ever win at the Toughsheet Community Stadium.

The England international opened the scoring after 13 minutes and earned last season's Premier League outfit a first win in Bolton for 31 years with his second 13 minutes from time.

In between, Wanderers, beaten for a fourth successive outing, equalised through midfielder Ethan Erhahon's maiden goal for the Trotters.

Image: Jarrod Bowen's double helped West Ham to a dramatic victory

And they looked on course for a ninth successive league victory over the Hammers when Ruben Rodrigues converted a 27th-minute penalty.

Instead, Konstantinos Mavropanos levelled with a 31st-minute header and Bowen completed the comeback.

It came as no surprise when Bowen gave West Ham the lead, lofting a left-foot shot high into the net after Gavin Bazunu blocked a close-range Pablo effort.

The Hammers' advantage lasted just five minutes before ex-Lincoln midfielder Erhahon equalised with a rasping left-foot strike that hit Mavropanos on its way beyond Mads Hermansen.

Looking for their first second-tier success since the opening day of the campaign, Bolton hit the front after 27 minutes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jarrod Bowen opens the scoring at Bolton as visitors West Ham go 1-0 in front.

Kyle Walker-Peters was already struggling to contain winger Kyliane Dong, when he felled the Augsburg loanee.

Rodrigues - who netted twice in Bolton's League One play-off final win last May, including a penalty - sent Hermansen the wrong way from the spot.

Now it was West Ham's turn to fashion a swift riposte. Arne Engels guided a free-kick to the far post where Mavropanos climbed highest to head in an equaliser.

The Greek centre-back almost reprised his goal soon after but from Bowen's inswinging corner, debutant Bazunu clawed the ball from under his crossbar.

Bolton, though, finished the half on top with the lively Dong shooting wide and Sam Dalby denied by Hermansen's stoppage-time save.

The action was less frenetic in the second half with West Ham more in control.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jarrod Bowen scored his second goal of the game as West Ham United reclaimed the lead against Bolton Wanderers.

Substitute Manor Solomon should have done better with a chance provided by Bowen while another replacement, Joel Piroe, blazed high into the away fans with only Bazunu to beat.

Bowen finally squeezed a close-range shot into the net despite Bazunu's desperate attempt to stop the ball trickling over the line.

And he should have completed a last-minute hat-trick but Wales international Josh Sheehan chased back to block the shot.

The managers

Bolton's Steven Schumacher:

"If we keep playing well the results will come.

"We thought we could take points off West Ham and we nearly did. I actually don't think we have deserved to lose any of the four games we have.

"I don't want to sound patronising but the lads are playing extremely well, competing with top teams, showing good team spirit, carrying out the game plan and creating some good chances and opportunities.

"It reminds me of last year when we drew five games on the spin and couldn't get over the line.

"In this league it is less forgiving, more punishing. The games we played last year and drew and not getting over the line, we are losing this year.

"That is the standard, this is what we worked so hard in League One to get to. So I am pleased with what we did apart from the scoreline."

West Ham's Nuno Espirito Santo:

"Bolton played a fantastic game and created enormous problems for us, so we had to react and be resilient when we needed to be.

"We must realise every team has threats and quality players. But so have we and we controlled it much better in the second half.

"The boys worked so hard for it so I am very happy. However, we all have to improve but first of all, we try to sustain the level which is hard in this league.

"I hope it (the future) is better. The belief of everyone, starting with the ownership, the staff, the players and the fans, we are trying to have better days.

"What I see and what I feel is unity in all departments of the club which is very important."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Willock grabs late goal as Newcastle edge Millwall
Sports.content:
Joe Willock's late goal sent a relieved Newcastle into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup as the Premier League side scraped to a 1-0 victory at Sky Bet Championship outfit Millwall.

Just before going ahead, the Magpies had been given a fright when a shot from Tairyk Arconte hit a post, with the hosts at that point threatening to upset the competition's winners of two seasons ago.

The Lions brought on 15-year-old midfielder Regan Anderson, who became Millwall's second youngest player, in the time that remained, but Newcastle held firm in what was a hard-fought tie.

Jacob Murphy bent a shot harmlessly over in the early exchanges in what was the first meeting between the two teams since 1993.

The first time Millwall's debutant goalkeeper Filip Marschall was called into action was in the 15th minute when he parried Willock's strike into the air, with the ball dropping to left-back Elkan Baggott rather than the lurking Yoane Wissa.

The visitors dominated the early proceedings and came close again when Sven Botman headed Murphy's corner narrowly over at the far post.

A rare foray out of their own half by the hosts led to their first half-chance as Lyndon Dykes' hooked effort from Baggott's cross was gathered easily by Lukas Hornicek.

The Lions were providing a threat from set-pieces, with a good delivery from a free-kick by Camiel Neghli being met by a flying header from Caleb Taylor that went just wide.

Newcastle then almost had a stroke of luck at the other end as Fabian Schar's long-range effort took a big deflection and ruffled the side-netting, with Marschall stranded.

It remained deadlocked at the break and Millwall began the second half brightly with Jenson Metcalfe smashing a long-range effort just over within two minutes of the restart.

A Metcalfe free-kick then led to another warning for the away side as a header from Lions captain Jake Cooper drifted wide.

The Magpies had struggled to impose themselves since half-time, although Harvey Barnes had just their second shot on target after 65 minutes when his tame effort was easily saved by Marschall.

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle sent on Anthony Elanga and deadline day signing Matias Fernandez-Pardo in an effort to finally force a breakthrough, but the Millwall centre-back pairing of Cooper and Caleb Taylor were repelling everything coming their way.

Millwall substitute Arconte was the closest to opening the scoring in the 79th minute when he got away from Tino Livramento before his shot came back off the near post.

Having survived that scare, the visitors snatched victory with nine minutes left when Lewis Hall's ball across the six-yard box was flicked in by Willock.

Image: Lewis Hall was quiick to praise new boss Matthias Jaissle

Hall hails Jaissle for lifting Newcastle negativity after cup win

Newcastle defender Lewis Hall speaking to Sky Sports:

"There was a lot of negativity before everything happened and as soon as the gaffer came in, he's been top, as well as all of the coaching staff.

"The way he's got us playing is amazing and I can speak on behalf of everyone - we're really enjoying playing under him.

"We knew it was going to be tough. Whenever you come away in the cup, anything can happen, so we're really proud of the win and to keep a clean sheet as well."

Willock: The Carabao Cup is important for us

Newcastle midfielder Joe Willock speaking to Sky Sports:

"We had a lot of chances in the first half, but we said at half-time that we needed to take our chances. Thankfully, in the second half we did, we got a goal and won the game.

"We won this competition before so it's very important to us. We've got a new coach and a lot of new players and we wanted to start the season well.

"I feel like we started it really well. We need to continue, and this was a big game in keeping that momentum."

Image: Matthias Jaissle remains unbeaten as Newcastle boss

Jaissle: It was all about patience

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle speaking to Sky Sports:

"We're really happy. Job done. It's never going to be easy here at Millwall in a cup match, so we knew about that challenge and we faced it.

"It was about patience, but also being passionate, being tough, collecting the second balls and being efficient in front of their goal. We used the chance and therefore I'm really proud.

"We matched the physical challenge quite well and made a step in the right direction compared to the first half against Bournemouth. We brought the fundamentals onto the pitch, therefore I'm pleased.

"Joe [Willock] is doing an excellent job. Since we joined, already in pre-season, you saw that there is potential.

"I'm really happy with the start so far. I think we show unity on the pitch and off the pitch already after such a short amount of time. But again, we are realistic. We're happy, we're grateful for that start and now the focus is already towards Leeds.

"I love it [English football]. Honestly, I love it. Coming out for an evening match and knowing that atmosphere is something you dream about. It's a privilege."

Sports.title: Haaland scores twice in win over Porto but Man City struggle to impress
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland's double earned Manchester City a 2-0 win at FC Porto - but it was another game where Enzo Maresca's side won but struggled to convince.

City's main man up front was surprisingly wasteful in the first half, seeing two glorious chances in the area saved by Diogo Costa as well as heading another good chance over the bar.

Porto's goalkeeper was in inspired form in the opening 45 minutes, also saving well from Rayan Cherki from the rebound of one of Haaland's chances.

But Haaland took just two minutes of the second period to make amends, barging Jakub Kiwior aside to nod an Enzo Fernandez cross in off the post.

But City then took their foot off the gas as the Portuguese champions started to grow in confidence. Porto failed to produce a shot on target but Alan Varela curled just wide of the far post from the edge of the box in a warning shot.

Image: Haaland scored twice in the second half

Then Gianluigi Donnarumma was nearly caught in possession by Porto forward William Gomes, with the City goalkeeper lucky to see the ball run away to safety. City did find a way to seal the result, however, as Haaland tucked home Rayan Ait-Nouri's cutback in stoppage time.

Erling's on Sergio's level! Erling Haaland scored his 36th UEFA Champions League goal for Manchester City, equalling Sergio Agüero as joint-most for the Citizens in the competition.

Despite another game this season where City have won but struggled to impress at the same time, Maresca failed to win away of his three away Champions League ties as Chelsea boss last term.

He will see a winning start to this campaign as a positive - especially as City have become the first team to beat Porto at the Estadio do Dragao this calendar year.

But improvement is needed ahead of Sunday's Manchester derby at Old Trafford, live on Sky Sports.

Manchester United

Manchester City Sunday 13th September 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

The key moments from Estadio do Dragao

16: SAVE! Antoine Semenyo starts the game brightly and curls an early effort into Diogo Costa's gloves.

21: BIG CHANCE FOR HAALAND! Semenyo feeds Phil Foden who clips a cross into the box for Haaland - who is denied by a smart glove from Costa.

27: BIG MISS! Haaland heads over another good chance via a cross from the left, this time from Semenyo.

29: BIG SAVE! Foden goes on a mazy run in and around the penalty area and forces another save from Costa.

31: DOUBLE SAVE! A man possessed! Costa denies Haaland's low drive from inside the box, then gets up to stop Rayan Cherki at the rebound.

42: OUCH! Marc Guehi catches Gabri Veiga with his arm which causes a lot of blood. With Porto calling for a red card for a violent elbow, the Man City defender avoids punishment. It was more accidental rather than malicious.

47: GOAL! Haaland takes just two minutes to rectify his wasteful first half by nodding a header in off the post from Enzo Fernandez's cross.

49: NO PENALTY! City goalkeeper Donnarumma clatters into Porto winger Pepe in the box… but the offside flag goes up against the forward.

57: SO CLOSE! Porto midfielder Alan Varela gets a chance to shoot and curls just wide of the far post. That was Porto's first shot of the game.

66: NERVY! Donnarumma is nearly caught in possession by Porto forward Gomes, but the ball runs behind for a goal kick.

85: JUST WIDE! City substitute Ait-Nouri has the chance to seal the result but steers a shot wide of goal from a good area.

90+1: GOAL! Haaland seals the result by slotting home Ait-Nouri's cutback after he did well to get to the byline.

Should Maresca be happy about Man City's performance?

Image: Erling Haaland gave Man City a win but they weren't convincing

Man City striker Erling Haaland to Amazon Prime:

"I hope so, we win away in a difficult game. Look at this atmosphere, it was unreal at times. So I hope [yes].

"Amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it was going to be a difficult fight, man against man. They're a top team, impressive, all of them. They play amazing football.

"Well done to them. But with all the pressure, we have to deliver on the biggest stage. That's what we did tonight.

"Honestly we controlled the whole first half. Of course, it's a bit uncomfortable when they come high. But we created a lot of chances. I could have easily had a few more goals.

"But second half we scored and they managed to push us for a good 25 minutes. We managed to hold through and finish the game.

"These are the games we have to win. We had a great start to the season and in the Champions League, you have to win games. If not, you get all the pressure. You never know what's going to happen.

"We have to learn. Enzo has to demand a lot from us and each other. At Manchester City, you have to win games and win trophies, that's what we have to do."

And here's Maresca's verdict - he's happy!

Man City head coach Enzo Maresca to Amazon Prime:

"We could have scored more goals, especially in the first half. But overall we deserved to win the game. We created enough chances to win the game, we didn't concede a lot.

"It's normal to come here and concede some noises so overall I'm happy with the performance.

"If you think you're going to come here in this stadium and just play and not concede anything, it's not reality. It's normal that they are going to create something. They didn't create a lot - some actions, some mistakes from us. But I think it's normal."

Analysis: Man City continue to play with fire

Enzo Maresca has a point. You can't turn your nose up at winning away at FC Porto - an intimidating atmosphere, one that is not used to suffering defeat. Doing so in a manner where they conceded little in terms of clear chances is also a positive.

But look at City's performances this season. Trounced in the Community Shield by Arsenal, then a late show to overcome Bournemouth with a fortunate win. Then came a resounding win over Crystal Palace, but then they nearly dropped the ball in their 1-0 win over Coventry.

This was another game where they could have dropped the ball. City dominated for 47 minutes but then allowed FC Porto back into it. There were slack passes and constant losses of possession - a better team would have found a way back into the game.

And City face a better test on Sunday. No team will be more desperate to take advantage of such play than Manchester United at Old Trafford. It will be another big atmosphere for Maresca's City to overcome. But if they continue to play with fire, they will get burnt.

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Christie nets hat-trick as Bournemouth blitz Championship Lincoln
Sports.content:
Ryan Christie scored a hat-trick to give Marco Rose his first win as Bournemouth manager as the Cherries swept aside Sky Bet Championship side Lincoln 4-0.

The Scotland international starred for the hosts with goals in the seventh, 69th and 88th minutes for his second career hat-trick, with Rayan stepping off the bench to wrap up the Carabao Cup third-round victory in stoppage time.

Rose made eight changes, including handing a debut to on-loan Juventus goalkeeper Michele Di Gregorio and a first start for Uruguayan striker Alvaro Rodriguez.

Only Ryley Towler kept his place from Lincoln's 1-1 draw at home to Southampton as the two sides met for the first time since 2010 when they were both in League Two.

Lincoln started brightly, but it was Bournemouth who opened the scoring after just seven minutes when Christie finished neatly at the near post from Ben Gannon-Doak's cross.

The lively Gannon-Doak then saw his effort blocked by Towler after cutting in from the left wing and firing a right-footed shot.

Di Gregorio was called into action for the first time after 22 minutes, keeping out Dan Oyegoke's flick before Towler blazed over from the rebound.

Lincoln goalkeeper Joe Gauci made a smart save to deny Bafode Diakite after the defender had headed a long throw goalwards.

Image: Rayan scored a 94th-minute fourth goal for the hosts

James Hill then fired over from distance as Bournemouth went hunting for a second goal. Six minutes before half-time Cherries left-back Julio Soler curled wide from 25 yards after David Brooks' corner had been only half cleared.

Hill also saw a shot from the edge of the penalty area deflected behind for a corner, before Christie's curling 20-yard effort was palmed away by Gauci with the final kick of the first half.

Rose will be frustrated to have picked up just two points from his first three Premier League games after conceding late goals against Manchester City, Everton and Newcastle.

His side almost doubled their lead five minutes into the second half when Gannon-Doak's curling effort glanced off the head of Rodriguez and flew just over the crossbar.

Scotland international Gannon-Doak then ballooned another long-range effort over in the 55th minute.

Hill came close to picking out the top corner with a 25-yard piledriver which smacked against the angle of post and crossbar.

Rodriguez had another good chance to open his Bournemouth account moments later, but slipped as he lined up a shot from the edge of the box and sent it high into the stands.

The £21m signing later headed inches wide from Hill's cross as he endured a frustrating full debut.

Christie showed Rodriguez the route to goal 21 minutes from time by heading in Brooks' corner at the far post.

The Scotland midfielder completed his treble in the 88th minute with a deflected shot from 14 yards out after being teed up by Diakite.

Rayan made it 4-0 in stoppage time with a tidy finish from the corner of the six-yard box.

Rose delighted with Christie impact

Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose:

"It was a top performance for 94 minutes and we had many shots on and off target. We only gave one chance away, so I am really happy.

"Ryan [Christie] is a nice guy. We really love him and he deserved it. He came back from an injury, worked hard and now he's back in shape.

"It's good for us because the upcoming time is really busy and we need everyone. In the next few weeks we have European football, cups in England and the Premier League is getting very demanding.

"I'm new in this club, new in this country, but it's about winning games and winning titles."

Cohen: We could not impose ourselves

Lincoln joint-head coach Chris Cohen:

"Certain players had moments in the game, but overall Bournemouth were by far the better team.

"We were looking for a low-scoring match and wanted to get to 60 minutes still in the game.

"The frustration is we did not implement our in-possession stuff at all and could not impose ourselves with our set-pieces as well as we normally do.

"We had a lot of new players and will learn a lot as a team from the game."

Sports.title: Real Madrid somehow cling on to beat Inter on José Mourinho’s big night
Sports.content:
Sometimes football is silly, sometimes it doesn’t make much sense, and sometimes it’s fun for it. On a night when there were 37 shots and the goalkeepers shared 13 occasionally absurd saves between them, José Mourinho’s current side beat his former team Inter on his Champions League return to Real Madrid. Just don’t ask exactly how. Except perhaps to cite Thibaut Courtois, whose astonishing 89th-minute stop from Henrikh Mkhitaryan explained much and allowed them, just, to hold on to the first-half lead they had been given by goals from Kylian Mbappé and Fede Valverde.

By Mbappé, Valverde, and Inter themselves, that is. You might be tempted to say the Italians had shot themselves in the foot, only if they tried Courtois would probably save that too. “If he wasn’t voted man of the match tonight, he never will be,” Mourinho said. It took 77 minutes for him to be beaten, Carlos Augusto’s goal giving this match a frantic last 15 minutes and Inter hope of justice, but it didn’t happen again. So a game that could have had any scoreline – “5-1 to us, 6-6, I don’t want to say they could have won,” Mourinho suggested – actually ended 2-1. Madrid’s manager called it “mad, and not a madness I like.”

This wasn’t always good from Madrid, in fact at times it was terrible. There was a void where the midfield should be, Mourinho thanking Trent Alexander-Arnold for filling in a “specific” midfield role that’s not for him. The intensity in the press high up was matched by a passivity elsewhere. Inter played through and round them, clocking up twice as many attacks and passes. At the end the Santiago Bernabéu whistled; Vinícius Júnior in particular felt their frustration. Yet their team, who also could have won by more – Jude Bellingham said he had missed “two sitters” – have started with a win.

View image in fullscreen José Mourinho makes his point against the team with whom he won the treble. Photograph: Diego Souto/Getty Images

The irritation had grown. When Madrid scored the first, this placed cheered but they might have laughed too. That Madrid led didn’t make sense; not when it came to the goal, not when it came to the game either. It had taken Madrid four minutes to get a meaningful touch, and by then Courtois had already made a superb save from Marcus Thuram. But this is Madrid in the Champions League and now somehow they led. Ninety minutes later, they still did, which didn’t compute either.

Quick Guide Dortmund's Karetsas taken to hospital Show Borussia Dortmund's Konstantinos Karetsas was taken to hospital after slumping to the turf 25 minutes into his Champions League debut against Villarreal. “Konstantinos Karetsas had to leave the field due to circulatory problems,” Dortmund said in a statement. “Kosta is doing well under the circumstances and is on his way to the hospital for further tests.” The 18-year-old Greece international passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass. Karetsas was treated laying down then taken away on a stretcher. The score was 0-0 at the time. Dortmund went on to win 3-2 at home. Renato Veiga’s 53rd-minute own goal put the Bundesliga side ahead before Santiago Mouriño equalised in the 66th. Serhou Guirassy restored the lead in the 80th minute and scored the third with an 84th-minute penalty, before scoring an own goal in added time while trying to help in defence. Real Betis twice came from behind to beat Lille 3-2 away, ⁠with Marc Bartra scoring in the 34th and 49th minutes before Troy Parrott’s 54th-minute winner. Lille ​scored their opener in the 12th minute ‌and regained the lead through ‌Alexsandro in the 37th. The hosts later had Ethan Mbappé sent off for an elbow to ‌the face of an opponent. AEK Athens ​made a winning start, beating the Austrian side LASK 1-0 in Greece thanks to Romanian midfielder Razvan Marin’s curling free-kick midway through the first half. Agencies Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Inter had been playing with what looked like ease until suddenly even the simplest things looked complicated. Hakan Calhanoglu and Lautaro Martínez had just fired off the third and fourth shots without reward when it happened. Inter had enjoyed 65% of possession so far but gave it up in a way that was comic. Curtis Jones struggled with the first ball, playing to Yann Bisseck who fatally lost his bearing and his footing. Stumbling like someone attached his legs the wrong way round, he gave it to Brahím Diaz who sent Mbappé away to score.

It was Madrid’s first shot and the opening goal. If that was silly, what came next was even more ridiculous. What is it Madrid do to goalkeepers in this competition? Receiving on his line, Josep Martínez saw Valverde steaming in and tried a drag back, which failed. A flick of the ankle and the Uruguayan had scored. Twenty-three minutes, two shots, 2-0. “That was not chance,” Mourinho said and the lead might have grown when another robbery saw Vinícius dashing away. Bissek, this time, made a fantastic saving challenge. For all the fortune this felt like a plan now: force the mistake, punish it. Madrid forced more too, which they didn’t punish.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Kylian Mbappé opens the scoring for Real Madrid in the 14th minute. Photograph: Violeta Santos Moura/Reuters

Inter recovered and reasserted themselves, a calmness in possession at one end that contrasted with the calamitousness further back. Curtis Jones, Lautaro Martínez and Augusto virtually walked into the area, where Jones’ effort smashed the crossbar. Then another gift, from Benjamin Pavard, saw Madrid escape just before the break. Bellingham was denied by a wonderful stop from Josep Martínez and Díaz hit the post. Inter led 12-3 in shots, boasted 70% possession and had completed 125 final third passes to Madrid’s 13. Madrid, though, led.

Those numbers evened as the game opened, the second half beginning with Josep Martínez coming out to stop Mbappé before Inter came back at them. Courtois saved from Jones, Nicolò Barella shot wide and Thuram scooped over. The roar that then greeted an outrageous Courtois double stop spoke of disbelief, although the flag was up. The feeling was similar when Josep Martínez scrambled across his line to stop Bellingham after Díaz’s glorious scoop over him and into the Englishman.

A competition built between the keepers. Madrid could have killed this, many times. Inter could have revived it. Courtois saved from Alessandro Bastoni. Josep Martínez saved from Mbappé with his legs. That was 6-5 to Courtois. There were whistles, frustration, but chances too: the 20 seconds or so between Lautaro Martínez being blocked at one end and Díaz slotting wide at the other told a tale. Inter finally scored when another incisive exchange saw Lautaro Martínez pull back for Augusto to score. There were f15 minutes left and a game on, but that, somehow, was that. Which didn’t make sense either.

Sports.title: Haaland double gives Manchester City ideal Champions League start in Porto
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca admitted a liking for the “boom-boom” of house music in the buildup to this match, then enjoyed the sweet notes of victory having overseen a gritty performance from his Manchester City side in incessant rain.

City had lost six of their past nine away games in the competition, and been beaten in the 2021 Champions League final at this venue, so to beat Porto and claim three points is a fillip for the manager’s nascent project.

A bust-up at half-time as the players and staff neared the tunnel may bring Uefa scrutiny, though. Images showed Rúben Dias placing a hand on what appeared to be Francesco Farioli, the Porto head coach. The defender did so as tempers frayed after a clash between Marc Guéhi and Gabriel Veiga that left the latter with a head injury, though he continued.

Informed of Dias’s act, Maresca was visibly angered when asked if his captain will be spoken to, as it could cost City. “Probably, anyway you can ask what you want but how many times you see me or my bench or the guys that work with me stand up on the bench. Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times you see their bench?” he said.

Overall, the Italian should feel exuberant. All four of his opening games have been won – maybe more than even the 46-year-old could have hoped for, Erling Haaland’s double maintaining the perfect start. The goalscoring phenomenon is now third on City’s all-time chart with 167 goals after only four years, with 59 in 59 Champions League matches.

Haaland said: “Amazing game, against the champions of Portugal. We have to deliver on the biggest stage and we did that tonight.”

Maresca gave Ayyoub Bouaddi a full debut, alongside Enzo Fernández in midfield, and the 18-year-old Moroccan impressed, though a failure to find Haaland brought a reprimand. “I told the chairman [Khaldoon al-Mubarak] we’ve got a gem there,” said Haaland. “But he should’ve played me through in the second half, I was all alone. I was a bit angry so I’ll tell him right now – but he played a good game, except that pass.”

Initially, Porto could allow City to pitter-patter passes about as there was no quickness or penetration. Farioli’s men offered an example of how when Guéhi’s ball short-changed Bouaddi, possession was nabbed, and suddenly William Gomes had to be stopped on the edge of City’s area. Earlier, Veiga sliced through and had Gianluigi Donnarumma saving: the offside flag went up but here were two warnings.

Quick Guide Dortmund's Karetsas taken to hospital Show Borussia Dortmund's Konstantinos Karetsas was taken to hospital after slumping to the turf 25 minutes into his Champions League debut against Villarreal. “Konstantinos Karetsas had to leave the field due to circulatory problems,” Dortmund said in a statement. “Kosta is doing well under the circumstances and is on his way to the hospital for further tests.” The 18-year-old Greece international passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass. Karetsas was treated laying down then taken away on a stretcher. The score was 0-0 at the time. Dortmund went on to win 3-2 at home. Renato Veiga’s 53rd-minute own goal put the Bundesliga side ahead before Santiago Mouriño equalised in the 66th. Serhou Guirassy restored the lead in the 80th minute and scored the third with an 84th-minute penalty, before scoring an own goal in added time while trying to help in defence. Real Betis twice came from behind to beat Lille 3-2 away, ⁠with Marc Bartra scoring in the 34th and 49th minutes before Troy Parrott’s 54th-minute winner. Lille ​scored their opener in the 12th minute ‌and regained the lead through ‌Alexsandro in the 37th. The hosts later had Ethan Mbappé sent off for an elbow to ‌the face of an opponent. AEK Athens ​made a winning start, beating the Austrian side LASK 1-0 in Greece thanks to Romanian midfielder Razvan Marin’s curling free-kick midway through the first half. Agencies Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Discard the ponderous pace might have been Maresca’s message because when Phil Foden switched flanks from the right and accelerated, Porto were splayed, and Haaland’s header from the cross required Diogo Costa to keep the contest goalless.

A near-carbon copy arrived when Antoine Semenyo popped the ball over from the left but, this time, Haaland’s header sailed over. City were warming up: Foden, Rayan Cherki and Haaland all being denied, as Porto were caught in a chokehold around their area.

At Leicester and then Chelsea Maresca drew criticism for a quasi-sideways style. Yet tonight’s XI had become direct and a threat, as when Bouaddi chipped the ball left from near halfway, it went forward at speed, and a panicked Porto cleared.

Now, when Veiga went down after the challenge with Guéhi, the match was halted and the discord that continued to the tunnel area started up.

Yet following the seemingly de rigueur fireworks before every Champions League game, Porto had begun with sky-high confidence after winning all of their five Primeira Liga outings, so when wandering off they remained content.

The mood changed instantaneously on their return. City, at last, showed the ruthlessness needed at this level. Cherki, broke into the area, swerved left, leaving Costa stranded. He fed Fernández and Haaland headed the delivery into the turf and home and the visitors had a priceless lead.

What would be Porto’s response? To rove upfield and go close to the equaliser, was the answer, a corollary of City’s openness, as when André Silva had an age to dip right and let fly, the former Portugal forward’s attempt hitting the side netting.

View image in fullscreen Erling Haaland outjumps Jakub Kiwior to head City into the lead. Photograph: Clive Brunskill/Getty Images

The lead was slender, as it was in Saturday’s 1-0 win over Coventry. Maresca acted when the hour passed, removing Cherki and Semenyo for Elliot Anderson and Iliman Ndiaye: two attackers for one forward and a holding player in Anderson whose role was to exert control and aid Bouaddi in snuffing out any Porto threat.

A second goal would also stymie the hosts, so Ndiaye skipped across the grass and unloaded, but the effort went straight into Costa’s clutches. Foden, too, tried to break in behind, but the ball was shepherded back to the Porto keeper.

Whenever Farioli’s team moved forward City remained vulnerable, despite Anderson’s presence. At the death, though, Haaland’s right-footed finish made sure of victory and meant that even when tempers flared again it was of zero import to Maresca’s team, who had emerged victorious on a difficult evening.

Sports.title: First-half treble powers Aston Villa to Champions League win at Club Brugge
Sports.content:
Aston Villa were 3-1 up after 43 minutes but were made to sweat for their first win of the season, emerging victorious from an entertaining Champions League opener with Club Brugge. John McGinn, who struck the only goal when Villa belatedly got their season up and running last September against Bologna, opened the scoring before Emi Buendía and a first goal for Nicolas Jackson in claret and blue appeared to put Villa out of sight at half-time.

The Belgian side have become familiar foes since Villa returned to the big time, the glitziest club competition of them all; a freakish Tyrone Mings handball gifted the hosts a penalty, and subsequently victory, in 2024-25 and on this occasion Aaron Wan-Bissaka conceded a second-half penalty to plunge a seesawing contest back into the balance.

“Today was a very important step forward, being resilient when we were struggling,” said Unai Emery. “It is very important to start with three points. Hopefully it gives us confidence for the next matches, in the Premier League this Saturday against Nottingham Forest.”

Emery had been at pains to radiate positivity despite another slow start – Villa picked up their first point of the Premier League season at the weekend and these goals represented their first of the campaign – but he was typically animated on the touchline in Brugge. He was particularly agitated midway through the second half when he felt, not for the first time this season, his substitutes were not ready for action. At Hull last weekend, it was Tammy Abraham and Wan-Bissaka, and a few days earlier Alejandro Garnacho against Arsenal.

This time the culprits were Alysson, Ross Barkley and Lamare Bogarde. “In the dressing room at half-time we were speaking about some players who were tired, [Boubacar] Kamara, Wan-Bissaka,” Villa’s manager said. “I tried to keep [them on for] 15 minutes, but when I asked the players to replace [them] they were talking through the set pieces, sorting individual issues, but I needed quickly their impact on the field, and they did afterwards.”

Karetsas was treated laying down then taken away on a stretcher. The score was 0-0 at the time. Dortmund went on to win 3-2 at home. Renato Veiga’s 53rd-minute own goal put the Bundesliga side ahead before Santiago Mouriño equalised in the 66th. Serhou Guirassy restored the lead in the 80th minute and scored the third with an 84th-minute penalty, before scoring an own goal in added time while trying to help in defence. Real Betis twice came from behind to beat Lille 3-2 away, ⁠with Marc Bartra scoring in the 34th and 49th minutes before Troy Parrott’s 54th-minute winner. Lille ​scored their opener in the 12th minute ‌and regained the lead through ‌Alexsandro in the 37th. The hosts later had Ethan Mbappé sent off for an elbow to ‌the face of an opponent. AEK Athens ​made a winning start, beating the Austrian side LASK 1-0 in Greece thanks to Romanian midfielder Razvan Marin’s curling free-kick midway through the first half. Agencies Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

In the end, it was a blend of old and new faces that got Villa over the line. Zion Suzuki made a couple of fine saves, João Gomes put in a typically tigerish performance and Jackson got the goal an encouraging all-round display deserved. The 19-year-old George Hemmings did not look out of place on his Champions League debut. “The old players need to keep our standards high, to show everybody this is the only way we can achieve the process in our objectives and targets,” Emery said. “I am so happy.”

Pau Torres was the unlikely catalyst for two of Villa’s three first-half goals. McGinn’s opener was a product of the centre-back roaming unchallenged to the edge of the box. Presumably it crossed Torres’s mind to shoot, though just as he was getting giddy, he spread play to McGinn, who guided a superb first-time, left-foot strike into the far corner of Yann Sommer’s goal. In starting on Tuesday night, the Swiss became just the second goalkeeper to represent five clubs in the Champions League, but it was a night to forget for the 37-year-old.

View image in fullscreen John McGinn punches the air after giving Aston Villa an 11th-minute lead. Photograph: PA Wire/PA

Club Brugge replied when the lively Jan Virgili found a way past Wan-Bissaka – who was making his full Villa debut – and located Hugo Vetlesen in the box, the Norway midfielder sending a crisp finish beyond Suzuki. The hosts were level for less than three minutes, a slick Villa move culminating in Buendía wheeling away in celebration. Jackson’s deft backheel supplied Gomes, who twisted inside the box and then picked out Buendía who did the rest.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Villa’s third arrived a few minutes before the interval. Emery punched the air, his delight at establishing a two-goal advantage plain to see. Torres collected the ball on the edge of the Villa 18-yard box and, after shifting the ball out of his feet, he sent a lofted pass spinning into the opposition half, where Jackson got in between the opposition centre-backs, Lee Han-beom and Brandon Mechele. Enter Sommer, who raced about 40 yards from goal. Jackson swiped the ball cleanly and then was too strong for Lee before passing into an empty net.

Things appeared rosy, but Villa had to withstand heavy pressure after a video assistant referee review led the Swiss referee, Sandro Schärer, to penalise Wan-Bissaka for handball in the box. Nicolò Tresoldi sent Suzuki the wrong way from the penalty spot and a few minutes later Suzuki pushed another shot on to the post.

Victor Lindelöf tested the nerves of Emery, slicing a routine clearance when attempting to relieve the pressure. Villa, too, had chances, Jackson getting a shot away after latching on to a McGinn pass and Bogarde had a shot cleared off the line by the home full-back Joaquin Seys.

Sports.title: Newcastle progress as Joe Willock strikes late to see off Millwall
Sports.content:
Newcastle did just enough in south-east London to progress to the next round of the Carabao Cup. Joe Willock scored the only goal of this boisterous, fun, slightly vague cup tie against a spirited Millwall team that was not so much down to the bare bones, as the bones beneath the bones.

By the end there was a sense both sets of fans were more or less happy. Millwall for the vigour of the performance and Newcastle for the result, the clean sheet and any signs of early progress in the dawning of the age of Jaissle-ball.

“We were worth it, we faced it, we did it,” was Matthias Jaissle’s verdict, having sent out a strong team, Jacob Ramsey coming in on the right for the early-season hot-hands Anthony Elanga. This was a significant win for Newcastle, who have been excitingly direct at times under their twinkly new manager, with his much-trailed blueprint for rapid transition, hyper-vertical attack and getting it forward quick-smart to the lads up front, but who still need to groove that system.

Millwall also are not sure what they are yet this season, although this is more to do with injuries. They have 13 players out, which is at least an improvement on the previous 15. Absurdly, Alex Neil has already come under some pressure after a couple of losses. Football needs its irrational edge, but there is also a limit.

Quick Guide Carabao Cup roundup: Rose gets his first win Show Ryan Christie hit a hat-trick as Marco Rose celebrated his first win as Bournemouth manager with a 4-0 demolition of Lincoln in the Carabao Cup third round. Substitute Rayan completed the scoring against the Championship Imps at the Vitality Stadium. Jørgen Strand Larsen struck twice to propel Crystal Palace to a 3-0 success over Middlesbrough at Selhurst Park. Strand Larsen nodded home in each half before substitute Daichi Kamada lobbed Boro goalkeeper Sol Brynn to seal victory. Chemsdine Talbi scored the only goal to earn Sunderland a 1-0 win against Premier League rivals Hull at the Stadium of Light. Bradford came from behind to win 3-1 at fellow League One club Leyton Orient. Goals from Will Swan, Stephen Humphrys and Nick Powell overturned a Macaulay Gillesphey own goal. Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

At kick-off the sky was still a deep blackish blue above the lip of the Dockers Stand, the lights of the south London trains trundling past the unfilled corners of the ground. The Den was its usual self, a place that always manages somehow to generate that unique crackle of nonchalant hostility, no matter how midweek the crowd (and this one was a near-full house).

View image in fullscreen It was a pretty busy night down at The Den. Photograph: Ashley Western/Colorsport/Shutterstock

Newcastle had most of the ball early on, but looked like what they are, a team still finding its shapes and rhythms. “They are PONY, Wall!” was one measured home fan assessment of the Jaissle project at this early stage.

It is a fair point perhaps. Newcastle’s manager does have a very precise idea of the patterns and tempo-shifts he wants from his team. This sort of systems-football can lead to periods of drift while players learn the brief.

Newcastle settled and began to dominate possession. Willock had the first real chance, snatching the ball from Romain Esse deep in the right-back zone and shooting powerfully but too close to Filip Marschall.

In return Millwall offered graft, full-stretch defence and two deep banks of four in the classic old-school style. With 36 minutes gone Caleb Taylor headed just wide charging on to a nicely flighted free-kick, their first effort at goal. By half-time this had become something more like a cup tie as Millwall created pressure down the left, ratted and pressed nicely in midfield, and delivered some potent set pieces.

Tino Livramento came on for Amar Dedic at the break. But it was Millwall who began at a clip, a zinging low cross from the right creating a scramble close to the Newcastle goalline, the ball eventually falling to Jenson Metcalfe, who shot with power just over the bar.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

After which it was more diffuse pressure from Newcastle. Most teams would feel the absence of a midfielder of Bruno Guimarães’ passing quality. This one definitely does.

View image in fullscreen Millwall’s Tairyk Arconte hits the post shortly before Newcastle’s goal. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters

For a while the game looked like it was, an early season cup distraction for two chop and change teams, no lack of energy, but all feints and ducks and grapples, like a boxer warming up in the mirror. By the hour mark Newcastle had 70% possession plus 17 shots at goal, but somehow Millwall’s collection of hurled together parts still looked more likely to create a telling chance.

Elanga came on, a measure of Newcastle’s desire to get this done. Millwall had the best chance of the game up to that point on 79 minutes, Taïryk Arconte, a real menace on the right, hitting the post with a shot that pinged back on to Lukas Hornicek’s body but somehow stayed out.

Moments later Newcastle scored with their first real moment of quality near goal. It was a lovely move to make it. Matias Fernandez-Pardo produced the key pass, a cute little shimmy and nudge outside to Lewis Hall. His cross found Willock in the centre, who finished it with a smart side-foot shot across the face of goal.

Millwall continued to press, without finding much penetration and by the final whistle there was a concerted wave of noise coming from the full half-end of Newcastle fans, for whom the journey home into Wednesday morning would at least be a happy one.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: West Ham go top after Bowen double sinks Bolton
Sports.content:
Captain Jarrod Bowen scored twice as West Ham’s 3-2 win over Bolton took them top of the Championship on goal difference. The England international opened the scoring after 13 minutes and earned his side a first win at Bolton for 31 years with his second 13 minutes from time.

In between, Wanderers, beaten for a fourth successive outing, equalised through midfielder Ethan Erhahon’s maiden goal for the club and they looked on course for a ninth successive league victory over the Hammers when Ruben Rodrigues converted a 27th-minute penalty. Instead, Konstantinos Mavropanos levelled with a 31st-minute header and Bowen completed the comeback.

Cyle Larin scored his fifth goal of the season as Southampton beat Swansea 3-1 to beat the side who were top of the table for the second home match in a row. Larin, who is the joint-top scorer in the Championship, found the net either side of Finn Azaz and Leo Scienza strikes to make it 13 games unbeaten at St Mary’s.

Watford shook off an awful first-half display to grab a 2-1 victory over Preston, who suffered their fifth defeat in six league games. Callum Lang had put the visitors ahead in the sixth minute as they threatened to overrun the Hornets, who hit back with two second-half goals in seven minutes from Edo Kayembe and Mamadou Doumbia.

Wrexham’s wait for a home win goes on after they were held to a 1-1 draw by winless Burnley who sit one place off the bottom of the table. Jacques Ekomie headed in his second goal for the club since joining in a £7m deal from Angers, cancelling out Zeki Amdouni’s first-half effort for the Clarets who at least ended a run of seven straight away defeats dating back to last term.

But it was a result that does little to help either side in their pursuit of promotion, with Wrexham having lost the momentum they carried into last season while Burnley face bigger problems after relegation from the top flight, having won only one league game since October. Former England striker Jamie Vardy joined this week, but the 39-year-old was suspended for this match as a result of yellow cards collected during his time with Italian side Cremonese.

Sheffield United returned to winning ways after a display of ruthless finishing secured a 2-1 win at Blackburn. All the goals came in a first half that Rovers dominated and deservedly took the lead in through Kristi Montgomery’s first goal for the club on 20 minutes. The Blades turned the game on its head with goals from their only two shots of the half as Tom Cannon stroked home a second on this ground in two weeks in the 35th minute. Sydie Peck rifled home his first of the season a minute before the break to complete the turnaround.

Cardiff’s winless start to the season continued as Stoke held on for a 1-1 draw in the Welsh capital and their first away point since January. Stoke had hope of an away-day success after a run of nine straight Championship defeats when Ben Johnson scored midway through the first half. But the Potters came under fierce pressure in the second half and Joel Colwill’s headed home for Cardiff hosts who hit a post three times. The draw – Cardiff’s fourth in six games – was enough to take the home side out of the relegation zone, while Stoke slip to 15th.

Sports.title: Air traffic chaos delays Arsenal flight to Naples for Champions League
Sports.content:
Arsenal’s preparations for their opening Champions League game against Napoli have been disrupted after they were caught up in the travel chaos that affected airports across the UK.

Mikel Arteta was forced to cancel his pre-match press conference at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on Tuesday after Arsenal’s flight was severely delayed by an air-traffic control issue. The Arsenal manager and his players are understood to have remained at the club’s training ground in Hertfordshire as they waited for the delay to pass after completing their morning session as usual.

Club sources have insisted there has been no alteration to their planned schedule other than arriving later than expected to the team hotel. Uefa has also agreed to allow Arsenal to cancel their mandatory press conference due to the delays, which have also affected supporters travelling to Italy for the match.

Jurriën Timber is set to be part of the Arsenal squad for the first time since the Champions League final defeat by Paris Saint-Germain on 30 May after recovering from a groin injury. The Netherlands defender missed the World Cup due to the problem that has dogged him since March but Arteta said before Sunday’s win over Chelsea that Timber was close to returning.

Cristhian Mosquera is still absent with a muscle issue but Marli Salmon, the 17-year-old defender who signed his first professional deal last month, is also part of the 23-man squad.

Arsenal won all eight of their group stage matches in the Champions League last season on their way to the final and have only lost one in their last 12 away games in the competition. But as they prepare for one of Europe’s most intimidating atmospheres, Arteta insisted they must take one game at a time despite starting the season with a 100% record in the Premier League.

“That puts us in a really good situation. The energy and the confidence around the team is high – now we have to show that,” he said.

“I’ve been in that stadium before, I know the atmosphere they create. The record at home is really, really strong. We know the challenge ahead. We are prepared and we’re ready to go.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Napoli finished as runners up behind Inter in Serie A last season, but have made a poor start this season under their new manager, Massimiliano Allegri. Kevin De Bruyne is expected to feature against Arsenal but they are without Scott McTominay, who had a successful surgical procedure to treat an irregular heartbeat yesterday. The 29-year-old is expected to resume training in two weeks.

Napoli are also are likely to be without influential former Fulham midfielder André-Frank Zambo Anguissa as Allegri takes charge of his first Champions League match for four years. “People in this town have passion for the team, we have to start winning games again,” Allegri said. “We know we are challenging a very strong team – Arteta has done extraordinary things. Let’s face it with pride and desire.”

Sports.title: Harry Kane and Alessia Russo among nominees for this year’s Ballon d’Or
Sports.content:
Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice have been nominated for this year’s men’s Ballon d’Or with Alessia Russo and Alex Greenwood nominated for the women’s award.

The 30 men’s and 30 women’s nominees were revealed by France Football magazine on Tuesday, with the winners to be announced at a ceremony in London on 26 October. Ousmane Dembélé, who won the men’s award last year, has been nominated again, as has his France teammate Kylian Mbappé, who made history when he overtook Lionel Messi for all-time World Cup goals (22) at this summer’s tournament.

In the women’s field, two-time winner Alexia Putellas, Ewa Pajor and Melchie Dumornay are among the favourites to succeed Aitana Bonmatí. Winner of the past three awards, Bonmatí did not make the cut after missing most of the season through injury. The Spaniard returned at the end of Barcelona’s quadruple-winning season that included another Champions League title.

Kane is odds-on to win the men’s award after a club-record 61 goals in 51 games for German double winners Bayern Munich last season. He also scored six times at the World Cup for England, a tournament where Bellingham and Rice shone as well, the latter also playing a key role in Arsenal ending a 22-year wait for the Premier League title.

Women's award Selma Bacha, Barbra Banda, Klara Buhl, Esmee Brugts, Mariona Caldentey, Scarlett Camberos, Kerstin Casparij, Temwa Chawinga, Cata Coll, Melchie Dumornay, Caroline Graham Hansen, Alex Greenwood, Patri Guijarro, Pernille Harder, Yui Hasegawa, Rose Lavelle, Mapi León, Lorena, Melvine Malard, Manaka Matsukubo, Vivianne Miedema, Ewa Pajor, Claudia Pina, Alexia Putellas, Wendie Renard, Alessia Russo, Khadija Shaw, Momoko Tanikawa, Caroline Weir, Tessa Wullaert. Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Lamine Yamal, who won La Liga with Barcelona and the World Cup with Spain, is second favourite to win the award, followed by his club and international teammate Rodri. Messi, who has a record eight Ballon d’Or awards, is on the shortlist after guiding Argentina to the World Cup final and winning Major League Soccer with Inter Miami.

Russo finished third in last year’s voting and enjoyed another successful individual campaign, scoring 24 goals in 40 club appearances. Greenwood, the Manchester City captain, lifted the Women’s Super League and FA Cup last season.

The Ballon d’Or ceremony is moving from its traditional Paris home to London this year to mark the 70th anniversary of the first award won by England great Stanley Matthews.

Sports.title: More than 100,000 people add names to complaint against Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
More than 100,000 people have added their names to a complaint against Gianni Infantino, alleging the Fifa president has “at a minimum, abused his power, violated his duty of political neutrality, and violated his duty of loyalty” through his interactions with Donald Trump.

The Reboot Fifa campaign was launched before the World Cup with the aim of delivering “the biggest complaint Fifa has ever received” over the organisation’s alleged failings of governance. The campaign has since extended the scope of its accusations to include the reversal of the ban for Folarin Balogun at the tournament and the aborted Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme.

The complaint was submitted on Tuesday to Fifa’s ethics committee and in a supporting letter the organisers of Reboot Fifa, the advocacy group Fair Square, call on the committee to take action. An original complaint, submitted in December of last year, failed to receive a response from the committee but has gained the backing of the Norwegian football federation and 50 European parliamentarians.

“The fact that 100,000 individuals added their names to this call for accountability is clear evidence of mounting public concern,” the Fair Square letter said. “As the independent judicial body tasked with the critical task of upholding the ‘integrity and reputation of football’, the ethics committee must not only act, it must be seen to act with appropriate haste, transparency and rigour.”

The letter lists eight incidents that form the basis of the Reboot Fifa complaint, which Fair Square alleges “provide compelling evidence that the Fifa president has, at a minimum, abused his power, violated his duty of political neutrality, and violated his duty of loyalty in his efforts to ingratiate himself with the US president.”

. The incidents include the Balogun affair – where Trump admitted he asked Fifa to review the US striker’s red card – and the FFE scandal. They also cite the awarding of the Fifa peace prize to Trump, Infantino’s involvement in Trump’s Board of Peace in the Middle East and the Fifa president’s promise to work with Trump to “make not only America great again but also the entire world”, an act Fair Square suggests shows a failure to remain politically neutral.

Fifa, when approached for comment, pointed to a statement first published a month ago. “It is increasingly evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president,” the statement said.

“Those who do not have the support of Fifa’s member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through Fifa’s established democratic processes.”
