Fifa confirmed on Sunday that Infantino would be seeking re-election for a fourth and final term next year despite pressure from Uefa and criticism from within the Asian confederation and Concacaf (the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation). Uefa has called on Infantino to stand down and recently announced its intention to pursue criminal claims in the US over the FFE plans.

Sports.title: ‘Disgrace’ – Incandescent Erling Haaland pulled away after wrestling Porto player in furious clash on ground
Sports.content:
‘Disgrace’ – Incandescent Erling Haaland pulled away after wrestling Porto player in furious clash on ground

Erling Haaland had to be dragged away from a heated incident during Manchester City's Champions League win over Porto.

Tensions boiled over in second-half stoppage time as Man City began their European campaign with a 2-0 win in Portugal thanks to a brace from Haaland.



5 Haaland achieved two milestones with his double in Porto Credit: Getty

5 Although there was an unsavoury end to the contest Credit: Getty

And the striker was at the centre of the flashpoint, clashing with Porto's Pablo Rosario and sparking a melee on the pitch.

Haaland was hurled to the ground by Rosario, with both players booked by referee Szymon Marciniak.



But talkSPORT's Adrian Durham wasn't impressed with the Porto man at all and took issue with Marciniak's officiating of the incident.

"Really naive refereeing," Durham said on air. "Rosario's basically trying to get Haaland sent off and it's a disgrace. Really poor refereeing, that."



It wasn't the first coming together of its nature on the night at the Estadio do Dragao.

Security staff had to step in as players and officials from both sides clashed at half time.



Porto had taken issue after Gabri Veiga was left bleeding from his head after being accidentally struck by Marc Guehi's trailing arm during an aerial challenge.

Guehi escaped any punishment – much to Porto's dismay – on a night which, perhaps surprisingly given how things flared up, saw only three players booked: Rosario, Haaland and his City teammate Josko Gvardiol.

That late scuffle aside, it was a celebratory, historic occasion for Haaland.

In notching his fourth and fifth goals of the season, and his 166th and 167th overall for City, he moved up to third on the club's all-time leading scorers list.



5 Enzo Maresca's perfect start to life at City goes on – it's now four wins out of four Credit: Getty

5 And Haaland has scored in three of them Credit: Getty

The Norway star has overtaken 1920s City hero Tommy Johnson, who scored City goals.

It represents a remarkable achievement for Haaland, who only moved to the Etihad Stadium four years ago but will be going for his fourth Premier League Golden Boot in five seasons in 2026/27.



Since arriving from Borussia Dortmund in 2022, he's gone along at a truly prolific average of 0.82 goals per game in all competitions.

The 26-year-old now has only Eric Brook (177 goals) and Sergio Aguero (still well out in front on 260 goals) left to catch.

5 Haaland needs 93 more goals to catch Aguero Credit: Getty

That being said, Haaland has already emulated Aguero in one respect, drawing level with him for the most Champions League goals for City with 36.



Haaland also goes clear of Bayern Munich legend Thomas Muller to take seventh place outright on the all-time list of leading Champions League scorers with 59 in total – at a remarkable average of exactly one a game.

For some comparison, it took Lionel Messi 80 Champions League appearances to reach 60 goals in the competition.

The Champions League continues

Elsewhere on the opening night of Champions League action, Aston Villa got their first win of the season, edging a 3-2 thriller against Club Brugge.

Two more English clubs are in action on Wednesday: Liverpool entertain Atletico Madrid and Arsenal travel to Napoli, amid travel chaos due to air traffic control issues in the UK.



Arsenal's game is live on talkSPORT 2, with Manchester United's home Champions League opener against Sabah on Thursday live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Scott McTominay undergoes heart surgery as Napoli give return timeline
Sports.content:
Scott McTominay has undergone successful surgery on a heart issue, Napoli have confirmed.

McTominay was diagnosed with mild benign arrhythmia, which is an irregular heartbeat.



2 McTominay has had surgery on a heart issue Credit: AFP

A statement from Napoli read: "On Tuesday morning, Scott McTominay underwent an ablation procedure at Spire Manchester Hospital. The operation was a complete success.

McTominay will rest for two weeks and then resume training."

What is cardiac arrhythmia ablation?

Cardiac arrhythmia ablation is a short procedure that, according to the British Heart Foundation, can last as little as just 15 minutes.

During surgery, a small cut is made on the patient's groin or wrist, with catheters are then placed inside and moved up to the heart.



The area inside the heart that has caused the arrhythmia is then destroyed by either radiofrequency energy or cryoablation.

This step of the procedure helps to block abnormal electrical signals in the heart.



McTominay played in Napoli's first two Serie A fixtures this season and was brought off in the 2-1 defeat to Como.

Max Allegri's side are back in action at home to Arsenal in their Champions League opener on Wednesday, live on talkSPORT 2.



Napoli previously expected McTominay to be out of action until mid-October.

If that is still the case, he would miss Scotland's upcoming internationals. Scotland have four fixtures scheduled for the newly extended international break beginning later this month.

2 McTominay could miss the international break with Scotland Credit: Getty

Slovenia, Switzerland and North Macedonia are their Nations League opponents as they begin their Group B1 campaign.



Sebastien Pocognoli will take charge of the side for the first time since being announced as the replacement for Steve Clarke.

The former Belgium and Premier League defender was previously with the Belgian U18s, Royale Union Saint-Gilloise and AS Monaco.

Pocognoli has joined a Scotland team that had a miserable World Cup campaign during the summer.

They scored one goal across their three group matches and missed out on the knockout stages.



McTominay played every minute as Scotland returned to the tournament for the first time since 1998.

Sports.title: Borussia Dortmund player rushed to hospital after being stretchered off pitch in worrying scenes
Sports.content:
Borussia Dortmund player rushed to hospital after being stretchered off pitch in worrying scenes

Borussia Dortmund winger Konstantinos Karetsas was rushed to hospital shortly after being stretched off against Villarreal.

The 18-year-old worryingly sat down on the pitch unchallenged in the 23rd minute of the Champions League match.

4 Karetsas dropped to the turf in worrying scenes on Tuesday Credit: Getty

4 Medics carried the teenager from the pitch before taking him to hospital Credit: AFP

Dortmund confirmed that the Greece international had been taken to hospital after suffering ‘circulation problems’.

Fans in attendance at Signal Iduna Park were understandably concerned by the player’s bad turn.

The club were quick to inform supporters of Karetsas’ condition and whereabouts.

They wrote on X: “Konstantinos Karetsas had to leave the pitch in the game against Villarreal due to circulation problems.

“Kosta is doing as well as can be expected given the circumstances, and he is on his way to the hospital for further examinations.”

He was quickly replaced by Arsenal star Ethan Nwaneri who joined the Bundesliga side on a season-long loan.

Borussia Dortmund 3-2 Villarreal

Dortmund had already suffered a huge injury blow with fellow summer signing Giannis Konstantelias suffered an Anterior Cruciate Ligament injury on the opening weekend of the season.

The injury is likely to keep him out of action for much of the campaign.

Nico Kovac's side were quick to regroup after the interval and showed their quality in an action-packed second half which saw Dortmund edge a five-goal thriller.

They were given a helping hand in eight minutes after half time thanks to an own goal from former Chelsea defender Renato Veiga.

4 Karetsas was a summer signing from Belgian club Genk Credit: Getty

Santiago Mourino leveled shortly afterwards for the La Liga side until Dortmund striker Sehrou Guirassy took centre stage.

The Guinean netted twice in the final ten minutes to hand his side a crucial three points.

He then incredibly put through his own net in the third minute of added time to put a nervous spin on the final exchanges.

Dortmund are not among the favourites to lift the Champions League but boast plenty of know how in reaching the latter stages,

Winners of the competition in 1997, Dortmund have since contested two finals - both stages at Wembley.

They were beaten 2-1 by Bayern Munich in an all-German affair in 2013.

4 Serhou Guirassy was decisive against Villarreal - at both ends! Credit: Getty

Their second attempt at glory came in 2024 but slipped to a 2-0 defeat to a Vinicius Junior-inspired Real Madrid.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi reportedly agrees deal to buy 100 per cent stake in second tier club
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi reportedly agrees deal to buy 100 per cent stake in second tier club

Lionel Messi has reportedly agreed a deal in principle to buy Spanish second tier club Eldense.

Diario AS reports that the eight-time Ballon d'Or-winning superstar has reached an agreement to acquire 100 per cent of Eldense's shares.



2 Messi has retired from Argentina duty but is still playing for Inter Miami Credit: Getty

The report adds that Messi's lawyers had been in talks for some time with the club's current owners, the Colombian investment group TH – led by Juan Carlos Trujillo.

Eldense have just returned to LaLiga2, the second tier of Spanish football, winning promotion back to the division at the first time of asking having been relegated in the 2024/25 season.

Based in the Valencian city of Elda, Eldense are managed by former Spain striker Claudio Barragan, who won six caps for La Roja in the early 90s.



Founded in 1921, they play their home games at the 5,776-capacity Estadio Municipal Nuevo Pepico Amat.

Messi's involvement already goes beyond the pitch

This wouldn't be Messi's first venture into club ownership.

The 39-year-old Argentine – who recently announced his retirement from international football following an epic career in which he captained his country to World Cup glory – took full ownership of third-tier outfit Cornella back in April.



But Eldense would be the first professional club in his portfolio.

Messi's prospective investment is said to be a solo endeavour without the support of any partners.

The greatest of all time?

It was in Spain where Messi ascended to all-time great status, during 17 glittering years with Barcelona.



A ten-time LaLiga champion and four-time Champions League winner with Barca, Messi played 778 games to top the club's all time appearances list – not to mention amassing 672 goals to obliterate their all-time scoring record.

2 Messi averaged 0.86 goals per game for Barcelona Credit: Getty

He won six of his eight Ballons d'Or as a Barca player, before leaving in 2021 an undisputed icon.

After a two-year stint with Paris Saint-Germain, he headed to MLS to join Inter Miami in 2023.



Messi in good company among current pros

Messi isn't the only active player to have dipped their toes into the world of club ownership and he joins, among others, his great contemporary Cristiano Ronaldo.

Ronaldo purchased a 25 per cent stake in another LaLiga2 outfit, Almeria, in February this year.

Last year, Croatia legend Luka Modric became a minority investor in Championship Swansea City.

In 2024, Kylian Mbappe's Coalition Capital investment fund bought an 80 per cent stake in French club Caen.



And the previous year, fellow France star N'Golo Kante struck a deal to take over as owner of Belgian outfit Royal Excelsior Vitron.

Sports.title: Arsenal sign 40-goal wonderkid, 16, from Premier League rival a week after deadline day
Sports.content:
Arsenal have completed the signing of another young prodigy from a Premier League rival.

The Gunners have acquired 16-year-old Mylo Bernard from Crystal Palace, reaffirming their strategy to bolster their pool of academy talent.



4 Mylo Bernard has swapped Crystal Palace for Arsenal's academy Credit: official arsenal academy

Bernard has signed a pre-contract deal with the north London club and joins as a first-year scholar.

He will then go on to sign professional terms when he turns 17 next year.

The striker caught the eye of multiple clubs having netted over 40 goals for Crystal Palace’s academy teams last season.



His goalscoring heroics earned him a call-up to the Eagles’ Under-18s side where he went on to score six times in the U18 Premier League.

Bernard has also featured for England U16s, registering four goals in eight appearances.



The starlet took to Instagram after completing his move and paid a classy tribute to his formative club.

Bernard says goodbye to Palace

He wrote: “After eight unforgettable years at Crystal Palace, I have decided to say goodbye.



“I have grown up playing for Crystal Palace and it has provided so many wonderful moments in blue and red.

“Crystal Palace has shaped me as a person and a player becoming a crucial part of my life.

“It has always been a pleasure playing at the club over the last few years and this part of my journey will always have a place with me.

4 Goal machine Bernard has impressed for both club and country Credit: Getty



4 Habeeb Ogunneye arrived from Manchester United this summer Credit: Getty

“Thank you to all my coaches and teammates that have pushed me to become a better player and have helped me in my journey at the club.

“I will forever be grateful for the past eight years I’ve had with this club.”

His signing signals Arsenal’s growing ambition to bolster their options at youth level.



The Gunners have already raided Manchester United this summer for top talents James Scanlon and Habeeb Ogunneye.

And Elijah Upson – son of ex-Arsenal defender Matt Upson – left north London rivals Tottenham to sign for the Gunners

There have been further raids in recent months.

4 Elijah Upson recently crossed the north London divide Credit: Getty

Igor Tyjon swapped Blackburn Rovers for the Hale End academy , Axel Donczew arrived at the club from Cardiff City and Phoenix Blayney signed from Northern Irish club Larne.



Georgian hotshot Andria Bartishvili is also closing in on a move to the club but is unable to make the deal permanent until he turns 18 next year.

Sports.title: Who could be next sacking of the 2026/27 season? Five candidates for the chop, including two Premier League bosses
Sports.content:
Who could be next sacking of the 2026/27 season? Five candidates for the chop, including two Premier League bosses

Michael Duff became the first casualty of the season as Wycombe Wanderers axed the Englishman, but who could be next?

The life of a manager in English football can be short lived with every team across the pyramid seeking wins to achieve their goals, as Duff has just found out.



5 Duff has been removed as Wycombe's boss after a poor start to the season Credit: Getty

As a result, teams who have started poorly and are in danger of not managing to hit their expectations for the season could be tempted to make a change in the dugout.

Equally, gaffers who have been in place at their respective clubs for a while but have also started really badly are likely to be in danger as well.

The fear of stale results, relegation or not achieving promotion might prove to be a catalyst for some teams to decide that the manager is the problem.



Yes, it is very early and many players are still bedding in at their new clubs, but football is a results business and those not managing to win are at risk.

As a result, talkSPORT.com (well, me) have come up with a list of Premier League and EFL managers that would admit they are in danger (as Ralph Wiggum would ominously say).



Alvaro Arbeloa

Anyone else getting serious Frank de Boer vibes from Alvaro Arbeloa and Fulham?

The Dutchman joined Crystal Palace in 2017 as the club's new manager, and he lasted just four league games. The Eagles lost every match and didn't score a single goal.



The defeats included a 3-0 loss at home to Huddersfield and losing to Burnley at Turf Moor.

De Boer was sacked and Roy Hodgson came in, saving the club from the drop zone.

And after three Premier League matches, Fulham have zero points with Liverpool away up next...

5 It has been a poor start for Fulham and there are murmurings of discontent Credit: Getty



At least Fulham have scored four goals, but some of their defending is amateur hour.

They have swapped steady and dependable Marco Silva for a punt with Arbeloa. And so far, the punt isn't working at all.

You then add in the reports of discontent behind the scenes with Alex Iwobi and Emile Smith Rowe removing all mention of Fulham from their Instagram accounts.

I'd be surprised if he's there for much longer after the weekend unless they shock everyone at Anfield.



For me, he's likely to be the first gone.

Frank Lampard

(Puts tin hat on) Frank Lampard managed to drag Coventry City from play-off heartbreak to promotion.

For that, he will be a Sky Blues legend forever. However, we are also in De Boer territory for Lampard as well.

5 The fixture list was unkind to Coventry, but they haven't even scored yet Credit: Getty

Coventry haven't scored in the Premier League yet and lost at home to fellow promoted side Hull City. Of course, they had games against Arsenal and Manchester City.



But Coventry invested heavily in the transfer market, and they have been tipped as the most likely team to stay up from the promoted ones.

Yet, here we are three games in, and they have no points and no goals.

Aston Villa are also in the same boat, but you don't sack Unai Emery. Plus they beat Club Brugge in their Champions League opener on Tuesday night.

Surely, despite everything he's done, if that continues, they would have to make a decision around Lampard.



I can imagine this isn't a popular take, but Coventry's survival is more important than Lampard's reputation.

Paul Heckingbottom

5 Heckingbottom is in a position to be removed if this awful form continues Credit: Getty

Preston North End are the most mid-table Championship club to exist. They are very rarely in trouble and very rarely come close to the play-offs or promotion.

But after four games, they sit second bottom with one win and three defeats.



The Lancashire giants splashed out in the summer as well to bring in Alfie Devine, Harry Clarke and Johnny Kenny.

And then when you factor in last season as well, and things aren't looking great for Paul Heckingbottom.

That is because Preston managed to blow their promotion hopes with a run of four wins in 20. They did beat bitter rivals Blackburn Rovers last time out, but the pressure is absolutely on.

Russell Martin

There are very few words left to describe just how poorly Russell Martin's last three jobs have panned out.



5 Things aren't looking great for Martin at Leicester Credit: Getty

Since getting Southampton into the Premier League, it has been blow after blow for the Englishman.

He was practically chased out of Rangers by their fans last season, and he's taken on a huge challenge at Leicester City.

The Foxes have experienced back-to-back relegations, but they can't afford to be in League One for very long, or worse find themselves in League Two.



So, Martin has one objective, which is to achieve promotion, and they are 18th...

Of course, it is still early days, but the Foxes have only won a single match in the league and were beaten 4-0 by Oxford United last time out.

There is almost nothing positive for Leicester supporters to hold onto, and it would make a lot more sense for this experiment to simply end before it is too late for Leicester to save their season.

Grant McCann

The Northern Irishman has been at Doncaster Rovers for over three years, and in the 2024/25 season, they stormed to the League Two title.



They achieved their only aim of staying in the third tier last season but no wins in all competitions represents a very poor start to the campaign.

That puts McCann at risk, especially because of his time with the club and that risk of things going stale.

Of course, it is still early, but it all depends on what Doncaster want to achieve this year.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta has learnt from trusting volatile Premier League boss with key Arsenal decision
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has learnt from his mistakes by sending Ethan Nwaneri on loan to Borussia Dortmund.

That's the view of European football expert Andy Brassell, who expects the Arsenal youngster to thrive in Germany after a bumpy ride on loan at Marseille during the second half of last season.



2 Nwaneri has joined Dortmund on a season-long loan Credit: Getty

Nwaneri started promisingly with the French giants, where Mikel Arteta was happy to send the attacking midfielder to work under 'really courageous manager' Roberto De Zerbi – but De Zerbi's departure just weeks after Nwaneri's arrival threw a spanner in the works.

And Brassell thinks Arteta ought to have been more wary of De Zerbi's 'combustible' nature which might have precipitated his Marseille exit.

'A bad error'

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT, he said: "I think Mikel Arteta has learnt from the mistake he made with loaning Nwaneri to Marseille, because he sort of pinned his hopes on De Zerbi [who took over at Tottenham in March].



"De Zerbi wanted a No.10 to build the team around, but obviously De Zerbi was also on the edge of the volcano and Arteta should have realised that tying his player's fate to a combustible coach – who I think people around Marseille knew might not be that far off a complete rupture – [wasn't the best move].

"That was a bad error and that cost Nwaneri a little.

"I'm sure, on a human level, it was a growth experience for him – whereas with Dortmund, [manager] Niko Kovac is, I think, secure and in a good place, but really their idea of making the team younger and developing players, that's Ole Book the sporting director as well.



"So I think there's more of a balance, more of a calm at Dortmund, even though it's an equally enormous club. And that should really help him.

"I think he's got lots of other good young players that he can click with. This is a very different profile to the Marseille squad where it was loads of old dogs, I think you can say, on many occasions.



"Of course, they have some younger players as well, but the way they lent on expensive imports from the Premier League I don't think was a particularly positive thing for them."

But Dortmund should be a much more beneficial environment for Nwaneri, believes Brassell.

2 Nwaneri scored twice in 11 appearances for Marseille last term Credit: Getty

"It's completely different at Dortmund," he concluded. "They're playing a lot of games, including the Champions League as well. He'll get a lot of opportunities.



"I think this move is really going to work for him."

Dortmund's English influence

Nwaneri, 19, is one of two young English players in the Dortmund squad.

He's joined by Jobe Bellingham, who followed in his brother Jude's footsteps by signing for the eight-time Bundesliga champions last year.

And Nwaneri is off to a good start with BVB, playing an important part in a late match-winning own goal as his new team fought back from 2-0 down to beat Hoffenheim 3-2 on his debut last weekend.

The England Under-21 international, who became the youngest player in Premier League history when he made his Arsenal debut aged 15 years and 181 days against Brentford four years ago, will be hoping to feature again when Dortmund host Villarreal in their Champions League opener on Tuesday.

Sports.title: James Rodriguez on the brink of surprise move to second-tier club
Sports.content:
James Rodriguez on the brink of surprise move to second-tier club

James Rodriguez is reportedly closing in on a move to Serie B side US Avellino.

The ex-Real Madrid star has been a free agent since June following a brief spell in the USA having left Minnesota United.

4 Rodriguez last stepped onto a pitch at the 2026 World Cup Credit: Getty

Rodriguez spent just over three months with the MLS outfit before leaving to prepare for the World Cup.

But he could now be set to end his four-month spell without a club, having been offered an intriguing route back into the game.

Rodriguez set for Italy switch?

According to Spanish outlet Marca, Rodriguez is set to join Italian second-tier side Avellino.

As per the report, the Colombia star is currently in talks with the Serie B side, with an agreement close to being reached between both parties.

Financial terms are yet to be finalised, with this the last obstacle between the playmaker and a move to Italy.

Should Rodriguez go through with joining Avellino, he will be managed by a familiar name to football fans.

Legendary former Italy and AC Milan defender Alessandro Nesta is the current manager of the Wolves.

The 2006 World Cup winner took charge of Avellino in June, signing a two-year deal with the Campania club.

Marca's report states that Nesta has held talks with Rodriguez himself, as he looks to convince the Colombian to help inspire a Serie A promotion charge.

Avellino finished eighth in Serie B last term, the last available play-off place, but were then eliminated in the preliminary round.

4 Italy great Nesta's latest managerial role has seen him take charge of Avellino Credit: Getty

4 Rodriguez failed to score in eight appearances for last club Minnesota United Credit: Getty

They currently sit fifth in the Italian second division after the first three matches of the new season, winning twice and drawing once.

James Rodriguez's career

With Rodriguez closing in on a move to Italy, he looks set to join the 14th club of his senior career.

The attacking midfielder burst onto the scene at the 2014 World Cup, when he starred in Colombia's run to the quarter-finals.

He scored one of the goals of the tournament, a stunning volley against Uruguay, and netted another five times while also providing two assists to win the Golden Boot.

Later on in the same summer, Rodriguez moved to Real Madrid in a £63million deal, and went on to spend six years on the Spanish giants' books.

He made 125 appearances overall for the Spanish giants, and registered 37 goals and 42 assists as well as winning both LaLiga and the Champions League twice.

4 Rodriguez previously spent a year in English football at Everton Credit: GETTY

Rodriguez spent the 2017/18 and 2018/19 seasons on loan at Bayern Munich, scoring 15 goals to help clinch back-to-back Bundesliga titles.

In September 2020, the playmaker joined Everton as he reunited with former Real Madrid boss Carlo Ancelotti.

He enjoyed a strong season with the Toffees, scoring six and assisting nine goals in 26 appearances across all competitions throughout the 2020/21 campaign.

However, Rafael Benitez took over as manager in June 2021 - a move Rodriguez has since revealed effectively spelled the end of his time in Merseyside - and he departed for Qatari outfit Al Rayyan in September of the same year.

Rodriguez has had a nomadic career since then, moving to Greek side Olympiakos in 2022, before leaving and spending a year in Brazil at Sao Paulo.

A return to Spain with Rayo Vallecano followed in the 2024/25 campaign, and he then moved on to Mexican outfit Leon, before an eight-game stint in MLS with Minnesota United earlier this year.

Sports.title: The three things Arsenal need to do this season to finally win the Champions League - from the players Mikel Arteta must learn to trust to the January transfer window plan and a returning hero
Sports.content:
The Hilton Budapest had been primed, a function room already booked in advance for Arsenal’s staff and players after last season’s Champions League final.

But instead of a raucous party to mark a first European Cup in the club’s 140-year history, a few reflective, sorrows-drowning drinks followed before an early flight back to London for the Premier League title parade through the streets of north London.

The disappointment exuding from Mikel Arteta in the post-match press conference following the defeat on penalties by Paris Saint-Germain was marked. Ending a 22-year wait for a Premier League title had gone out the window, his words verged on anger.

‘Pain, that's it, when you are so close in the competition and you are a few penalty kicks away from winning the biggest football club competition, that's the way which you feel,’ he said.

After ending that long, agonising wait to be crowned champions of England, conquering Europe is Arteta's final frontier. The Spaniard has never tasted success in a European competition as a player or manager, and often uses the Champions League as a reference point in how legacies are defined.

Arsenal are well primed to make that final step. They were, after all, only a few kicks from glory in May, and have strengthened further this summer with additions such as Bruno Guimaraes, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa. But how do they get over that final hurdle?

Mikel Arteta's side were a penalty shootout away from finally lifting their first European Cup against Paris Saint-Germain in Budapest in May

Gabriel's decisive miss from the spot was an agonising end to a season that could have been historic

1. Trust the depth

Arsenal’s squad depth gives Arteta the luxury of rotating without necessarily weakening the starting XI.

Ben White has made a case to continue at right back even when Jurrien Timber returns from injury, his telepathic connection with Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard forming a triumvirate which opponents have difficulty stopping on the right flank.

In the middle, Myles Lewis-Skelly has performed well in place of the injured Bruno Guimaraes. The new £75million Brazilian is expected to walk into the line-up on Wednesday against Napoli but after his recent displays, Lewis-Skelly will be on the Brazilian’s heels if there’s any dip in form. It’s a great situation to have for Arteta. But he still needs to utilise it.

Last season, he arguably gave far too many minutes to Declan Rice when he was already tiring, for example. The England midfielder, who went on to play a key role at the World Cup, made 55 appearances in all competitions, with 49 starts and 4,454 minutes, or 91 per cent of Arsenal's minutes when he was available for selection. No Arsenal outfielder played more. Rice himself during the World Cup admitted he had been playing through neural pain in his hamstring since December.

Arsenal had four outfield players above 4,200 minutes - Rice, Martin Zubimendi (4,298), William Saliba (4,254) and Gabriel (4,210). This level of excessive workload must be better shared if Arsenal are to go all the way to the final again, and potentially lift the elusive trophy.

Zubimendi and Rice's back-up, Christian Norgaard, were not trusted to give the Spaniard a rest, but now Lewis-Skelly or Guimaraes can offer that. Konsa can cover while Saliba and Cristhian Mosquera are injured, and Piero Hincapie can slot seamlessly in if Gabriel needs a spell out.

Even Arteta hinted at this in Budapest after the defeat by PSG, saying: ‘You have to get into the competition with all the squad available in the best moment, each player. And we've had more players, many more players than last season but not all of them in that condition for different reasons. And that's something we have to improve as well.’ At least he’s aware. Now he needs to trust those on the bench to get him through.

Declan Rice has spoken of the neural pain he suffered from this summer, and surely cannot keep on playing as many minutes as he did last season

In Myles Lewis-Skelly and Bruno Guimaraes, Arteta has two high-class options he can call on to give Rice a rest

2. Go again in January

Viktor Gyokeres has fallen down the pecking order with Kai Havertz fully fit.

It was always the plan last season, but an injury to Havertz on the opening day at Old Trafford last season resulted in Gyokeres becoming the Gunners’ first-choice striker in the previous campaign, where he struck 21 goals across all competitions after joining for £56million.

The Swede, though, has only made one substitute appearance in three league matches, coming off the bench for 12 minutes against Chelsea on Sunday and showing signs of rust.

After Havertz and Gyokeres, though, Arteta’s options thin out dramatically. Midfielder Mikel Merino could once again be thrown up front to fill the gap, though this would not be ideal. Having failed in their chase for either Vinicius Junior, Julian Alvarez or Lautaro Martinez, Arsenal are very light in the striker position.

It begs the question: can the club lure the likes of Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi in the January window? He’s a player Arteta admires, has a special place in fans' hearts after scoring the goal that helped seal the title in May and could provide the firepower needed to get Arsenal over the line in Europe too.

Eli Junior Kroupi scored home and away for Bournemouth against Arsenal last season - could he be the missing piece in Arteta's puzzle?

3. Timber's limbering up

The importance of Timber can’t be overstated. In the Budapest defeat, the Dutchman was only half-fit, and came on for an out-of-place Mosquera only after the Spaniard had given away a penalty for a lunge on PSG's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Timber is defensively solid, rarely bypassed by opposition players and commits forward with overlaps, too, in the final third. When fully firing, he is arguably the best right back in the league, and was voted as such in the PFA Team of the Year last season.

The 25-year-old trained on Tuesday morning and is in the squad for Wednesday’s fixture against Napoli.

Timber’s return has been a long, arduous journey from a groin injury which had affected him since March. It ruled him out of the Netherlands’ World Cup squad before returning to light training sessions at the start of Arsenal’s pre-season in July.

If the Gunners can have Timber fully fit for the latter stages of the competition, that is a huge plus.

Sports.title: The summer signing giving Unai Emery an extra attacking dimension - and the new man he will be alarmed by: Club Brugge 2-3 Aston Villa
Sports.content:
A first win of the season, a first goal for Nicolas Jackson and the ideal start to Aston Villa's Champions League campaign – but we may not see the best of Unai Emery's men until after the international break at least.

Heading into this game, Villa had not scored since Brian Madjo's strike in the Super Cup defeat by Paris Saint-Germain nearly a month ago.

But they put that right here as John McGinn, Emi Buendia and Jackson all struck before half-time. Hugo Vetlessen equalised briefly for Club Brugge, who closed the gap in the second half thanks to Nicolo' Tresoldi's penalty.

Both sides missed chances in a chaotic match that would have made Emery desperately nervous. The Villa boss craves control and here Villa rarely had it.

Yet after losing six key players over the summer and making an unconvincing start to the Premier League, this may be the result Villa needed to get their season moving...

Suzuki finding top speed

First Emi Martinez, now Zion Suzuki. Aston Villa certainly love a goalkeeper with 'main character' energy and just like Martinez, Suzuki looks like he will draw the spotlight.

Aston Villa got their first win of the season, a first goal for Nicolas Jackson and the ideal start to the Champions League

Zion Suzuki's range of passing with either foot is remarkable and gives Villa an extra attacking dimension

Where Martinez made his name through his astounding saves and unsavoury antics, it is the kicking that sets Suzuki apart. The Japanese's range of passing with either foot is remarkable and gives Villa an extra attacking dimension.

The game was barely a minute old when Suzuki picked out Aaron Wan-Bissaka, who was on the right touchline halfway inside the Brugge half. Wan-Bissaka and McGinn combined to set up a chance for Buendia but the Argentine missed the target.

Suzuki's kicking will naturally push the opposition back, just as a batter will hit over the top in cricket in order to spread the field. It is great to watch.

There may be some teething problems at the other end, though, as Suzuki's shot-stopping and aerial ability is not quite as convincing. But the early signs are that the £30million have been spent well.

Defensive fragility

Pau Torres was the only member of last season's first choice back four who played here and Villa looked vulnerable, especially out wide.

MATCH FACTS AND PLAYER RATINGS Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 7.5; Wan-Bissaka 4.5 (Bogarde 68, 6), Lindelof 7, *TORRES 8*, Maatsen 5.5; J Gomes 6.5, Kamara 7.5 (Barkley 68, 6); McGinn 7, Buendia 7 (Alysson 68, 6), Hemmings 7; Jackson 6.5 (Abraham 81) Scorers: McGinn 11, Buendia 22, Jackson 44 Booked: Maatsen, McGinn, Gomes Manager: Unai Emery 6 Referee: Sandro Schaerer 6

Ezri Konsa, Matty Cash and Lucas Digne were ultra-reliable as Villa finished fourth and won the Europa League – but now Konsa is at Arsenal, Digne is at Paris Saint-Germain and Cash was left at home due to muscle discomfort.

Aaron Wan-Bissaka had a torrid time against Brugge's Spanish winger Jan Virgili and was brought off after 68 minutes. When Konsa was at Villa, he would slot in at right-back at times like these. Instead, Emery had to send on Lamare Bogarde – his fourth-choice central midfielder – to handle Virgili.

It usually takes time for new signings to find their rhythm under Emery. Morgan Rogers was the exception, but players like Digne, Youri Tielemans – now with Manchester United – and Buendia all had to work hard to earn his trust.

Still, Emery will have been a little alarmed by Wan-Bissaka's display. The former Manchester United man, on loan from West Ham, can expect plenty of time in the analysis room after this showing.

Unai Emery will have been a little alarmed by new signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka's display

Emi Buendia is living proof that no player is ever totally out of the picture under Emery at Villa

Never give up

Emi Buendia is living proof that no player is ever totally out of the picture under Emery at Villa.

The playmaker suffered a serious knee injury on the eve of the 2023-24 season and in the following campaign, he was loaned to Bayer Leverkusen in January.

In summer 2025, Buendia was so far out of the picture that he was even considered by Birmingham, who had just been promoted from League One.

But Buendia stayed, won back his place in the team and in May, he scored one of the goals of the season in the Europa League Final to help Villa lift their first major trophy since 1996.

He finished off an excellent move here to restore Villa's lead in the first half. The club have added significant attacking talent this summer, with Johan Manzambi and Ibrahim Mbaye arriving for more than £100million combined and Alejandro Garnacho joining on loan. All of them will have a tough job to squeeze Buendia out of the team.

Sports.title: 'Angry' Erling Haaland playfully scolds Man City's £85.7m teenage 'gem' Ayyoub Bouaddi for failing to pass to him
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland aimed a lighthearted dig at new Man City team-mate Ayyoub Bouaddi after Enzo Maresca's side beat Porto in their Champions League opener.

City won 2-0 at the Estadio do Dragao thanks to a second-half brace from Haaland in another positive result for their new-look team following a busy summer.

Along with Haaland, who was named as the Player of the Match, Bouaddi impressed on his first start for the club since his £85.7million move from Lille.

And when asked by Prime Video for his thoughts on his new team-mate's performance, Haaland was full of praise for the 18-year-old.

'I think he did a really, really good game,' he said. 'The last couple of weeks in training... I just told the chairman (Khaldoon Al Mubarak) he's been amazing in training and everything, so I think we've got a gem there.'

Haaland then joked: 'To be honest, I think he should have played me in, in the second half.

Erling Haaland reacts to Man City's win in Porto 🗣️



Still a few bits to learn for new signing Ayyoub Bouaddi 😅 pic.twitter.com/bbAeD1y905 — Prime Video Sport UK (@primevideosport) September 8, 2026

Erling Haaland aimed a lighthearted dig at Ayyoub Bouaddi after Man City beat Porto 2-0

Bouaddi, an £85.7m summer arrival from Lille, was impressive on his first start for the club

'I was all alone, so I was a bit angry. I will tell him right now, but he played a good game, except for that pass.'

Haaland smirked as he finished that sentence, before he was pressed on whether his new boss Maresca would be happy with his side's performance and where they could improve.

'We have to learn,' Haaland added. 'Enzo has to demand a lot from us. We have to demand a lot from each other.

'We have to win games because in Man City you have to win games, you have to win trophies. That's what we have to do with this club.

'I hope (he will be pleased). We won away in a difficult game. Look at this atmosphere, it was unreal at times, so I hope he is happy.'

Maresca, who was an assistant coach to Pep Guardiola during City's Treble-winning season, has now won four of his first five games in the hotseat since replacing his former boss.

And, when pressed after the game, he shared similar thoughts on Bouaddi's impressive display.

Enzo Maresca (left) was similarly full of praise for the 18-year-old Moroccan international

'Oh my God! Bouaddi was very good,’ Maresca said. ‘Against Coventry he lost two balls and after that he was inside our box, calm.

'This shows how good he is because any player, after you miss two passes, can panic.

‘You don’t expect it a guy who’s 18 to manage this game and he was top. I didn’t see him in any moment panic. This is the reason why he is here with us.’

City return to action on Sunday when they travel to Old Trafford to face Manchester United in the first Manchester derby of the season.

Sports.title: Borussia Dortmund star rushed to hospital after slumping to the pitch with 'circulatory problems' during Champions League tie
Sports.content:
Borussia Dortmund have stated teenage star Konstantinos Karetsas is 'doing well under the circumstances' after being taken to hospital with circulatory problems. Karetsas, 18, had to be substituted 27 minutes into their Champions League tie against Villarreal on Tuesday night. The Greek attacker was seen kicking the ball back to his team-mate before sitting down on the pitch in discomfort. Dortmund medical staff entered the pitch to attend to Karetsas, who could then be seen lying on the pitch. Karetsas was ultimately stretchered off the field of play, with Dortmund later confirming he was suffering from 'circulation problems'. 'Konstantinos Karetsas had to leave the pitch in the game against Villarreal due to circulation problems,' a club statement read. Konstantinos Karetsas slumped to the pitch during Dortmund's Champions League tie with Villarreal The teenager was taken to hospital with Dortmund stating he was suffering from 'circulation problems' 'Kosta is doing as well as can be expected given the circumstances, and he is on his way to the hospital for further examinations.' German newspaper Bild reported that Karetsas had missed training on Monday due to fatigue. Karetsas joined Dortmund last month in a £27million move from Belgian side Genk in the summer. The teenager's fellow Greek Giannis Konstantelias had joined for a similar fee earlier in the window, but suffered an ACL injury on his debut in a major blow to Dortmund. That injury led to Dortmund loaning in Ethan Nwaneri from Arsenal. Nwaneri came off the bench in place of Karetsas on Tuesday as Dortmund began their Champions League campaign with a victory. Serhou Guirassy scored twice and also put through his own net in a 3-2 win by the Bundesliga side. A Renato Veiga own goal had put Dortmund ahead before Santiago Mourino levelled for Villarreal. Guirassy netted twice in the closing ten minutes to earn a victory, before an injury time own goal.

Sports.title: Gabriel Jesus reveals he was made to train away from his Arsenal team-mates before sealing cut-price £8.6m move to Barcelona
Sports.content:
Gabriel Jesus reveals he was made to train away from his Arsenal team-mates before sealing cut-price £8.6m move to Barcelona

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Gabriel Jesus has aimed a parting shot at Arsenal after revealing he was forced to train away from his team-mates before securing a move to Barcelona.

The Brazilian forward was left out of the Arsenal squad for their first two games of the season, with the expectation he would leave the club.

Jesus ultimately sealed a cut-price £8.6million move to Spanish giants Barcelona on deadline day, ending his four-year spell with the Gunners.

Speaking to SportyTV, Jesus has admitted his final days at the club were spent training away from his Arsenal team-mates, which he claimed had been an abrupt decision.

'The truth is I was training, I did all the pre-season training with Arsenal normal and then obviously I knew already that probably I will not play there or get some opportunity,' Jesus said.

'But no-one told me nothing.

Gabriel Jesus has revealed he was forced to train away from his Arsenal team-mates in his final days at the club

Jesus' four-year spell at Arsenal came to a close earlier this month when he joined Barcelona

'I'm a professional you know and then obviously I was training with the group and then from nothing they put me to train away from the group.

'I was training and doing my maximum to be ready if I have the chance to play in a high level again and then obviously in the last week it was very quick.

'The work with Deco, and the president of the club, and my agent was amazing. In one day, it was sure that I would have the opportunity to come (to Barcelona). I said yes, straight away, no matter what and I am so happy to be here.'

Jesus had been involved in all four of Arsenal's official pre-season matches in the build-up to his departure, albeit having limited game time in each.

The forward had initially joined the Gunners in 2022 after five years at Manchester City but largely played a bit-part role under Mikel Arteta.

Jesus had missed most of 2025 with a cruciate ligament tear, but was part of the Gunners squad that eventually ended the club's long wait for a Premier League title.

The forward made 123 appearances for the Gunners in total, scoring 32 goals and providing 22 assists.

Arteta had lauded Jesus's contribution to Arsenal after his departure to Barcelona was confirmed.

Jesus made his Barcelona debut on Sunday after his cut-price move to the Spanish giants

'He was a massive contributor for us to change the dynamic and the energy in and around this club,' the Arsenal boss said earlier this month.

'I think when Gabi came in he brought this energy, this belief within, this aura, that's really helped achieve what happened next.

'And now, yeah, he has an amazing opportunity to enjoy one of the biggest clubs in the world, and a beautiful place to live as well, and we are happy for him.'

Jesus made his Barcelona debut on Sunday, playing the final ten minutes of their 5-0 win over Valencia in LaLiga.

Sports.title: Dogged Man City banish ghosts of the Dragao as Erling Haaland brace sees off stubborn Porto in ill-tempered 2-0 win after security had to 'separate' players in tunnel brawl - JACK GAUGHAN
Sports.content:
Dogged Man City banish ghosts of the Dragao as Erling Haaland brace sees off stubborn Porto in ill-tempered 2-0 win after security had to 'separate' players in tunnel brawl - JACK GAUGHAN

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Ghosts of the Dragao were whispering. Whispering about holding midfielders and overthinks, whispering about Kai Havertz and gaping defences, whispering about throwing away matches that Manchester City had dominated.

The circumstances around the 2021 Champions League final in this very stadium still haunt those of a City persuasion but not the squad. How can they? Only Phil Foden and Ruben Dias are left from that defeat by Chelsa, a Covid final in front of half a ground and when travelling City supporters were drowsy from the drink in the baking sun down by the River Douro. Drowsier still after the performance.

Past glories and past failures cannot be on Enzo Maresca's agenda, carving a fresh team with a tweaked identity, although starting a teenager in Ayyoub Bouaddi instead of the more seasoned Elliot Anderson could easily have ended as a nod to Pep Guardiola's infamous decision to not operate with a conventional No 6 against Thomas Tuchel's Chelsea.

As it was, Bouaddi excelled, City making sure this continental campaign started positively through Erling Haaland's double on a tempestuous night that saw reserve goalkeeper Marcus Bettinelli allegedly pushed by home officials in the tunnel at half-time, sparking a brief brawl, with Dias having nudged Porto boss Francesco Farioli.

City had authority when it mattered, wasting a glut of chances before doing enough in the sort of feverish atmosphere where away fans simply could not be heard and one that could have seen a young team wilt.

It is four victories from four to start the Maresca reign. They search for complete performances that will doubtless come with more time. Winning while learning is no bad thing at all, with the style becoming more distinctive.

Erling Haaland scored twice as Manchester City overcame Porto 2-0 in the Champions League

Haaland proved the difference between the sides in a bad-tempered tie at the Dragao

The match saw multiple clashes between the sides with tempers flaring during the tie

So insistent on penning Porto in, Matheus Nunes spent much of his evening pressing on the edge of the opposition's box. That is all perfectly understandable until realising that he was the right back. At one point from a free kick on halfway, Maresca appeared to be asking Nunes to leave his station and push forward, making sure Marc Guehi came over to cover.

They went man-to-man constantly, Bouaddi asked to fill in as Nunes galivanted. It's high risk and high reward. If nothing else, this new City team will not die wondering.

Given the bounty of opportunities that were fashioned before half time, Maresca will rightly believe that this alteration to the set club style has started very nicely indeed. Three times Haaland found himself guilty of missing big chances.

A truly confident Foden in full flight would have netted another, created by Rayan Cherki, with the Frenchman also coming up against an inspired Diogo Costa.

This method of playing spins on an axis. Mostly that will be anchored by Anderson, whose first weeks in City blue have drawn copious praise, yet Bouaddi's introduction – a full debut – points to how Maresca may want to manage this squad.

In coming from Lille for £85million, Bouaddi was not cheap. His talent is unquestioned. He's played in the Champions League before and dazzled for Morocco at the World Cup. Yet despite all that pedigree, he is still only 18 and to be thrown in shows a degree of faith not always obvious at the very highest level.

His positional understanding looked smart enough for the demands placed upon a sitting midfielder with a right back acting as a forward. His ability in tight spaces is well suited to City, that is obvious, but the breaking up of play and turning Porto around was something perhaps more surprising.

One bit of screening and stopping Pepe from darting towards goal when City were out of position felt mature beyond his years.

'Oh my God, Bouaddi was very good,' Maresca said. 'Against Coventry he lost two balls and after that he was inside our box, calm. This shows how good he is because any player, after you miss two passes, can panic.

'You don't expect it a guy who's 18 to manage this game and he was top. I didn't see him in any moment panic. This is the reason why he is here with us.'

Maturity was generally in short supply elsewhere, with tensions high and both teams embroiled in a flashpoint at the break. Guehi had clattered into Gabriel Viega and Porto raged for the harshest punishment.

Ayyoub Bouaddi started in midfield for Enzo Maresca's side and the teenager excelled

Marc Guehi was involved in a clash with Gabriel Veiga on the stroke of half-time in the match

Porto had raged over the incident leading to both players clashing in the tunnel at the break

It continued after Szymon Marciniak blew for half time, tempers on the pitch (Enzo Fernandez close to the scene, of course) and with the temporary tunnel shaking as both sets of players went to their dressing rooms as a skirmish ensued. Eyewitnesses claimed that security had to separate players and Marciniak unusually intervened.

Porto wanted some of that needle and attempted to unsettle City, although didn't truly worry Gianluigi Donnarumma until Alberto Costa's headed wide from a corner.

'How many times you see me or my bench stand up?' Maresca asked. 'Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times you see their bench? We know in this kind of game when you come here it's always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, I think we dealt it very well.'

Porto were already a goal down by the Costa chance, City ahead 94 seconds after the restart. Haaland finally produced when asked, bundling a header in.

It owed much to the expanse of Maresca's midfield, working possession from right to left until Cherki found Fernandez and Haaland obliged from the Argentine's cross.

There was later something in this for the hosts, though. Porto crept forward, trying to force mistakes, and City reverted to a doggedness that even the best need, before Haaland stroked home a second in stoppage time, a 167th in blue and becoming the club's third highest goalscorer ever in his inevitable surge towards history.

Sports.title: Ryan Giggs reveals how Elliot Anderson told him to 'leave me alone' on golf course as he tried to convince England star to snub Man City - and the Man United player Pep Guardiola rated highest
Sports.content:
Ryan Giggs has revealed Elliot Anderson told him 'leave me alone' after the Manchester United legend attempted to convince him to join the club this summer.

Daily Mail Sport reported last year that Anderson had been Man United's top midfield target for the summer transfer window, but had trailed rivals Man City in the race.

Man City would ultimately land Anderson for £116million in the summer, with Man United going on to sign Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos in their midfield overhaul.

Ahead of Anderson featuring in a first Manchester derby at the weekend, Giggs revealed on Rio Ferdinand Presents: The Debrief that he had attempted to convince the England star to snub Man City's advances.

Giggs explained he had bumped into Anderson on the golf course on holiday, just ahead of the World Cup.

'It was literally a few days before he went to the World Cup. I peppered him,' Giggs told Ferdinand.

Ryan Giggs has claimed he tried to convince Elliot Anderson to snub Man City and join Man United

Giggs said Anderson, who later joined Man City for £116m, told him to 'leave me alone' as he tried to convince him to sign for the Red Devils

'He didn’t know how to take it at first, and then he relaxed a little bit.

'But for the first four or five holes, we were literally crossing. And at the end of it, he went, "will you just let me, leave me alone. Will you just let me play my golf, please? You’re in trouble."'

Ferdinand added: 'That’s what I do when I see some players. I don’t care.

'You’ve got to try all sorts to get these deals over. It’s mad, though. Obviously, the price tag was crazy. And it’s just like astronomical money. And Man United ain’t got the budget to pay for that.'

Giggs, who made a club record 963 appearances and later had a spell on Man United's coaching staff, also offered his thoughts on Marcus Rashford after his return to the club.

He claimed former Man City boss Pep Guardiola had once claimed at a dinner, which included Sir Alex Ferguson, he believed Rashford was Man United's 'best player' and would 'take him tomorrow'.

'There’s about eight of us, so he [Ferguson] sat me next to Pep, this was about, I’m going to say about eight or nine years ago.

'I’ve gone to Pep and says, "you know, who do you like at United?", "He went, well, who do you think?"

Giggs claimed at a dinner Pep Guardiola had once claimed Marcus Rashford was the one player he would take from Man United

'So I went, De Gea? He went, no. Luke Shaw? I was just like, no. He said the best player at Man United, Marcus Rashford. I would take him tomorrow.

'And that just made me [think], what’s he seeing Pep? And that was obviously as a centre forward.'

Giggs also added that during his spell as Man United's assistant manager in 2015, he had been approached by a French supporter of the club who urged him to sign a young Kylian Mbappe from Monaco.

He stated that the fan recommended Mbappe after watching a lot of youth football in France, and later emailed details to Giggs to convince him to scout the young forward.

Mbappe had made his first forays into first team football that season with Monaco, making 14 senior appearances for the Ligue 1 side during the 2015-16 campaign.

'Me and Albert [Stuivenberg], who’s the coach with Arsenal, he was another assistant at United at the time, we used to in the afternoons just go and watch games or go and watch players at the training ground,' Giggs said.

'I’ve told him about this thing, he says, "come on, let’s get him up." And we got a few youth games with Monaco and we seen him and just like, "wow, what is this?"

'You know, you can see players and they can be special, but he did look exceptional, obviously.

'We told the scouting team, they went to watch him. Someone in France went to watch him and he was actually playing PSG. Monaco were playing PSG.

Giggs claimed in 2015 he had been approached by a Man United fan telling them to scout then Monaco teenager Kylian Mbappe

'They went to Paris to watch him. Anyway, I think a few weeks later, I said to this guy, how did it go? He went, yeah, they weren’t too sure about him, so we just left it, and that was it.'

Mbappe had played 81 minutes against PSG in a 2-0 win in the March of the 2015-16 season, when the forward was just 17.

He would later sign for PSG for a £165million fee in August 2017 and went on to score 256 goals in 308 games for the French giants and won six league titles.

Mbappe, who joined Real Madrid on a free transfer in 2024, played a key role in France's World Cup win in 2018 and is now the tournament's all-time record scorer.

Sports.title: Arsenal caught up in UK airport travel chaos: Gunners forced to cancel Mikel Arteta's Champions League press conference in Naples with flights grounded by air traffic control 'technical failure'
Sports.content:
Arsenal caught up in UK airport travel chaos: Gunners forced to cancel Mikel Arteta's Champions League press conference in Naples with flights grounded by air traffic control 'technical failure'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Arsenal's preparations for their Champions League tie against Napoli were disrupted after they were caught up in the travel chaos engulfing UK airports.

The Gunners are back in European action on Wednesday when they face the Italian side in Naples.

However, Mikel Arteta's pre-match press conference on Tuesday night had to be cancelled after Arsenal's flight to Italy was delayed.

That was because of the air traffic control issues in the UK, with planes at most major UK airports grounded on Tuesday following a 'technical failure'.

The problem has seen almost 300 flights from the UK cancelled, impacting thousands of holidaymakers along with the Premier League champions.

Arsenal's squad are now not set to arrive in Naples until 9.30PM local time.

Arsenal's preparations for their Champions League tie against Napoli were disrupted after they were caught up in the travel chaos engulfing UK airports

Hundreds of flights were cancelled after an air traffic control 'technical failure'

It was reported that they remained at the club's London Colney-based training ground while they were waiting for the issue to be resolved, before travelling to the airport later on when their new flight time was announced.

At around 6.30PM, Arsenal then shared a video on their X account of the squad boarding a plane.

In an update on Tuesday afternoon, National Air Traffic Services (NATS) said it had identified an issue with its 'flight processing system', adding that 'recovery will take some time', but said it had 'implemented a fix'.

The organisation, which provides air traffic control services to 15 UK airports, gave no details as to the cause of the problem.

But a spokesperson told the Daily Mail there is currently no indication the issue is due to a hack or other cyber incident.

In more positive news for the Gunners, Jurrien Timber is set to be included in their squad for the match.

The Dutch defender last featured off the bench in the Champions League final against PSG in May.

However, that was his first appearance in more than two months and he subsequently missed the World Cup through injury.

Speaking ahead of their Premier League tie against Chelsea on Sunday, Arteta had provided a positive update on Timber and hinted that a return was not too far away.

'Jurrien is in really good condition at the moment, he’s been a few weeks on the pitch and has been training with us, so he’s in a really good place,' Arteta said.

'We will decide [on his involvement on Sunday] after training [on Saturday].'

Arsenal defender Jurrien Timber is set to be in their squad following a lengthy injury lay-off

Napoli have three points from three league games so far this season and their squad includes former Premier League stars such as Kevin De Bruyne, Rasmus Hojlund and Billy Gilmour.

Former Man United man Scott McTominay will miss out though, after recently undergoing corrective heart surgery.

In a statement released earlier this month, Napoli had said: 'Following the onset of a mild benign arrhythmia, Scott McTominay will undergo corrective surgery using a cardiac arrhythmia ablation (PFA) in the coming days.

'He will be available again after the international break.'

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola snub confirmed as Reds star makes 'very sad' confession
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Bradley Barcola snub confirmed as Reds star makes 'very sad' confession

Contract talks have dominated discussions ahead of Liverpool's Champions League campaign kicking off

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola is in line to make his Champions League debut for Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola's first Champions League adventure begins with Liverpool hosting Atletico Madrid. The Reds boss welcomes Diego Simeone's side on Wednesday night in a repeat of last year's fixture at Anfield, which the home side came out on top in a 3-2 victory.

‌



The Spaniard will certainly hope history will repeat itself in what is expected to be a cauldron of noise as the Reds kick off their European campaign. The Premier League side are coming off their first win of the season after defeating Ipswich Town 2-0, courtesy of Alexander Isak's brace.

‌



Bradley Barcola made his debut at Portman Road after his £123million move was confirmed from Paris Saint-Germain. The Frenchman has since been dealt a blow, while Iraola has been hit with one of his star players opening up about their future.

‌



Barcola snubbed

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola wasn't included among the 30 nominees for the Ballon d'Or (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

The France international was not among the 30 players nominated for the Ballon d'Or. The list was released on Tuesday, with Barcola's absence ranking among the biggest surprises, alongside his former PSG team-mate, Desire Doue.

The Champions League holders had a remarkable 10 players on the list, including summer signing Ferran Torres. Barcola, 24, enjoyed a fruitful last season in France, scoring 13 goals and contributing 7 assists in 49 games across all competitions.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool's disappointing defence of their Premier League title last season, while going trophy-less, meant that the club was not represented among the nominees.

Mac Allister 'sad'

View 3 Images Alexis Mac Allister aired his grievances over his contract situation (Image: getty)

‌



Alexis Mac Allister was the player who joined Iraola in Tuesday's pre-match press conference and the midfielder stunningly revealed he had options to leave the club in the summer while also admitting he was 'very sad' about the fact he has not been offered a new contract.

He said: "There was a chance (I could leave), of course, as everyone knows. I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract, which makes me very, very sad because everyone can see I give 100 per cent for this football club every single day in training. I always give my best."

Sports.title: Lionel Messi splashes out on second football club as 'full takeover agreement reached'
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi splashes out on second football club as 'full takeover agreement reached'

Lionel Messi could become the owner of another football club with a deal reportedly on the verge of being announced

View 2 Images Lionel Messi could be about to complete a full takeover of another club (Image: Megan Briggs/Getty Images)

Lionel Messi has reportedly agreed to complete a full takeover of a Spanish second division club, just over a week after announcing his retirement from international football. Messi, 39, is currently in the middle of his fourth season in Major League Soccer with Inter Miami, and already appears to have an eye on the future.

‌



The Barcelona legend helped Argentina reach the final of the World Cup in the summer, before his country suffered a 1-0 defeat to Spain in the showpiece match in New Jersey.

‌



Messi signed a new contract with Miami earlier this year that will run until the end of the 2028 MLS season, at which point the former Paris Saint-Germain will be 41 years old.

‌



A fresh report from Spain, meanwhile, has claimed that Messi is now venturing further into the world of club ownership, with a deal appearing to be close to completion to oversee a full takeover.

Diego Simeone makes honest Julian Alvarez admission ahead of Liverpool clash READ MORE :

Spanish publication AS has claimed that Messi is on the verge of acquiring a 100 per cent stake in La Liga 2 club CD Eldense, who are currently sat in the relegation zone.

It has been reported that an agreement has been reached for Messi to become the majority owner of the Spanish second-tier club, with his lawyers said to be holding talks with TH, a Colombian investment group.

‌



The report goes on to claim that an official announcement confirming the full takeover from Messi could happen within the next few days.

Should a deal get over the line, it would be the second club under Messi’s ownership, with the other being Cornella, which plays in the fifth tier of Spanish football.

It was just last month that Messi announced his retirement from international football, with his final match for Argentina being the defeat to Spain in the World Cup final in July.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Messi announced his retirement just a few weeks after his father, Jorge, passed away, and posted an emotional message confirming his plan to no longer represent his country.

"After all this time that has passed since the final, and after much thought, I want to announce to everyone that I am retiring from the National Team,” Messi posted on Instagram.”It was a decision that hurt, and still hurts, to my core, but I understand that it's the right time.

‌



"I swear that I always gave my all, not just in the last few years when we won everything, but before that too. I always fought and gave everything for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you proud to be Argentinian through football.

"There's not much time left, and chapters are closing, and this is one that hurts me deeply. I love, loved, and will always love being on the National Team. I've given everything I have; I have nothing more to give, and besides, there are some great young players coming up behind me who deserve to be there.

View 2 Images Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international football last month (Image: Leonardo Fernandez/Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"Thank you for all the love and support over these 20 years. I'm going to miss hearing you all from the inside so much. Now I'm going to be just one of you, cheering and supporting you from the sidelines (in good times and bad, even more so).

"Thank you to my family for always being there, for accompanying me on this beautiful but difficult journey. Thank you to each and every one of the coaches, teammates, and managers I had the privilege of working with. I take with me unforgettable memories and moments.”

‌



Messi continued: "I leave with the peace and pride of having given you, along with my teammates, dreamlike moments. It was incredible to have experienced it with you all. I love you!

"Thank you, God, for making me Argentinian. Go Argentina! I wrote these words on July 21st, two days after the final. Today, after what happened to my dad, I'm even more convinced than before."

Sports.title: Borussia Dortmund star, 18, rushed to hospital after being carried off in Champions League game
Sports.content:
Borussia Dortmund star, 18, rushed to hospital after being carried off in Champions League game

Borussia Dortmund have released a statement after one of their players had to be stretchered off the field and sent immediately to the hospital from their Champions League clash

View 2 Images Konstantinos Karetsas receives medical treatment (Image: Alex Gottschalk/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images)

Borussia Dortmund star Konstantinos Karetsas has been taken straight to the hospital after being stretchered off the field in their Champions League clash against Villarreal. The Bundesliga side have revealed that Karestsas suffered a 'circulation problem'.

‌



The Greece international, 18, went down without a challenge from the opposition, sitting down on the turf. He raised his arm to call for treatment, having moments before dribbled and played a pass with no problem.

‌



Karetsas, who joined Dortmund from Genk in the summer, was making his fifth appearance for the club. The shocking scenes will have caused plenty of alarm, but the German club have indicated he is doing as well as can be expected.

‌



Dortmund said in a statement: "Konstantinos Karetsas had to leave the pitch in the game against Villarreal due to circulation problems. Kosta is doing as well as can be expected given the circumstances, and he is on his way to the hospital for further examinations."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

There was consternation on the sidelines, with former Dortmund ace Mats Hummels, working as a pundit on Prime Video, highlighting his concern.

‌



"When the doctors did not look at his legs at all and were only focused on his upper body, it sent a shiver down my spine," he said. "We would not wish something like that on anyone. Those are really horrible scenes we had to see there."

Karetsas was replaced by Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri with just 27 minutes played in Dortmund. They were able to overcome their concern to take the lead against the Yellow Submarine after half-time as Renato Veiga turned the ball into his own net.

View 2 Images Konstantinos Karetsas received treatment on the pitch (Image: Christof Koepsel/Getty Images)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Villarreal got on level terms after 66 minutes when Santiago Mourino got on the scoresheet. But Dortmund were able to make their pressure tell as Serhou Guirassy scored in the 80th minute to restore their advantage, and the same player scored from the penalty spot five minutes later to give the home side an unassailable lead.

Dortmund did receive a scare when Guirassy knocked the ball into his own goal in the 93rd minute. The Bundesliga team were able to hang on to earn three points.

Article continues below

There were also surprising scenes at the Westfalenstadion, with only 39 Villarreal fans turning up to enter the away section for the Champions League match. Dortmund had to close a 4,000-seat section due to the short notice when they learned of the situation.

Sports.title: Why Borussia Dortmund stand is empty for Champions League as team fail to sell tickets
Sports.content:
Why Borussia Dortmund stand is empty for Champions League as team fail to sell tickets

Borussia Dortmund will face Villarreal in the Champions League but will potentially have one area of the stadium empty

View 2 Images Borussia Dortmund will host Villarreal in the Champions League at Signal Iduna Park (Image: Christof Koepsel/Getty Images)

Borussia Dortmund’s match against Villarreal in the Champions League will have a noticeably empty section in the stadium this week. Dortmund and Villarreal will go head-to-head in each of the club’s first European matches of the season, with the fixture taking place at Signal Iduna Park.

However, one section of the famous stadium will have zero supporters watching from the stands, with Villarreal not filling their full allocation for away supporters.

Champions League rules allow away teams to have 5% of the overall capacity of a stadium available for travelling fans.

Dortmund’s home stadium has an overall capacity of around 81,000, meaning that Villarreal would have been entitled to just over 4,000 of their fans to watch the match inside the famous venue.

However, a report in Sport Bild has claimed that Villarreal has informed Dortmund that they will not fill their full allocation for the fixture.

It has been claimed that the Spanish club have sold just 39 tickets for away fans to watch the game in Germany, and as a result, has been given back to Dortmund for home fans.

The report further claims that, after being informed of Villarreal’s ticket sale numbers, Dortmund have decided to accommodate those fans in the West Stand, instead of the North East corner, which is typically reserved for away supporters. That will leave an entire section of the ground empty.

Dortmund boss Niko Kovac was quick to emphasise the difficulty of the match ahead for his team as they prepare to face a Villarreal side that finished third in La Liga last season.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

"They finished third last year and are playing in the Champions League for the second year in a row," Kovac told said, via Dortmund's club website.

"Normally, the top three spots in Spain are locked up. If you break into that group (alongside Barcelona, Real Madrid, and Atletico Madrid) that really says something!"

Kovac added: "They have a new coach now, but they continue to play the Spanish style with a lot of possession.

View 2 Images Borussia Dortmund manager Niko Kovac has spoke about the match with Villarreal (Image: Alexandre Simoes/Borussia Dortmund via Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"They're technically very sound and very precise in their execution. When they have the ball, this team makes very few mistakes.

"We'll have to make sure we reduce their time in possession. When we have the ball, they can't play their game and have to defend more, which will hopefully work in our favour. It's going to be a very difficult game."
