Se localizó infraestructura eléctrica, internet satelital y equipos especializados en generación de activos… pic.twitter.com/lfgKk3pY3s — Secretaría de Seguridad Pública (@SSPGobPue) September 6, 2026

During the operation, authorities uncovered a highly equipped digital operations center. Agents seized large-scale electrical and technological infrastructure that included transformers, medium-voltage terminals, 300 specialized computer units (GPUs) and operational satellite internet antennas.

The initial criminal charge being prepared is energy theft, but prosecutors say money laundering charges have not been ruled out. Forensic accountants are tracing the origin of the funds used to acquire the expensive technological hardware.

State authorities have confirmed that investigators have expanded their search to neighboring municipalities in anticipation of similar operations.

Puebla Security Minister Francisco Sánchez said the “farms” are part of a network that takes advantage of the proximity to hydroelectric facilities in the Sierra Norte to steal massive volumes of energy.

Cryptomining consumes a significant amount of energy and produces a lot of noise, Sánchez said, so remote and isolated locations away from communities are favored.

“We have been monitoring this … area of ​​the state, especially due to its proximity to the [Nuevo Necaxa] dam,” he said, adding that the discovery of a large-scale power line connection helped the authorities locate the clandestine farm.

Last year, officials busted a crypto farm in the small Puebla community near the dam where properties owned by the Electrical Workers Union were allegedly being used to operate mining facilities powered by illegal connections to the Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) power grid.

Two other mining operations straddling the border between Puebla and Tlaxcala were also dismantled in 2025.

Cryptocurrency mining — which is not illegal in Mexico, although cryptocurrencies are not legal tender here — is a process that uses computers to solve complex mathematical operations in order to validate transactions and earn rewards in digital assets.

In its latest report on non-technical losses covering the period from January to July 2024, the CFE estimated that energy theft, meter tampering and illegal connections cost the company approximately 13.8 billion pesos (US $817 million).

Cryptocurrencies are increasingly being used to move funds between financial users and countries quickly, cheaply and discreetly, such that they have become a popular money-laundering tool for criminal groups.

With reports from El País, Xataka México, Debate and La Jornada de Oriente

World.title: MND Local: Pro tennis and golf face uncertainty in Los Cabos
World.content:
Money trumps tradition in professional sports, at least where the Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) is concerned. That was the takeaway from the recent report by Spanish-language tennis journalist Iván Aguilar that the ATP 500 Series event in Acapulco (Abierto Mexicano Telcel) will go away in 2028 to make way for a new Masters 1000 Series event in Saudi Arabia.

Acapulco has been a mainstay on the ATP Tour since 2001, hosting the most consequential tennis tournament in Mexico and a marquee event in Latin America. The long-running competition has always drawn top-tier talent. Legendary Spanish player Rafael Nadal, for example, was a four-time champion at the Mexican Open in Acapulco. So its loss to the tour, if confirmed by the ATP, will be deeply felt.

🚨🚨🚨ACAPULCO Y LOS CABOS FUERA DEL CALENDARIO ATP🚨🚨🚨 ¡Mexico se quedará sin torneos ATP para 2028! Los árabes han comprado la licencia del Abierto Mexicano de Tenis. El Abierto de Los Cabos pasará a ser un Challenger 175 para jugarse en el primer trimestre del 2028 pic.twitter.com/TN8JLRAAPx — Iván Aguilar (@ivabianconero) September 2, 2026

Los Cabos will also be affected by the schedule changes, Aguilar noted, as the Los Cabos Tennis Open (Mifel Tennis Open by Telcel Oppo, in sponsor-speak), which recently celebrated its 10th anniversary, will be downgraded from an ATP 250 Series event to a Challenger 175 tournament in 2028, with a shift in its calendar placement also in the works.

This news, combined with recent announcements by the Professional Golfers’ Association (PGA) Tour, which is in the process of a major reworking of its own schedule, ensures that two of the three biggest annual sporting events in Los Cabos — Bisbee’s Black and Blue, the world’s biggest fishing tournament, is the other — will undergo significant changes in coming years.

The Saudi money driving ATP changes

The ATP’s calendar shakeup is being driven by Saudi Arabia’s US $900 billion Public Investment Fund (PIF), and by its dedicated sports arm, SURJ Sports Investment. According to The New York Times’ sports arm, The Athletic, SURJ has spent hundreds of millions of dollars buying back tournament licenses to clear a space on the calendar for a 10th Masters 1000 tournament, a 56-player draw likely to take place in Riyadh beginning in February 2028 with an estimated US $6 million prize pool. This is part of a massive overall investment by Saudi Arabia in the ATP Tour.

Among the licenses SURJ purchased to retire or relocate as part of the ATP’s “calendar optimization” program are those from the Chengdu Open, Hong Kong Open, Moselle Open, and the dormant Kremlin Cup. The Athletic reported in March that negotiations were also ongoing to acquire the licenses of tournaments in Acapulco and Buenos Aires. Aguilar’s subsequent reporting suggests the negotiations to acquire the license for the Mexican Open in Acapulco are complete.

Changes to the tennis tournament in Los Cabos

The loss of the Mexican Open and the demotion of the Los Cabos Tennis Open from an ATP-sponsored event to a second-tier Challenger 175 tournament amounts to a gutting of ATP events in Mexico. No top-tier ATP-sponsored events are expected to remain in the country by 2028. Los Cabos keeps its professional tournament, albeit with weaker fields — top-10 players have regularly appeared at the event during its decade-long history, but will likely become a thing of the past — and a fraction of the prize money.

The tournament will also move from its traditional late July calendar slot to sometime during the first few months of 2028. The 2027 editions of the Mexican Open and Los Cabos Tennis Open, meanwhile, have been confirmed, so there is at least one more opportunity for spectators to enjoy each of these events in their current form.

How the PGA’s new schedule affects Los Cabos

Just like in professional tennis, the other major North American individual sport, golf, is looking at major changes as it prepares to make its most significant structural overhaul in decades. Beginning in 2028, the PGA Tour will split into two tiers: a Championship Series and a Challenger Series. As a consequence of this update, the FedExCup Fall Series, of which the World Wide Technology Championship (WWTC) at Tiger Woods’ El Cardonal course at Diamante in Cabo San Lucas has been a part, will no longer exist.

Saudi investment has also played a role in the history of this tournament. For its first 16 editions, the WWTC was held at the Greg Norman-designed El Camaleón Mayakoba Golf Course on the Riviera Maya. However, when Norman became CEO of the Saudi Arabia-backed LIV Golf Tour, the PGA moved the tournament to Los Cabos in 2023. Diamante, the upscale resort and residential community that is home to several Tiger Woods-designed courses, became its new site, with the Woods-designed The Legacy Club talked about as the future location of the WWTC after its opening in 2027.

An uncertain future

But that future is now up in the air following the PGA Tour’s calendar shakeup. The WWTC, notably, only has a contract with the PGA Tour through 2027. Nor does it necessarily fit neatly into either of the new series tracks premiering in 2028. Although the WWTC has drawn top tour pros to compete for its distinctive El Arco-inspired trophy — Ben Griffin was in the world’s top 10 when he won the tournament last year — FedExCup Fall events are not high-profile enough to be slotted into the new Championship Series.

The Challenger Series is a possible landing spot — despite the international locale — and the Tiger Woods connection certainly helps, since the calendar restructuring was approved by the Woods-chaired Future Competition Committee.

But uncertainty remains … both for the WWTC and the only other PGA-sponsored event in Mexico, the VidantaWorld Mexico Open in Nuevo Nayarit. This year, the two are back-to-back on the schedule, with the VidantaWorld Mexico Open slated for Oct. 29 to Nov. 1, and the WWTC for Nov. 5 to 8.

Chris Sands is a writer and editor for Mexico News Daily, and the former Cabo San Lucas local expert for the USA Today travel website 10 Best and writer of Fodor’s Los Cabos travel guidebook. He has also contributed to numerous other websites and publications, including The San Diego Union-Tribune, Marriott Bonvoy Traveler, Forbes Travel Guide, Porthole Cruise and Travel, and Cabo Living.

World.title: US, Mexico carry out ‘High Eagle’ operation to ground cartel drones along border
World.content:
Mexico and the United States are currently carrying out an anti-drone operation at the border between Baja California and California, according to the Mexican Ministry of National Defense (Defensa).

Criminal groups use drones near the Mexico-U.S. border to assist their illicit activities, including the smuggling of people and drugs into the United States.

In a statement issued on Monday, Defensa said that the Águila Alta (High Eagle) “binational anti-drone operation” is taking place in the border region between Tijuana, Baja California, and San Diego, California.

The ministry said that the Aug. 31-Sept. 21 operation is occurring “within the framework of the Mexico-United States Bilateral Implementation Group” — a security group established a year ago — and that it is related to “concurrent (mirror) operations that the Armed Forces of both countries and U.S. law enforcement agencies are carrying out through simultaneous reconnaissance along the common border.”

Defensa said that the aim of the operation is to have a “safer border through the detection and disablement of commercial drones that are used by criminals at the common border to watch authorities during the trafficking of people and drugs.”

It didn’t say how many drones had been detected and disabled during the ongoing operation.

The Defense Ministry, led by General Ricardo Trevilla Trejo, said that the operation — described as “similar” to one that took place at the border between Ciudad Juárez and El Paso in March — consists of two stages, the first of which has already been completed.

It said that stage 1 took place from Aug. 31 to Sept. 2 in Tijuana and San Diego. During the stage, “a coordination exercise addressing drone issues was conducted, culminating in simultaneous ground reconnaissance missions, with each force operating within its own territory,” Defensa said.

The ministry said that the second stage of the operation is taking place “as of this date” — i.e., Monday, Sept. 7 — and until Sept. 21. The stage involves “the deployment of forces in the border region of each country, supported by fixed and mobile anti-drone equipment,” Defensa said.

“Security cooperation between Mexico and the United States is carried out with full respect for national sovereignty and is governed by the principles of reciprocity, shared and differentiated responsibility, mutual trust and respect for sovereign decisions and territory, favoring at all times the interests of the Mexican state,” the ministry said.

The announcement of the bilateral anti-drone operation came three days after the United States Northern Command said in a statement that the Joint Task Force–Southern Border (JTF-SB) had taken down more than 300 unmanned aircraft systems (UAS), or drones, along the U.S.-Mexico border this year.

“JTF-SB defeated more than 300 UAS this calendar year employing kinetic and non-kinetic systems, with more than 100 defeats occurring in the month of August,” said USNORTHCOM, one of 11 unified combatant commands of the U.S. Department of Defense.

“… The UAS were assessed to be associated with illicit activity along the border. Transnational criminal organizations use UAS to support illegal cross-border activity, including smuggling operations and surveillance of law-enforcement and military personnel,” USNORTHCOM said.

It noted that JTF-SB personnel have conducted patrols along the border “in coordination with Mexican military personnel.”

Trevilla said Friday that U.S. authorities had informed the Mexican government that drones are mainly used in the border region by people who smuggle migrants into the United States

“They are commercial drones. They only capture images … and what they’re seeking to find are routes that are free, where there is no presence of [U.S.] authorities,” the defense minister said.

Last month, Mexico and the United States signed a defense agreement on new technologies that allows Defensa to acquire drones and counter-unmanned aerial systems in the U.S. Army’s online marketplace. However, the Defense Ministry said at the time that it hadn’t made any purchase commitment.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: The Latin Grammy Winner Touring Brazil With an Accordion and No S
World.content:
Music: Brazil

Key Facts What happened. João Gomes, Jota.pê and Mestrinho are touring Brazil with their album Dominguinho.

João Gomes, Jota.pê and Mestrinho are touring Brazil with their album Dominguinho. What it won. The 2025 Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Roots Album, on November 13.

The 2025 Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Roots Album, on November 13. How big the tour is. Twenty-seven announced dates through January, then six European cities in February.

Twenty-seven announced dates through January, then six European cities in February. The catch. The Rio show is an outdoor garden concert at 15:00, not a seated hall recital.

The Rio show is an outdoor garden concert at 15:00, not a seated hall recital. The spelling. The project is Dominguinho. The accordionist it honours was Dominguinhos, with an S.

The project is Dominguinho. The accordionist it honours was Dominguinhos, with an S. What it costs. Comparable dates ran from R$165 to R$1,095, or about US$32 to US$215.

Three musicians from different corners of Brazilian music made a loose record in ten days. It won a Latin Grammy, and the tour behind it runs to twenty-seven dates.

The Latin Grammy Winner Touring Brazil With an Accordion and No S

If you live in Brazil and have not heard of this, it is the most acclaimed Brazilian roots album of its year. If you are visiting, it is the shortest route into the music of the Northeast.

It Won, and the Category Matters

The album won the Latin Grammy for Best Portuguese Language Roots Album at the ceremony in Las Vegas on November 13, 2025.

Coverage that says nominated is reporting the September 2025 story and stopping there. The nomination was real, and so was the win two months later.

It was João Gomes’s first Latin Grammy, after nominations in 2023 and 2024. Jota.pê had already swept all three of his categories in 2024.

One caution on sourcing. The academy’s own database would not open to us, so the win rests on four Brazilian outlets that agree on the details.

The Name Is Not a Typo

The project is called Dominguinho, singular. The musician it honours was Dominguinhos, with an S.

Brazilian coverage flagged the difference deliberately, and foreign readers and copy editors alike tend to assume an error.

The title works two ways. It evokes a lazy Sunday afternoon, since domingo means Sunday, and it nods to the accordionist’s legacy.

Jota.pê has resisted calling it strictly a tribute. He describes the record as a hangout between friends playing that turned into an album.

Who Dominguinhos Was

José Domingos de Morais, born in Garanhuns in the interior of Pernambuco in 1941, was the accordion virtuoso of his generation. He died in 2013.

He met Luiz Gonzaga, the founding figure of the genre, at the age of nine. He moved to Rio at thirteen to work with him.

What made him matter was the bridging. He played the rural music of the Northeast with bossa nova, jazz and pop musicians, recording with Gilberto Gil and Caetano Veloso.

He won a Latin Grammy himself in 2002. When three young musicians name a record after him, Brazilian listeners hear a claim to a lineage.

Forró, and Why the Accordion Signals Something

Forró is the umbrella name for the dance music of Brazil’s Northeast. That is the dry, culturally distinct region behind much of the country’s internal migration.

Its core trio is accordion, zabumba, a two-headed bass drum, and triangle. The accordion is called the sanfona.

It occupies the place the fiddle holds in American country music. It is the instrument that signals regional identity and rural origin.

For decades this music carried a class stigma in the wealthier Southeast. The past few years have moved it to the centre of Brazilian pop, and this record is part of that shift.

The Three of Them

João Gomes, 24, comes from the Pernambuco backlands and is the commercial engine. He broke out around 2021 as the star of piseiro, a stripped-down keyboard-driven offshoot of forró that spread through social media.

Jota.pê, 31, is from Osasco in Greater São Paulo and is the critical favourite. He works in Brazilian popular music with strong Afro-Brazilian influences, and he is not a Northeastern regional artist at all.

Mestrinho, from Sergipe, is the accordionist and the direct instrumental heir to the Dominguinhos line. He is the technical and traditional anchor of the group.

A second volume of the project arrived on May 7 through Sony Music Brasil, twelve tracks self-produced by the three of them. That is the material the current tour carries.

The Dates, and What Rio Actually Is

Twenty-seven dates have been announced. Rio is November 14, Salvador November 28 at the Arena Fonte Nova, and Belo Horizonte December 5 at the Mineirão.

Recife follows on December 6 at Classic Hall and Goiânia on December 19. The run continues into January with Belém, Brasília and Curitiba.

The Rio show needs a correction most listings miss. It is in the gardens of the Cidade das Artes in Barra da Tijuca, starting at 15:00.

That is an outdoor afternoon concert, and it is 18 and over because alcohol is served. Anyone picturing a seated recital in the concert hall has the wrong building in mind.

A European leg follows in February 2027, with Dublin, Berlin, Porto, Madrid, Barcelona and Lisbon. Only the Porto venue, the Coliseu, has been named.

What It Costs

Rio prices had not been published in readable form at the time of writing. We are not printing a figure we cannot see.

Comparable dates give the shape. The São Paulo show in April ran from R$165 (about US$32) to R$995 (about US$196) for a VIP package.

Standing was R$245 (about US$48) and premium standing R$495 (about US$97) at that show. A Belo Horizonte date in February ran standing at R$360 (about US$71) full price.

Conversions use 5.0856 reais to the US dollar, the Banco Central closing rate for September 8, 2026.

A Banco do Brasil cardholder presale with a twenty per cent discount runs across the Brazilian dates. Half-price meia-entrada applies as it does everywhere in Brazil.

One Belo Horizonte listing described the Mineirão show as free entry while also saying ticketing had not been announced. Treat that as a template error rather than an offer.

More: Brazil news, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Did the album win a Latin Grammy or was it only nominated? It won, on November 13, 2025, for Best Portuguese Language Roots Album. The nomination story from September 2025 is often recirculated as if the ceremony had not happened. Why is the name spelled without an S? The project is Dominguinho, the accordionist honoured was Dominguinhos. The title also plays on domingo, the Portuguese word for Sunday. What kind of show is the Rio date? An outdoor afternoon concert in the gardens of the Cidade das Artes in Barra da Tijuca, starting at 15:00. It is sold as standing, front stage and box, and it is 18 and over. Where else does the tour go? Twenty-seven Brazilian dates through January, including Salvador, Belo Horizonte, Recife, Goiânia, Belém, Brasília and Curitiba, then six European cities in February 2027.

World.title: Ty Segall Plays Brazil for the First Time, After Almost Twenty Years
World.content:
Concerts: São Paulo

Key Facts What happened. Ty Segall plays São Paulo on November 15, his first show in Brazil after nearly twenty years.

Ty Segall plays São Paulo on November 15, his first show in Brazil after nearly twenty years. Where it is. Audio on Avenida Francisco Matarazzo, a 2,800-capacity standing room in Barra Funda.

Audio on Avenida Francisco Matarazzo, a 2,800-capacity standing room in Barra Funda. What it costs. Six tiers from R$180 (about US$35) to R$520 (about US$102), plus fees.

Six tiers from R$180 (about US$35) to R$520 (about US$102), plus fees. The cheaper way in. A solidarity ticket is sold in exchange for a kilo of non-perishable food.

A solidarity ticket is sold in exchange for a kilo of non-perishable food. The catch. It is 18 and over, with no accompanied-minor exception published.

It is 18 and over, with no accompanied-minor exception published. What comes next. Three other Latin American dates, in Mexico, Argentina and Chile.

Ty Segall has made roughly seventeen albums since 2008 and has never played Brazil. That ends on November 15, in a club rather than at a festival.

Ty Segall on stage with his band. He plays his first Brazilian show in Sao Paulo on November 15 (Photo: Thomson200, CC0 via Wikimedia Commons)

This is not a stadium booking or a festival slot. It is one Sunday night in a 2,800-capacity room, promoted by the independent outfit that brought Bikini Kill to Brazil.

The Show

Ty Segall plays Audio on Sunday November 15. Doors open at 18:00, and the venue is at Avenida Francisco Matarazzo 694, in Barra Funda.

The venue calls itself Audio, one word and no accent. Listings that write Audio Club or Áudio are using names the house does not use.

The promoter is Associação Cultural Cecília, the São Paulo independent-culture association founded in 2008. It has staged more than a thousand shows and previously brought Acid Mothers Temple, Lee Ranaldo, Tom Zé and Bikini Kill.

Two São Paulo bands open, Ema Stoned and Bike, with a DJ set by Supernovissima. No stage time for the headliner has been published, so do not plan around one.

Prices, and the Food-Donation Ticket

The seller lists six ticket offers, from R$180 (about US$35) to R$520 (about US$102). The published headline is from R$180.

At the on-sale in July the first lote ran at R$180 for meia-entrada and R$360 (about US$71) full, plus fees. The current lote could not be read from open pages.

There is also an Ingresso Solidário, a discounted ticket bought in exchange for a kilo of non-perishable food at the door. Salt and cornmeal are excluded.

Conversions use 5.0856 reais to the US dollar, the Banco Central closing rate for September 8, 2026.

The seller’s price table sits inside a purchase flow we could not read. We are not printing a tier list we cannot see.

Payment is by card or Pix, in up to twelve instalments. Buying through the seller’s app within about 500 metres of the venue waives the service fee.

The Half-Price Rule, and Who It Covers

There is one sector, Pista, holding 2,800 people. The meia-entrada quota is 1,120 places, or forty per cent, as federal law requires.

Half price covers students with the national student card and people registered in the federal social database. Public-school teachers and people with disabilities plus a companion also qualify.

Over-60s get fifty per cent separately under the elderly statute, and that entitlement sits outside the forty per cent cap.

Documents are checked at purchase and again at the door. Anyone who cannot produce them pays the difference to get in.

For most foreign visitors this is not an accessible discount. It requires Brazilian documentation rather than simply being a student somewhere.

Who Ty Segall Is

Ty Segall is an American garage-rock musician and producer from Laguna Beach, California, born in 1987. He records for Drag City in Chicago.

He is known as much for volume of output as for volume of amplifier. His solo discography runs to roughly seventeen studio albums since 2008, sometimes three or four in a single year.

That count excludes a parallel run of bands and collaborations, including Fuzz and GØGGS. His range runs from fuzz-blown garage punk to acoustic and glam-inflected records.

He is a central figure of the Californian garage revival of the 2010s. That scene also produced Thee Oh Sees and his own bassist, Mikal Cronin.

What He Is Touring

The album is Chrome, nine tracks released on August 28 through Drag City. A companion record called Love Fuzzz came out the same day.

He is touring with a full band rather than solo. The line-up is Mikal Cronin on bass, Emmett Kelly on guitar, Ben Boye on keyboards and Evan Burrows on drums.

That is the same line-up credited on the album, several songs of which were written in the room during rehearsals.

Speaking to Rolling Stone Brasil in September, he said he wants to dig through record shops while he is in the country. On the show itself he was blunter: come if you want to hear rock and roll played very loud.

The Rest of the Latin American Run

São Paulo is the only Brazilian date, and Brazilian coverage calls it a single show. It is one leg of four across the region.

Querétaro in Mexico comes first, on October 24 at the Cervecería Hércules. Buenos Aires follows on November 7 at Niceto Club.

Santiago is on November 10 at Blondie, then São Paulo on the 15th. Argentine coverage frames Buenos Aires as a return, so Brazil is the debut and Argentina is not.

The venue sits beside the Barra Funda metro and rail interchange, which is the practical way there and back. Paid parking is sold separately, from 17:00, at Avenida Francisco Matarazzo 678.

More: Brazil news, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is this really Ty Segall’s first show in Brazil? Yes. He has been recording since 2008 and has roughly seventeen solo albums, and this is his first Brazilian performance. How much are tickets? Six tiers from R$180 (about US$35) to R$520 (about US$102), plus fees. A solidarity ticket is also sold in exchange for a kilo of non-perishable food. What time does he play? Doors are at 18:00 and no stage time has been published. With two support bands and a DJ set, the headline set will be considerably later. Can I get in under 18? No. The show is 18 and over, and neither the venue nor the seller publishes an exception for minors with a guardian.

World.title: Matteo Bocelli Plays Four Brazilian Cities in October, Not Two
World.content:
Key Facts What happened. Matteo Bocelli plays four Brazilian cities in late October, on the Falling in Love tour.

Matteo Bocelli plays four Brazilian cities in late October, on the Falling in Love tour. How it grew. It was announced in March as a single São Paulo show. Three cities were added later.

It was announced in March as a single São Paulo show. Three cities were added later. What it costs. Rio starts at R$336 (about US$66). The top São Paulo seat is R$1,108 (about US$218).

Rio starts at R$336 (about US$66). The top São Paulo seat is R$1,108 (about US$218). The catch. This is not an Andrea Bocelli concert. His father is not on any of these dates.

This is not an Andrea Bocelli concert. His father is not on any of these dates. Who is turned away. Rio is 18 and over. São Paulo and Curitiba admit from 16.

Rio is 18 and over. São Paulo and Curitiba admit from 16. What comes first. The Latin American leg opens in Santiago on October 21, at a newly renamed arena.

Concerts: Brazil

Matteo Bocelli brings the Falling in Love tour to Brazil in late October for four theatre shows. Most listings still say two, and the age limit changes between cities.

Matteo Bocelli Plays Four Brazilian Cities in October, Not Two

These are deliberately small rooms, and the tour sells them that way. Anyone booking at the top price should know exactly whose voice they are paying for.

Four Cities, Not One

São Paulo comes first, on Saturday October 24 at the Tokio Marine Hall. Curitiba follows on Tuesday the 27th at the Teatro Positivo.

Rio de Janeiro is Thursday October 29 at Vivo Rio. Belo Horizonte closes the run on Saturday the 31st, at the Grande Teatro in the Palácio das Artes.

Doors open at 19:00 and the show starts at 21:00 at all four. The official Brazilian tour site calls them four exclusive shows.

The run was announced in March as a single São Paulo date. Curitiba, Rio and Belo Horizonte were added later, which is why older listings are short.

What It Costs

Rio has the widest spread and the cheapest way in. Camarote C starts at R$336 (about US$66) and the top tier reaches R$1,097 (about US$216).

In between, Rio runs Frisas at R$380 (about US$75), Setor 03 at R$560 (about US$110) and Setor 01 at R$784 (about US$154).

São Paulo starts higher. Setor 03 is R$358 (about US$70), Setor 02 is R$448 (about US$88) and Setor 01 is R$728 (about US$143).

The top São Paulo tier, VIP Premium, is R$1,108 (about US$218). That is roughly five times the entry price of his 2024 Brazilian shows.

Curitiba publishes one tier clearly: R$550 plus a R$71 fee, so R$621 all in (about US$122). The seller there adds a booking fee, while the São Paulo and Rio seller does not.

Conversions use 5.0856 reais to the US dollar, the Banco Central closing rate for September 8, 2026.

Belo Horizonte prices had not appeared in readable form at the time of writing. Neither had on-sale dates for three of the four cities.

The Age Limit Changes Between Cities

Rio is 18 and over. That is stricter than the rest of the run and easy to miss.

São Paulo and Curitiba are 16 and over. Curitiba prints the usual carve-out for younger children with a parent or legal guardian.

No age rating was published for Belo Horizonte at the time of writing. Check before booking for a family.

The meia-entrada, Brazil’s half-price entitlement, applies at every date and is exactly fifty per cent.

It is not a discount foreigners can generally use. It covers students, the young, the old and people with disabilities, and documents are checked at the door.

What the Show Is Not

This is not an Andrea Bocelli concert, and the price of the top tier makes that worth stating plainly. His father is not on any of these dates.

The difference starts with the rooms. The Tokio Marine Hall holds 4,000, and the other three are theatres.

Andrea Bocelli plays arenas and stadiums. His own 2026 anniversary tour is an arena run, and he sang at the Winter Olympics opening in February.

The format differs too. Matteo plays a pop-classical crossover set of his own material, not an operatic programme with a symphony orchestra and guest sopranos.

He has appeared in Brazil before as a guest in his father’s shows. He headlined his own first Brazilian run in October 2024.

Who He Is

Matteo Bocelli was born in Forte dei Marmi, in Tuscany, in October 1997. He turns 29 sixteen days before the São Paulo show.

He is the second son of the tenor Andrea Bocelli. His first release was a family Christmas record in 2022, made with his father and his sister Virginia.

His solo debut came in September 2023, an album simply called Matteo. That distinction matters, because the Christmas record is often miscalled his debut.

The current album, Falling in Love, came out in September 2025 on Decca. He co-wrote every original track on it.

One song lands differently in Brazil. His duet version of Mi Historia Entre Tus Dedos is the Grignani song Brazilians know as Quem de Nós Dois.

The Venues, and One Common Mix-Up

The Tokio Marine Hall is in Santo Amaro, in the south of São Paulo, at Rua Bragança Paulista 1281. It is the former Tom Brasil, and before that the HSBC Brasil.

It is not the former Citibank Hall, and the two are regularly confused. That building is a different, larger venue on Avenida das Nações Unidas, now called Vibra São Paulo.

Vivo Rio sits on Avenida Infante Dom Henrique in the Parque do Flamengo, a short distance from the city centre.

The Curitiba show is at the Teatro Positivo in Campo Comprido. Belo Horizonte is at the Palácio das Artes on Avenida Afonso Pena.

The Latin American leg opens in Santiago on October 21, at the arena in Parque O’Higgins. That venue was renamed the Santander Arena on September 6, so both names are still circulating.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many Brazilian shows are there? Four: São Paulo on October 24, Curitiba on the 27th, Rio de Janeiro on the 29th and Belo Horizonte on the 31st. Doors are at 19:00 and shows start at 21:00. Is Andrea Bocelli performing? No, these are Matteo Bocelli’s own headline shows in theatres and small halls. His father is not on any of the dates. How much are tickets? Rio is the cheapest way in, from R$336 (about US$66). São Paulo runs from R$358 (about US$70) to R$1,108 (about US$218) for the top tier. What is the minimum age? It differs by city, with Rio at 18 and over while São Paulo and Curitiba admit from 16. Nothing was published for Belo Horizonte at the time of writing.

World.title: The Mars Volta Play Mexico City, and This Time the Whole Catalogue
World.content:
Concerts: Mexico City

Key Facts What happened. The Mars Volta play the Pepsi Center WTC in Mexico City on Sunday November 29.

The Mars Volta play the Pepsi Center WTC in Mexico City on Sunday November 29. Why it matters. The 2025 shows played one album start to finish. This run draws on everything.

The 2025 shows played one album start to finish. This run draws on everything. What it costs. General admission is about 1,290 pesos (about US$76), rising to 2,827 (about US$167).

General admission is about 1,290 pesos (about US$76), rising to 2,827 (about US$167). The catch. Buy from abroad and the cardholder must collect in person, with matching ID.

Buy from abroad and the cardholder must collect in person, with matching ID. The other date. They play Puebla the night before, alongside Caifanes and The Flaming Lips.

They play Puebla the night before, alongside Caifanes and The Flaming Lips. Who opens. The Puerto Rican artist Kianí Medina is the announced special guest.

The Mars Volta return to Mexico City on November 29 for a career-spanning set. That is not what they were doing a year ago, and buying from outside Mexico is the hard part.

The Mars Volta on stage, with Omar Rodriguez-Lopez on guitar and Cedric Bixler-Zavala on vocals. They play Mexico City on November 29 (Photo: Steve Collis, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

Omar Rodríguez-López calls Mexico his magic place, and the band treats it as a second home market. This is the show where they finally play the old songs again.

The Show

The Mars Volta play the Pepsi Center WTC on Sunday November 29, starting at 20:00. The venue is inside the World Trade Center complex in Colonia Nápoles, in the Benito Juárez borough.

The show time comes from the venue’s own event page and the band’s official tour feed, which agree exactly. No doors time has been published anywhere.

The promoter is OCESA. Tickets are sold through Ticketmaster México and at the venue box office.

The Puerto Rican artist Kianí Medina is the announced special guest. This is a single headline show rather than a festival slot.

The Set Is the Story

Their 2025 shows played the album Lucro Sucio; Los Ojos del Vacío in full, and nothing else. That is unusual even by their standards.

The 2026 run is explicitly career-spanning and draws on the whole catalogue. For anyone who waited out the 2025 tour, that is the difference that matters.

The album itself came out in April 2025, eighteen tracks of prog, jazz, electronics and psychedelia. A fan-voted live album was announced in July.

The band last played this same venue in May 2023. Mexico is reported to be their second-largest market.

Prices, and Where They Come From

General admission is listed at about 1,290 pesos, roughly US$76. Sección C is about 1,513 pesos, or US$89.

Box Superior runs to 1,686 pesos (about US$100), and the Corona Lounge tier reaches 2,827 pesos (about US$167).

Accessible seating is priced with Sección C, at about 1,512 pesos. Conversions use 16.91 pesos to the US dollar, the interbank close for September 8, 2026.

One caveat we will not hide. Ticketmaster México blocks automated access, so these figures come from Mexican press rather than from the seller.

Sources also differ by a few centavos, and none establishes clearly whether the published prices include service charges. Check the seller before you commit.

A Citibanamex presale ran on September 1 and the general sale opened on September 2. The band’s own tour feed still showed tickets available today.

The Box-Office Trap for Foreign Buyers

The venue requires the cardholder in person, with matching photo identification, for card purchases at the box office. A passport, residency card, national ID or driving licence is accepted.

Will Call pickup works the same way and needs the physical card. Tickets not collected within the stated window are cancelled outright.

That catches visitors who buy from abroad and expect to collect on arrival with someone else’s card. It does not work.

Buying at the box office in person has one real advantage. The venue charges no service fee there, unlike the online seller.

Digital tickets need mobile data at the gate, because the barcode refreshes. The choice between print and digital cannot be undone once made.

Who They Are

The Mars Volta formed in El Paso, Texas in 2001, around the singer Cedric Bixler-Zavala and the guitarist and producer Omar Rodríguez-López.

Both came out of At the Drive-In, the post-hardcore band that broke up in 2001 on the edge of a commercial breakthrough. The pair explored dub first, in a side project, before starting this one.

The sound fuses progressive rock, free jazz, salsa and Latin percussion with punk aggression, and the song titles are frequently Spanish. They became the most commercially successful openly experimental rock band of the 2000s.

Get the split right, because it is often reported loosely. They went on hiatus in September 2012 and formally broke up in January 2013, after a falling-out between the two principals.

They reconvened privately in 2019 and announced the reunion in June 2022, with a self-titled album that September.

The Puebla Date, and Getting There

They also play Tecate Comuna at Foro Cholula in San Andrés Cholula, Puebla, on November 28. That is the night before, on a bill with Caifanes and The Flaming Lips.

Puebla is about two hours from the capital and needs a separate ticket. Anyone doing both should book the road time deliberately.

For the Mexico City show, the Pepsi Center WTC sits sixty metres from Avenida Insurgentes with more than 3,000 parking spaces.

Public transport is Metrobús Line 1 to Poliforum, or Metro Line 7 to San Pedro de los Pinos. The box office opens 11:00 to 19:00 on weekdays and 11:00 to 16:00 at weekends.

The hall takes roughly 6,500 to 8,000 people in concert format. Most events admit all ages, and no age restriction has been published for this one.

Frequently Asked Questions

When and where do The Mars Volta play in Mexico City? Sunday November 29 at the Pepsi Center WTC in Colonia Nápoles, starting at 20:00. No doors time has been published. How much are tickets? General admission is about 1,290 pesos (about US$76), rising to 2,827 pesos (about US$167) for the Corona Lounge tier. Those figures come from Mexican press, not the seller. Will they play the old songs? Yes. The 2025 shows played one album in full, but the 2026 run is career-spanning and draws on the whole catalogue. Can I buy a ticket from outside Mexico? You can pay online, but the box office requires the cardholder in person with matching identification. Uncollected tickets are cancelled, so plan the pickup before you travel.

Key Facts What happened. Beéle plays Santiago on Wednesday October 7, at 21:00, on the Borondo tour.

Beéle plays Santiago on Wednesday October 7, at 21:00, on the Borondo tour. The catch. The venue stopped being the Movistar Arena on Saturday. It is now the Santander Arena.

The venue stopped being the Movistar Arena on Saturday. It is now the Santander Arena. What it costs. Eight tiers from 40,250 pesos (about US$43) to 115,000 pesos (about US$123).

Eight tiers from 40,250 pesos (about US$43) to 115,000 pesos (about US$123). Still available. The bank presale sold out, but the general sale was still open today.

The bank presale sold out, but the general sale was still open today. Who needs an adult. Under-15s must be accompanied, and children under three are not admitted.

Under-15s must be accompanied, and children under three are not admitted. What is not published. No doors time exists. The venue posts it on social media nearer the date.

The Colombian singer Beéle returns to Santiago on October 7. The building he plays changed its name two days ago, and most listings have not caught up.

The Parque O Higgins dome in Santiago, photographed under its former Movistar Arena branding. Since September 6 it has been the Santander Arena (Photo: Jorge Barrios, CC BY-SA 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

If you are searching for this show, the venue name in your search is probably out of date. Everything else about the night is published in full, which is rarer than it sounds.

The Venue Changed Its Name on Saturday

The dome in Parque O’Higgins was the Movistar Arena for sixteen years. On Saturday September 6 it became the Santander Arena.

This is not a rumour or a plan. The old web address now redirects to the new one, and the site carries the new name throughout.

The change follows Telefónica’s sale of its Chilean business and the retirement of the Movistar brand there. The naming deal expired this month, and Banco Santander took it on.

The operator has not changed, and neither has the building. Only the name and the signage have.

Expect confusion for months. Even the seller’s own page carries the new name in its purchase header and the old one in its page title.

The venue’s own event page does the same thing, with a headline saying Santander Arena above a paragraph still saying Movistar Arena.

The Show

Beéle plays on Wednesday October 7 at 21:00. The address is Beaucheff 1204, in Santiago Centro.

The promoter is Multimúsica. The only authorised seller is Puntoticket, which the venue states explicitly for all its shows.

The tour is called Borondo: Detone y Abandone. It opened in Spain in July and runs through Europe and Latin America.

This is his second Santiago run in about a year. He played the same building in 2025, when it still carried the old name.

Prices, in Full

Eight tiers are published, which is unusually complete. The cheapest is Tribuna at 40,250 pesos, about US$43.

Platea Alta costs 51,750 pesos (about US$55), and the standing floor, Cancha, is 63,250 pesos (about US$68).

Platea Baja Silver is 86,250 pesos (about US$92) and Cancha VIP is 97,750 pesos (about US$105).

The most expensive seat, Platea Baja Golden, is 115,000 pesos (about US$123). Wheelchair spaces and companion seats are both 51,750 pesos.

Conversions use 933.82 pesos to the US dollar, the Banco Central de Chile observed rate for September 8, 2026.

A Banco Falabella presale opened on July 23 with a twenty per cent discount and sold out. The general sale opened the next day and was still marked available today.

Who Beéle Is

Brandon de Jesús López Orozco was born in Barranquilla, on Colombia’s Caribbean coast, in September 2002. He turns 24 three weeks before this show.

His music mixes Colombian coastal rhythms with afrobeat, dancehall and reggae. That Caribbean base is what separates him from the Medellín reggaeton sound most foreigners assume.

His first hit was Loco in 2019. The 2020 remix with Farruko, Natti Natasha and Manuel Turizo reached the Billboard Latin digital chart.

The real breakout came with his debut album Borondo, released in May 2025. Note the year, because at least one widely used reference gives 2024 and is wrong.

He has since released a collaborative album with Ozuna and an EP in August. He now has more than 35 million monthly listeners on Spotify.

Entry Rules Worth Reading First

Everyone entering needs a ticket, including small children. Under-threes are not admitted at all.

From three years up a ticket must be bought, and anyone under 15 must be accompanied by an adult.

You need the ticket, printed or on a phone, plus your identity card or passport. The venue asks for both at the door.

Tickets for this show are not nominative. The venue applies that rule to some events, and this one’s published conditions do not include it.

No doors time has been published. The venue says it announces opening on its official social accounts nearer the date, so do not guess.

Getting There

The practical route is Metro Line 2 to Parque O’Higgins, or on foot along Tupper. The station sits beside the park.

Driving is more restricted than at most venues. Vehicle access requires a parking ticket bought in advance through the seller, not paid at the gate.

The entrance you use depends on what your parking ticket says, either Avenida Viel or Avenida Tupper. There is no on-site purchase.

The hall holds about 15,500 people and is Chile’s largest covered venue. A Wednesday show in Santiago Centro means a working-day crowd leaving late.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Beéle playing at the Movistar Arena? It is the same building, but the name changed on September 6. It is now the Santander Arena, in Parque O’Higgins, Santiago Centro. How much are tickets? Eight tiers, from 40,250 pesos (about US$43) for Tribuna to 115,000 pesos (about US$123) for Platea Baja Golden. The standing floor is 63,250 pesos (about US$68). What time does it start? The show starts at 21:00 on Wednesday October 7. No doors time has been published, and the venue says it announces that on its social accounts. Do I need identification to get in? Yes, the venue asks for your ticket plus an identity card or passport. Tickets for this show are not nominative, so they can be transferred.

This is the Spanish singer’s return to Uruguay on a tour built around standards rather than his own hits. For anyone in Montevideo, it is one night between two Argentine dates.

The Show

Bisbal plays the Antel Arena on Saturday October 17. Doors open at 19:30 and the show starts at 21:00.

Those times come from the venue’s own event page and appear nowhere else. Treat them as the venue’s word rather than as confirmed twice.

The producers are Piano Piano, a Uruguayan promoter, together with the Argentine company DF Entertainment.

Tickets are sold only through Tickantel. The promoter’s own wording is that it is the sole platform.

What It Costs, and What Is Missing

The published range runs from 2,400 pesos (about US$60) to 8,000 pesos (about US$199).

That range is all anyone outside the seller can see. Neither Tickantel nor the venue publishes a sector-by-sector table.

The seat map sits behind a virtual queue that requires a registered account, so the breakdown is not obtainable from open pages.

Conversions use 40.22 Uruguayan pesos to the US dollar, the Banco Central del Uruguay rate for September 8, 2026.

Those prices were set when the sale opened on May 13. No official update has appeared since, in either direction.

The venue still lists the show as on sale. Tickantel warns of high demand and routes buyers into a queue rather than straight to checkout.

Who He Is, for Anyone Who Missed 2002

David Bisbal is a Spanish singer from Almería, in Andalusia, now 47. He came second in the first series of Operación Triunfo, Spain’s star-making talent show.

Second, not first. His debut album Corazón Latino followed in 2002 and sold heavily across Spain and Latin America.

The songs most people know are Ave María, Bulería and Dígale. He also sang with Rihanna on Hate That I Love You in 2008.

That makes him a fixture of a particular Spanish-language pop era rather than a current chart act. The audience for this show knows every word.

The Album Behind the Tour

The tour is called Eternos and marks 25 years of his career. The promoter’s framing of the anniversary holds, since his breakthrough was 2001.

The album of the same name came out on October 2, two weeks before the Montevideo date. It is a crooner record of classic covers rather than new material.

So the show is likely to lean on standards alongside the hits. Nothing published sets out a setlist.

This is his second Antel Arena show. He played the same room on December 1, 2023, on his twentieth-anniversary tour.

Where Montevideo Sits in the Run

The Latin American leg runs to eighteen dates across nine countries and territories. Santiago opens it on October 6.

Lima follows on October 9, then Buenos Aires on the 12th and Córdoba on the 14th. Montevideo is the 17th.

Rosario comes the very next night, on the 18th, then Bogotá on the 21st and Santo Domingo on the 24th.

Puerto Rico, Mexico and the United States follow in November and December. Anyone flexible about the city has options either side of the river.

Getting There and Getting In

The Antel Arena is at Avenida Dámaso Antonio Larrañaga 4001, in Villa Española, about six kilometres northeast of the old city.

Bus lines 71, 79, 144, 174, 180, 192, 328, 330, 538, L41 and D8 all serve the area. Montevideo has no metro.

The site has 1,200 car spaces and 120 for motorcycles and bicycles. Book online in advance, or pay on arrival at the José Pedro Varela entrance.

Parking on the central medians of Varela and Larrañaga is banned. Two taxi ranks sit on the perimeter, and there are marked pickup points for ride-hailing apps on Larrañaga.

Children under three enter free without occupying a seat, and from four years up a ticket is required. Under-15s must be accompanied by a responsible adult over 18.

Nothing has been published about identification at the door. Tickantel requires a registered account to buy, which is a purchase rule rather than an entry rule.

World.title: Zanzibar Has Turned a Doorway in Stone Town Into an Export Industry
World.content:

One email, every weekday morning. African markets, politics and business — filed from our newsroom in Rio.

ZANZIBAR · CULTURE

Key Facts —The place: The museum occupies part of a Stone Town building the Bulsara family lived in. The museum itself calls it the family home, not the birthplace. —The date: He was born in Zanzibar in 1946, to Parsi parents from western India who worked in the colonial administration. —The departure: The family left for England in 1964, during the Zanzibar revolution. —The setting: Stone Town has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2000, recognised for its Swahili, Arab, Indian and European architecture. —The economy: Tourism is about 29% of Zanzibar’s economy and some 80% of its foreign exchange earnings, and Stone Town is its cultural anchor. —The draw: The museum sits on the standard walking circuit of the old town, alongside the Old Fort and the House of Wonders.

The Zanzibar Freddie Mercury Museum occupies part of a Stone Town building the Queen singer’s family lived in, and has become a fixed stop on the island’s cultural circuit. It sits inside a UNESCO World Heritage site that tourism now depends on.

What the Zanzibar Freddie Mercury Museum actually is

It is small, and it is a doorway first. The building in Stone Town carries a carved sign and display cases of photographs, and it is the address most associated with the birth of Farrokh Bulsara in 1946.

He became Freddie Mercury in London, and Queen never played in Tanzania. The connection is biographical rather than musical.

That has not stopped it becoming one of the most photographed façades on the island.

A very Zanzibari story about who belongs

Bulsara’s parents were Parsis from western India, working in the British colonial administration on an island then ruled by a Sultan of Omani descent. The family left for England in 1964, during the revolution.

The museum opened in November 2019, founded by Andrea Boero and Javed Jafferji and partnered with Queen’s own production company. It has not published visitor numbers.

Zanzibar received 917,167 visitors in 2025, up from 736,755 in 2024, with officials putting receipts at about US$1.1bn. No cumulative figure for 2026 has been published.

There is one thing the museum leaves out. It displays his birth certificate but not his sexuality or his death from an AIDS-related illness in 1991.

Its co-founder has explained that Zanzibar is a conservative Muslim society. Same-sex acts between men carry long prison sentences there, and a Mercury birthday event drew organised objection in 2006.

Stone Town’s architecture records exactly that layering: Swahili, Arab, Indian and European elements in the same street, often in the same building. UNESCO inscribed it as a World Heritage site in 2000 for precisely this reason.

A museum to a Parsi-Zanzibari rock singer is not an anomaly in that setting. It is a fairly literal expression of it.

The company provides financial services, including payment, prepayment, digital banking, and credit solutions. Culture is the island’s second industry, and its first is fragile

Tourism accounts for about 29% of Zanzibar’s economy, and it divides between beach resorts on the east coast and cultural visitors in Stone Town. The two economies behave differently.

Beach tourism is price-sensitive and easily substituted by other Indian Ocean destinations. Heritage tourism is harder to replicate, because the buildings cannot be moved.

That makes Stone Town’s cultural sites disproportionately valuable to the islands’ economy relative to the revenue they take at the door.

The preservation problem underneath

Stone Town’s coral-rag buildings decay quickly in salt air, and many are in poor condition. UNESCO has repeatedly raised concerns about deteriorating structures and unregulated development within the site.

Small privately run museums occupy some of those buildings and keep them in use, which is a form of preservation even when it is not conservation. Occupied buildings survive longer than empty ones.

The question for the islands is whether visitor revenue can fund maintenance at the scale the fabric requires.

Why an investor might care about a doorway

Zanzibar has been marketing itself hard to investors and to remote workers, and Tanzania has been positioning the islands within its wider tourism strategy. Cultural anchors are what let a destination charge more than its beaches alone would earn.

A single museum does not move an economy. A recognisable circuit of them changes the average spend per visitor and the length of stay, which is where tourism economics actually live.

The islands are marketing more than beaches

Zanzibar’s tourism strategy has leaned increasingly on culture, food and history rather than sand alone, and Stone Town is the asset that makes that possible. Spice tours, Swahili architecture and the slave-trade memorial sites all sit within a short walk of each other.

Cultural visitors stay longer and spend more per day than resort guests, which is the economics tourism boards everywhere chase.

The islands have also been courting remote workers, for whom a working old town is more appealing than a beach compound.

Ownership and interpretation are contested

Small privately run museums are commercial ventures, and their interpretation is not always agreed by everyone. A Freddie Mercury attraction has drawn criticism on the islands from those who feel the connection is thin or the celebration inappropriate.

That tension is not unusual in heritage tourism. It is sharper where the subject left as a child and became famous somewhere else.

Seasonality shapes the whole business

Zanzibar’s visitor numbers rise sharply between June and October and again around the turn of the year, and fall away during the long rains. Cultural sites in Stone Town smooth that curve slightly because they do not depend on beach weather.

For operators, an extra shoulder-season month is worth more than a busier peak. Heritage attractions are one of the few levers that deliver it.

What to watch next

The first thing is visitor numbers to Stone Town as against the beach resorts, which the islands publish irregularly. The second is progress on conservation funding within the World Heritage site.

The third is whether the wider Indian Ocean tourism recovery holds through the coming season.

He was born in Stone Town in 1946; the exact house is not established. When did his family leave Zanzibar? The family left for England in 1964, during the Zanzibar revolution. Why is Stone Town significant? It has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2000, recognised for architecture combining Swahili, Arab, Indian and European elements. How important is tourism to Zanzibar? Tourism is about 29% of Zanzibar’s economy and around 80% of its foreign exchange earnings, split between east-coast beach resorts and cultural visitors to Stone Town. What threatens Stone Town? Its coral-rag buildings decay quickly in salt air, and UNESCO has raised concerns about deteriorating structures and unregulated development within the site.
