World.title: Arlene Arnold denied bail in fatal pint bottle stabbing of common-law husband Clive Hendricks; Tells court she was punched several times to the head before attack
World.content:
Arlene Arnold denied bail in fatal pint bottle stabbing of common-law husband Clive Hendricks; Tells court she was punched several times to the head before attack

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A Belize City mother of six who claims she was being beaten by her common-law husband before she fatally wounded him with a broken pint bottle will have to seek bail from the High Court after a Senior Magistrate declined to release her on Tuesday.

Arlene Tanice Arnold, 50, is charged with manslaughter in the death of her common-law husband, 45-year-old Jeremy Gerald “Clive Tambran” Hendricks.

At Tuesday afternoon’s bail hearing, the Senior Magistrate said she had reviewed relevant precedents and found that bail had been granted at the Magistrate’s Court level in cases involving manslaughter by negligence, but not simply manslaughter. Arnold was therefore advised that her bail application would have to be made before the High Court.

She remains remanded at the Belize Central Prison until November 10 unless she is granted bail by the High Court.

Arnold was arraigned Monday, when no plea was taken. Her attorney, Ronell Gonzalez, told the court that she is the mother of six children, including two minors who depend on her, and argued that Hendricks’ death occurred during a domestic dispute in which Arnold had allegedly been subjected to violence.

The defence claims Hendricks had abused Arnold previously and that two reports had been made against him, with another matter involving the couple reportedly before the Family Court. Gonzalez further alleged that Hendricks punched Arnold around the head and temple during Saturday morning’s confrontation and that she reacted while fearing for her safety.

Police, however, offered a somewhat different account at Monday’s press briefing. ASP Stacy Smith said the Gender-Based Violence Response and Investigative Unit had advised investigators that there was no history of reported domestic violence cases between Arnold and Hendricks. Smith added, however, that people living in the area told police that physical altercations between the couple appeared to have been relatively common.

The fatal incident occurred at about 3:33 a.m. on Saturday, September 5, near the corner of New Road and Pickstock Street.

Police responding to the area found Hendricks lying in the street and bleeding profusely from his right arm. He was rushed to the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital but was pronounced dead at 4:44 a.m. Investigators believe the wound to his arm may have severed a major artery.

Police allege that Hendricks and Arnold had been involved in a physical altercation when Arnold wounded him once in the right tricep with a broken pint bottle.

Arnold was later located at an address in the Holy Emmanuel area after her daughter reportedly contacted police. She was initially detained pending a murder investigation and later gave investigators a statement under caution.

After the case file was forwarded to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, police were directed to charge Arnold with manslaughter rather than murder.

Arnold’s attorney is now expected to pursue a bail application before the High Court.

World.title: 3 men, 17-year-old boy charged with stealing tractor belonging to Brian Mira
World.content:
3 men, 17-year-old boy charged with stealing tractor belonging to Brian Mira

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Four people, including a 17-year-old minor, have been charged with stealing a tractor belonging to businessman Brian Mira, brother of Belmopan Area Representative Oscar Mira and a figure linked to one of the family businesses at the centre of the ongoing “Mira Millions” controversy.

Tyrone Jordan, 27, of Hattieville; Dwayne Garbutt, 44, of Belize City; Estevan Humes, 51, of Santa Familia, Cayo; and the 17-year-old Hattieville resident appeared in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Tuesday, where they were jointly charged with theft.

All four pleaded not guilty and were granted bail of $3,000 each plus one surety in the same amount. They must report to the police station nearest their homes every Friday and are due back in court in November.

Police say the case unfolded shortly after 11 p.m. on September 5 when Hattieville officers, acting on information about a stolen tractor, went to an area near Mile 19.5 on the George Price Highway.

Officers reportedly encountered a red Massey Ferguson tractor being driven along a dirt road. A white International 10-wheeler truck was parked nearby, while a black Chevrolet Equinox was allegedly seen exiting the dirt road behind the tractor.

Police say the driver of the Equinox attempted to reverse after seeing the police mobile. Garbutt, who was allegedly driving the SUV, and the 17-year-old passenger were detained.

Humes was allegedly found driving the tractor, while two other men who were near the 10-wheeler truck were also initially detained as part of the investigation.

Police subsequently contacted Mira, 44, of Belmopan City, who visited the Hattieville Police Station and provided documents establishing his ownership of the tractor.

According to police, Humes later told investigators that he had been communicating with a man he knew as “Tyrone” and had arranged to pick up the Massey Ferguson tractor near Mile 19.5.

Police later detained Jordan in Hattieville on September 6. Investigators say Humes identified him as the man with whom he had allegedly been communicating regarding the tractor.

Jordan, Garbutt, Humes and the minor were subsequently charged with theft.

The identity of the tractor’s owner adds a political dimension to what would otherwise be a routine theft case.

Brian Mira is the brother of Oscar Mira, who stepped away from his Cabinet duties in June amid intense scrutiny over leaked SmartStream records showing millions of dollars in Government payments to businesses linked to members of the Mira family.

One of those businesses is MP Farms. Public reports identified Brian Mira as a contact for the company, while Stanley Mira was listed as its owner. 7News reported that leaked records showed 601 transactions totaling approximately $5.67 million to MP Farms between September 2024 and June 2026, with the overwhelming majority originating from the Ministry of Defence.

Earlier records also reportedly showed almost $390,000 in payments to MP Farms processed in a single day in September 2025, during the period when Oscar Mira held responsibility at the Ministry of Defence.

Oscar Mira has denied influencing procurement decisions or Government payments involving his relatives. The Auditor General is currently examining procurement processes at the Ministry of Defence, and no finding of wrongdoing against Mira has been made.

Garbutt was also separately arraigned on three traffic offences arising from the investigation. He pleaded guilty to driving without third-party insurance, driving an unlicensed motor vehicle and driving without a valid Belize driver’s licence.

He was fined $205 for the insurance offence, $55 for driving an unlicensed vehicle and $105 for driving without a valid Belize driver’s licence, with separate payment deadlines and default prison terms.

World.title: Police officer, licensed gun holder detained after 26-year-old shot during Belmopan dispute
World.content:
Police officer, licensed gun holder detained after 26-year-old shot during Belmopan dispute

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A police officer and a licensed firearm holder have both been detained as investigators try to determine who shot a 26-year-old man during a dispute in Las Flores, Belmopan on Monday night.

Police say officers responded to a residence at around 8:00 p.m. on Monday, September 7, following a report of a dispute. During the police response, the 26-year-old man was shot and injured.

He remains hospitalized in stable condition.

According to police, the investigation has so far established that both a licensed firearm holder who was involved in the original dispute and a responding police officer may have discharged their weapons.

Both firearms have been seized, packaged and will be submitted for comparative ballistic testing to determine which weapon fired the shot that struck the victim. Police say an expedited examination will be requested because the ballistic findings are expected to help determine how the investigation proceeds.

Both the licensed firearm holder and the police officer have been detained, and police have launched separate criminal and internal investigations into the incident.

During Tuesday’s press briefing, police were also questioned about allegations circulating on social media that the responding officer may have given the licensed gun holder permission to fire. Police said investigators were not aware of any information supporting that claim and stressed that there is presently no indication that the officer and firearm holder had any prior agreement or plan to act together.

Police urged anyone who witnessed the incident or has information supporting those allegations to make a formal report.

The identities of the detained men have not been released because neither has been charged at this time.

World.title: Truck rolled backwards on hill before fatal accident that killed Mauricio Solis, police say
World.content:
Truck rolled backwards on hill before fatal accident that killed Mauricio Solis, police say

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating a fatal heavy-equipment accident near the Guacamayo Bridge that claimed the life of 49-year-old San Ignacio resident Mauricio Solis.

The incident occurred shortly before midday on Thursday, September 3, along the Chiquibul Road.

According to police, Solis was a passenger in a dump truck that was towing a trailer carrying heavy machinery. Investigators say the machinery was secured to the trailer and the driver was attempting to climb a hill when the truck reportedly developed mechanical difficulties and began rolling backwards.

The driver lost control and the vehicle overturned. Solis was thrown from the truck and became trapped beneath it, sustaining severe injuries. He was subsequently pronounced dead.

Police processed the scene and have opened an investigation. A file is being compiled and will be forwarded to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions for directives once the investigation is completed.

Solis was an employee of Bulridge Ltd. and was on duty at the time of the accident. However, Bulridge has since clarified that the dump truck, trailer and heavy equipment involved did not belong to the company and were not being operated by a Bulridge employee. According to the company, Solis had been assigned to accompany private contractor Bahadur Trucking & Backhoe Service to a designated worksite.

Bulridge said the equipment belonged to the private contractor and that, like Solis’s family, the company is awaiting the findings of the police investigation.

World.title: Belize Territorial Volunteers, BDF and Coast Guard coordinate security for annual Sarstoon expedition
World.content:
Belize Territorial Volunteers, BDF and Coast Guard coordinate security for annual Sarstoon expedition

By Zoila Palma: Today, the Belize Territorial Volunteers (BTV) met with senior officials of the Belize Defence Force (BDF) and Belize Coast Guard to coordinate security and operational arrangements for the group’s upcoming annual expedition to the Sarstoon River.

The meeting, held in Punta Gorda, brought together BTV leaders and Lieutenant Colonel Justo Veliz Jr., Commanding Officer of the BDF’s 1st Infantry Battalion, along with Lieutenant Juan Bulum, Sector South Commander of the Belize Coast Guard.

Discussions included measures aimed at ensuring the safety and orderly movement of participants during the September 10 expedition.

The BTV said that the meeting was productive and reflected a shared commitment to national safety and Belize’s sovereignty.

BTV said collaborative measures were established to prioritize the safety of both Belizean and international participants taking part in the excursion.

BTV Leader Wil Maheia expressed appreciation to the BDF and Coast Guard for their cooperation. “We extend our sincere gratitude to the leadership and personnel of both the Belize Defence Force and the Belize Coast Guard for their professional cooperation and dialogue today,” Maheia said.

“Working together ensures that our citizens can exercise their rights safely as we honor our nation’s sovereignty,” he added.

The BTV says the expedition will be peaceful and orderly, with participants travelling to the Sarstoon River on Thursday, September 10, as part of activities marking Belize’s 45th Independence.

World.title: Have you seen Charles Westby Jr.?
World.content:
Have you seen Charles Westby Jr.?

By Zoila Palma: The family and friends of Belize City resident Charles Westby Jr. is concerned about his whereabouts.

Westby Jr. was last seen on Thursday August 27, 2026.

He is of Creole descent and about 5’10” in height.

Anyone with information on his whereabouts is urged to call Crime Stoppers at 922, use the P3 app, or report to the nearest police station.

World.title: International News: Football stars Messi, Yamal among nominees for 2026 Ballon d’Or
World.content:
International News: Football stars Messi, Yamal among nominees for 2026 Ballon d’Or

By Zoila Palma: Football superstar Lionel Messi and Spanish teenage sensation Lamine Yamal are among the 30 nominees for the 2026 men’s Ballon d’Or, as the football world begins the countdown to one of the sport’s most prestigious individual awards.

The nominees for both the men’s and women’s categories were announced today with the awards ceremony scheduled for October 26 in London.

Yamal, Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé are being viewed as some of the leading contenders for the men’s prize. Kane enjoyed a prolific season with Bayern Munich, scoring 73 goals, while Mbappé continued to impress with Real Madrid.

Yamal has also strengthened his case after a remarkable rise to prominence with Barcelona and Spain, helping the national team secure the World Cup this summer.

Eight-time Ballon d’Or winner Messi has also earned a place among the nominees.

The Inter Miami and Argentina star continues to feature among the world’s elite, with his performances at the World Cup contributing to his inclusion.

Other notable names on the 30-player list include Jude Bellingham, Ousmane Dembélé, Erling Haaland, Bruno Fernandes, Vinícius Jr., Rodri, Lautaro Martínez, Achraf Hakimi and Vitinha. The award is determined through voting by a panel of international football journalists, making the final result one of the most closely watched individual honors in the sport.

World.title: Police say no motive yet in Barry Johnston murder; surveillance footage aiding investigation
World.content:
Police say no motive yet in Barry Johnston murder; surveillance footage aiding investigation

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police say they have not yet established a motive for the murder of 33-year-old Barry Johnston, who was gunned down in Belize City’s Kings Park area on Monday night.

According to police, Johnston was speaking with two people who were seated inside a van parked on the street when two men approached and fired several shots. Johnston was fatally wounded, while another man was shot and survived.

Investigators have since obtained surveillance footage from the Crime Fusion Center, which police say is proving useful to the investigation. Police would not confirm reports that an automatic weapon was used.

Public reporting places the shooting at the corner of F and Seventh streets in Kings Park. Surveillance footage provided to Breaking Belize News showed a vehicle leaving the area onto Sixth Street. BBN also previously reported that the second shooting victim was hospitalized in stable condition.

During Tuesday’s police press briefing, investigators were questioned about possible gang connections and whether the killing could be linked to a recent aggravated burglary at Johnston’s home in the Belama area. Police stressed that no motive or connection has been established.

Police confirmed that Johnston was known to law enforcement and had previously been convicted of drug trafficking. Johnston had also faced an aggravated assault with a firearm charge in connection with a 2015 incident. That case did not result in a conviction; in December 2016, the charge against Johnston and three other men was struck out for want of prosecution after the complainant failed to testify.

Police also declined to comment on questions about whether Johnston had any connection to a separate missing-person investigation, saying they would not cast aspersions without evidence.

The investigation continues.

World.title: Rough start
World.content:
Grade two students at Holland Primary School in class under a bamboo structure on Monday.Photo: Naphtali Junior

THE education ministry on Monday reported a generally smooth reopening of schools across the island for the start of the 2026/27 academic year but principals, mostly in hurricane-ravaged western Jamaica, highlighted a raft of difficulties.

Among the complaints were incomplete repairs as well as classes held in heat-trapping tents that turn into sweltering ovens under the tropical sun.

“Based on preliminary data received from all seven educational regions covering approximately 1,000 schools, only three schools did not open today, meaning that approximately 99.7 per cent of the schools captured in the data were able to open on the first day of the new school year,” the ministry said in a news release.

While the ministry said late furniture delivery was among the most frequently reported challenges on Monday, Jamaica Observer journalists received first-hand reports of the rough start to the academic year in the sections of the island that suffered the brunt of Hurricane Melissa’s fury last October.

Stories on Pages 3 to 10.

World.title: Two traditions, one future
World.content:
Education Minister Senator Dr Dana Morris Dixon (centre), along with former Hydel High Principal Dr Walton Small (right), as well as teachers and students of the newly merged Hydel Cumberland High School, release balloons in celebration of the official opening of the merged institution on the first day of the new academic year, Monday. (Photos: Garfield Robinson)

EDUCATION Minister Senator Dr Dana Morris Dixon officially unveiled the newly merged Hydel Cumberland High School Monday, declaring that the unification wasn’t about erasing either school’s identity, but rather combining the best of their traditions to create a single learning environment better equipped to serve students and make fuller use of existing resources.

“I love to see the new motto: ‘On the wings of excellence, endeavour to soar.’ And that’s a merger of the two mottos of the two schools. So even starting with the name, we merged the two schools. With the motto, we have merged the two schools and their ethos,” Morris Dixon said Monday while delivering greetings at the name unveiling ceremony at the school’s campus in Portmore, St Catherine.

As she helped to officiate both the historic first day of the school and the start of the 2026-2027 academic year, Morris Dixon explained that Cumberland High School had a capacity for 1,200 students but had only been operating with just over 300 students when she visited about a year ago. She added that the infrastructural challenges at Hydel High, coupled with Cumberland’s available space, made the merger a practical option.

“One of the things we had thought about was potentially moving the children in little groups to different schools, putting them all around St Catherine. But I think this is the best option. I think this was quite strategic in nature, and that’s how we’re going to continue to do this restructuring of education in Jamaica — be strategic — because now that we have one institution instead of two, it means we can direct more resources to one… that is our plan,” said Morris Dixon.

Already, significant investment is being made in the new school. The minister announced that $70 million is being spent to improve its electrical system while work is also being done on the home economics laboratory.

She added that the school’s parking lot will be expanded to accommodate the increased number of staff, while upgrades to the sporting facilities are also planned.

“So there’s a lot that will happen here, and Principal [Carlon Pitt] can ask for everything he wants. Principal, we’ve already granted your first wish, which was more students, but your success, the success of this merged institution, is really important to the Ministry of Education. We are very much committed to it. We’re committed to seeing the traditions work together and to achieve so much more,” she said.

Morris Dixon acknowledged, however, that bringing together two established school communities would not be without challenges but promised that her ministry would be strongly supporting the school’s leadership to smoothly navigate any trials that may arise.

“There are understandable emotions when schools merge. I know there is sadness from some who are, you know, leaving a space that they’re used to. There are those who are seeing all these new children come and these new teachers come. There are a lot of emotions involved in this, and so I want to acknowledge those emotions. Change is never easy; it’s always hard. And us adults, we sometimes have a harder time than the children with change,” she said.

“So teachers, I know this is an emotional period for you… I know that you’re great, I know you’re wonderful, I have no doubt that we have the best teachers in this world in Jamaica, so I know we can get through this. The ministry is here to support, in whatever way we can, to the students who may be coming to this new environment. You have a good principal, you have a good team here; you’re going to be okay,” Morris Dixon assured.

Principal Pitt told the Jamaica Observer that as the former head of Cumberland High he was highly receptive to the idea of a school merger.

Welcoming this new chapter in his career, Pitt emphasised that his vision focuses heavily on academics while prioritising students’ holistic development.

Highlighting Cumberland’s status as a leading Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) institution in St Catherine, alongside Hydel’s strong culture of sports and academics, the principal noted that the merger offers the perfect opportunity to fulfill his goals.

“Whatever we do in school, it must result in student outcome, the students must be the biggest beneficiary of whatever we do. And so the primary focus is on adding value, value-added education, adding value to the students with respect to their starting point and where they exit. So far we have added more sciences to the curriculum. We have now the traditional sixth form… we have a sports programme to roll out that we are excited about, and so with all of these things it is about the holistic development of the child,” Pitt said.

World.title: Jahshii to embark on islandwide tour; aims to reconnect with his fans
World.content:
JAHSHII...the fanbase a grow and mi just waa continue grow with the fans.

IN a move to reconnect with his fan base, dancehall artiste Jahshii is set to embark on a multi-stop tour across the island in November.

The Born Fighter artiste says the tour will feature performances backed by Tower Band and he’s also bringing along some special guests at each stop.

“The fanbase a grow and mi just waa continue grow with the fans,” he told the Jamaica Observer recently.

“The islandwide tour will kick off in November, and you can expect high-energy performances, special guests at each stop. We’ll be going across the island, and it will be a live music experience like no other,” Jahshii assured.

He added, “We really want to get the fans dem closer, like in an up close and personal vibe, so we have been doing rehearsals while locking in the venues.”

Jahshii, who is best known for songs like Pieces featuring Masicka, Cream of the Crop and

Born Fighter, revealed that it wasn’t an easy journey to get to where he is today.

“Mi a come from nobody naw do nuttin fi mi; a fight wi fight to get up deh. But it is very satisfying to help other emerging talent and see how they develop and make it in the music,” he shared.

Father to a young son, Jahshii says fatherhood has changed his perspective on life.

“It has changed my outlook on life; family comes first and my priorities come first. That’s what we get from being a father,” he shared.

Jahshii’s latest single Auto Pilot, produced by Troublemekka, was released two months ago. He says new music is on the way.

“We definitely have some new music coming especially for the ladies, because we not leaving them out,” he said.

World.title: CPL Hall of Fame award named in honour of Sir Garfield Sobers
World.content:
Garfield Sobers

BRIDGETOWN, Barbados (CMC) — The Republic Bank Caribbean Premier League (CPL) has announced that the trophy presented to each year’s player inducted into its hall of fame will be officially named the Sir Garry Sobers Award, in tribute to the man universally recognised as the greatest all-rounder West Indies cricket has ever produced.

The naming follows the recent launch of the CPL Hall of Fame which will honour two inductees annually, one player and one off-field contributor.

Dwayne Bravo and Ian Bishop were confirmed as the inaugural class, and the CPL has now secured the Sobers family’s blessing to attach Sir Garry’s name to the award, marking one of the most significant moments in the league’s history.

As one of the finest cricketers the game has ever seen and a defining figure of West Indies cricket, Sir Garry’s name gives prestige to the Hall of Fame recognition.

The Sir Garry Sobers Award will be presented for the first time at the CPL Hall of Fame Gala Dinner on September 15, 2026 at the Hilton Barbados.

The evening is being held in support of the Sir Clive Lloyd Healthcare Foundation’s prostate cancer awareness, testing, and early detection work across the Caribbean.

With the trophy carrying Sir Garry’s name the gala brings together two of West Indies cricket’s most respected figures for a single showpiece night in support of the region.

Pete Russell, CEO of CPL, said “Sir Garry Sobers was, without question, the greatest all-rounder the game has ever seen, and having his name on this award means a great deal to everyone at CPL. We are enormously grateful to the Sobers family for trusting us with his name and his legacy. It gives this trophy, and this hall of fame, a weight our players will carry with real pride. To present it for the first time at a gala dinner in support of Sir Clive Lloyd’s Healthcare Foundation makes 15 September an even more prestigious night for West Indies cricket.”

World.title: ‘SPOILT KIDS’
World.content:
RICKETTS... FIFA has supported us and I’ll be very ungrateful not to show some regard, and show some respect, and say thanks to a man that has supported Caribbean football (Photo: Observer file)

JAMAICA Football Federation (JFF) President Michael Ricketts has come to the defence of FIFA President Gianni Infantino, saying he doesn’t deserve the treatment he’s receiving from stakeholders. Ricketts also labeled UEFA “spoilt kids” for its stance against the FIFA boss.

On Sunday, football’s world governing body confirmed that Infantino intends to stand again in next year’s elections for a fourth term, despite mounting criticism over recent months. Infantino proposed selling stakes in FIFA competitions, including the men’s and women’s World Cup, to private investors and offered FIFA’s 211 member associations US$40 million ($6.3 billion) each if they backed the plan.

However, the 56-year-old Swiss ultimately scrapped it following widespread opposition, including European football governing body, UEFA, who voted to boycott all World Cups if it went ahead. Concacaf, who governs North America and the Caribbean, also rejected the proposal.

Infantino, though, attempted to smooth things over with several Concacaf members after attending a Caribbean Football Union (CFU) Presidents’ Meeting and the CFU Under-14 series in the Dominican Republic last month, where Jamaica reached the final. Concacaf President and FIFA Vice-President Victor Montagliani had written to Infantino, asking him not to attend.

Reports from England stated many of the Concacaf members were “infuriated” by Infantino’s behaviour.

However, while not providing the details of the meeting, Ricketts told the Jamaica Observer that the FIFA boss was treated with the utmost respect.

“That’s how reporting and that’s how media is — some people try to sensationalise certain events to suit their own agenda — but that’s the farthest thing from the truth,” he said. “I think Infantino was warmly, warmly welcomed; he was embraced by almost every single CFU member.”

Ricketts, who has served as JFF boss for nearly a decade, admits that Infantino should have approached the proposal differently, although he had no issue with its premise.

“Infantino might have made a mistake, but the intentions were to help Caribbean countries or help smaller countries. Can you imagine Jamaica getting 40 million US dollars to invest in football? Can you imagine the difference that would make in four or five years?” said Ricketts.

“In my very first utterance, I did say that the gesture would suit me but we thought [there] was [a] lack of communication, lack of discussions, it seemed non-transparent. But I don’t think Infantino meant to hurt anybody or would have tried to make himself a beneficiary of the gesture.”

The fallout from the proposal continues Belgium Football Association, on Monday, the latest to oppose Infantino’s re-election. At least 11 other FIFA member associations have publicly withdrawn their support including major European football nations such as England, Germany, Norway and the Netherlands.

UEFA has led calls for Infantino to step down and is preparing legal action against him, accusing the FIFA president of “criminal mismanagement” over the proposal. FIFA, in return, has accused the Euopean governing body of a “smear campaign against it and its leadership”.

Ricketts believes UEFA are being unreasonable and has no intention of following its stance.

“People will have different views and different opinions for different reasons. But I am not supporting UEFA because I think that they always want to be in opposition and always want to oppose. It doesn’t matter who is president, they are going to have issues. It doesn’t matter how well the president does, they are going to have issues and I think that UEFA is behaving like a set of spoilt kids,” he said.

“From a commercial standpoint, they really don’t need FIFA. They probably have as much money as FIFA does so they can do and say anything. I can’t do that because I need support and FIFA has supported us and I’ll be very ungrateful not to show some regard and show some respect and say thanks to a man that has supported Caribbean football.”

More than 20 FIFA member associations, including 2026 World Cup finalists Argentina, World Cup co-host Mexico and African champions Morocco, have publicly expressed support for Infantino .

Ricketts praised Infantino’s performance but says the decision on Jamaica’s support for rests with the JFF board.

“This is something I probably don’t even have the right to speak on because it’s a decision that the board will have to make. But personally, I think Infantino has done a good job,” he said.

The nominations for FIFA presidential candidates must be submitted by November 18. Infantino is currently the only candidate, though Concacaf President Victor Montagliani is being touted as a potential challenger.

World.title: Wedding, Fashion & Interior Design
World.content:
Inspired by the beautifully curated spaces they encounter worldwide, couples are choosing venues like boutique hotels to evoke those same unforgettable feelings on their wedding day. -

New York Fashion Week is upon us, and it got me thinking about how much fashion and interior design influence the wedding industry. We often look at weddings as their own creative world, but they are actually incredibly responsive to what is happening around us. What we wear, how we decorate our homes, the restaurants and hotels we are drawn to, even the way luxury brands present themselves all eventually find their way into weddings.

And increasingly, I think the most interesting weddings are borrowing ideas rather than following wedding trends.

The Runway Has Always Found Its Way to the Aisle

Fashion is perhaps the most obvious influence. What happens on the runways of New York, Paris, Milan and London eventually changes what brides and grooms want to wear, but its influence goes much further than the dress.

The current fashion conversation is full of personality: sculptural silhouettes, interesting textures, dramatic draping, bows, metallics, sheer fabrics, unexpected colour and a renewed appreciation for beautiful tailoring. Those ideas translate remarkably well into weddings.

A beautifully draped fashion silhouette can inspire the treatment of a tent. A couture floral appliqué can become the starting point for an invitation, cake or tablescape. A runway colour combination can suddenly make traditional wedding palettes feel completely different.

Even bridal fashion itself has become less formulaic. Brides are changing looks throughout the celebration, experimenting with shorter dresses, statement accessories, dramatic veils and fashion-forward reception looks. Grooms, too, are embracing more colour, texture and individuality.

Weddings Are Beginning to Look More Like Beautiful Interiors

Interior design is having an even greater influence on weddings.

For years, wedding décor was largely about flowers, linens and centrepieces. Couples are paying attention to chairs, lamps, rugs, bars, shelving, interesting furniture, textured fabrics and architectural details. The lounge is no longer simply somewhere to put a sofa; it can feel like the living room of an incredibly stylish home. Bars are becoming statement pieces. Dinner spaces are layered with lighting and objects in much the same way an interior designer would style a room.

I particularly love the move towards residential-style lighting. Table lamps, shaded pendants and warm pools of light immediately change the feeling of a wedding. They make large spaces feel intimate and give outdoor celebrations a sense of permanence and warmth.

This is where I think the influence of boutique hotels, restaurants and private members’ clubs has become especially important. Couples travel. They dine out. They experience beautifully designed spaces around the world, and naturally they want their celebrations to evoke some of those same feelings.

They may not say, “I want an interior-designed wedding.” They say, “I want it to feel like this hotel in Paris,” or “I loved this restaurant in New York.” That distinction matters.

The New Luxury Is Atmosphere

I think we will continue to see couples becoming more confident about mixing influences — vintage furniture with contemporary florals, fashion-inspired fabrics with traditional tablescapes, chrome against soft linen, sculptural pieces beside organic greenery.

The objective isn’t necessarily for everything to “match.” It is for everything to belong to the same story.

Fashion Is Also Teaching Weddings to Be More Personal

Perhaps my favourite influence from fashion is individuality. For a long time, weddings came with an unwritten formula of what was considered “bridal”. White, blush, certain flowers, certain chairs, certain stationery, certain photographs. That vocabulary has expanded enormously.

Today’s couple can create a wedding that is minimalist, maximalist, tropical, editorial, romantic, architectural, vintage, fashion-forward or wonderfully difficult to categorise.

Looking Beyond the Wedding Industry

As New York Fashion Week begins, I’ll certainly be watching the clothes, but I’ll also be looking at the sets, colour combinations, fabrics, styling and tiny details that make a collection memorable.

Because inspiration doesn’t always arrive labelled “wedding.”

Sometimes it is a handbag. A hotel lobby. A fashion show. A restaurant in another country. A fabric you can’t stop touching. A beautifully designed room. A colour combination you would never have thought to put together.

The best wedding professionals know how to notice those things, reinterpret them and make them relevant to the couple, the location and the celebration. For me, that is where wedding design becomes most exciting.

The future of weddings isn’t simply about following the next wedding trend. It is about looking at the wider world of design, fashion, travel and culture — and asking: how can we turn that inspiration into something that feels entirely our own?

Shikima Hinds

Managing Director

Shikima Hinds Events Concierge

World.title: Documentary on James Bond creator Ian Fleming to premiere at GoldenEye
World.content:
Portrait taken in the early 1960s of Ian Fleming, a British journalist, secret service agent, writer, whose most famous creation was the superhero James Bond, agent 007. (Photo: AFP)

Ian Fleming and the Curse of James Bond, directed by Adam Low, a new feature documentary exploring the life, imagination and enduring legacy of James Bond creator Ian Fleming, will premiere at GoldenEye, Fleming’s former Jamaican home, during the 80th anniversary year of the villa’s construction.

The documentary explores Fleming beyond the legend of 007, considering the contradictions, pressures and fascinations that shaped both the man and the charged literary world he created, according to a press release by Gross Media, which executive produced the project.

Presented at GoldenEye by Gross Media, the premiere weekend – November 19 to November 22, 2026 – brings together biography, place and mythology in a setting deeply connected to the Bond story.

“GoldenEye’s enduring legacy as a center of Jamaican art and creativity is rare and compelling,” said Gross Media founder David M Gross. “So much new has originated here and radiated outward — through music, painting, literature and the performing arts. Our film invites a new generation to come to Oracabessa, St Mary, to understand that legacy and be inspired by it.”

Built in a uniquely Jamaican architectural style, the iconic villa features whitewashed walls, wooden louvers and has no glass windowpanes.

Upon returning from espionage duties during World War II, Fleming built the villa in 1946 on Jamaica’s famed North Coast. GoldenEye became the creative sanctuary where he wrote each of the 12 James Bond nov els and the stories that introduced one of the most recognizable characters in modern popular culture.

Eight decades later, the property remains a living landmark: part legendary literary site, part cultural myth and an enduring symbol of Jamaica’s oversized place in the Bond story and the wider cultural world.

“Fleming built GoldenEye as a place where he could write, and every James Bond novel was written here. Eighty years later, it remains the spiritual birthplace of Bond. To screen a film that looks so closely at Fleming himself, during GoldenEye’s 80th year, is very special,” said Chris Blackwell, Founder, and Marika Kessler, CEO, Island Outpost.

Adam Low, the film’s director, said he was “determined to put Jamaica at the centre of the story” with the project.

“Even the Bond books not set there are infused with the island’s atmosphere, landscape and history. By including Jamaican voices — from Fleming’s longtime gardener Ramsay Dacosta to novelist Marlon James as well as Minister Olivia ‘Babsy’ Grange whose relative Aunt Violet was Fleming’s house manager — the film shows how deeply Jamaica shaped Fleming’s imagination and the world of Bond,” Low said.

“As Minister Grange says in the film, ‘Jamaica is the star of the Bond films,’ and the documentary makes a compelling case that without Jamaica, there would be no James Bond,” said Low, underlining the Jamaican connection.

The perspective of the film deepens the premiere’s connection to GoldenEye by positioning Jamaica not simply as Fleming’s retreat, but as a defining creative force behind Bond’s settings, sensibility and mythology.

“By weaving together Jamaican voices, landscapes and history, the documentary underscores the island’s central place in both Fleming’s imagination and the continuing cultural life of 007,” said film editor Joanna Crickmay.

According to the release, the film’s opening sequence features a moving benediction in the Rastafari tradition by author, journalist and cultural liaison Barbara Blake-Hannah, while driving the vibrant streets through Oracabessa, St Mary, en route to GoldenEye with Desmond Dekker & The Aces’ legendary rocksteady and reggae track “007 (Shanty Town)” on play.

The premiere film weekend will bring guests from around the world to the place where Fleming’s daily writing ritual helped launch the Bond phenomenon, the release stated, adding that the programme includes a screening at PlayScape, a cocktail party at the GoldenEye villa with a Jamaican jazz band, a classic Jamaican BBQ on Button Beach with members of the film’s crew and Ian Fleming-themed morning breakfasts: scrambled eggs, toast, guava jelly, local fruits and Blue Mountain coffee.

Together, the events offer guests a rare opportunity to experience the film in the setting most closely associated with Fleming’s creative life, according to the press release.

World.title: Stronger schools
World.content:
Education Minster Senator Dr Dana Morris Dixon walks with students of Maud McLeod High School in Westmoreland where she filmed her back-to-school message to the nation.

After a school year battered by Hurricane Melissa, particularly in western Jamaica, but capped by improved results in the country’s major examinations, Education Minister Senator Dr Dana Morris Dixon is looking to the new school year with optimism, pointing to increased investment, and stronger infrastructure as Jamaica pushes to transform its education system.

The scale of the challenge facing schools remains stark.

According to Morris Dixon’s back-to-school message, more than 688 schools were damaged by Melissa, 313 of them severely, while almost $26 billion is being spent on repairs and reconstruction. As she has repeatedly done in the past few weeks she acknowledged, however, that the work is not advancing as quickly as the Government would like.

Still, she said preparations were being made to get schools open, including contingency arrangements for institutions where repairs have not yet been completed.

“Thanks to the excellent work of our principals, boards, and the ministry team, we are working to have all schools open tomorrow. I have to thank all who have worked so hard over the summer and who have put in place contingency plans to support reopening even where repairs are not completed,” she said.

For Morris Dixon, however, rebuilding after Melissa is only part of the task.

The Government is entering the new school year with more than $835 million in operational support for schools, representing an average 55 per cent increase in funding. The minister said all schools received the first tranche of the increased funding in June, ahead of the reopening.

More than $1 billion is also being invested in educational resources, including workbooks, readers, textbooks, e-books, virtual learning solutions, and supplementary materials.

The increased spending comes against the backdrop of what Morris Dixon described as a strong finish to the last academic year, despite the disruption caused by the Category 5 storm.

“Despite the historic, once-in- a- 100-year devastation caused by the passage of Hurricane Melissa, we ended the last academic year with improved results across our major exams — PEP, CSEC and CAPE. Jamaica’s children did so well despite so much being thrown at them!” she said.

The minister is now betting on that resilience, alongside new investments, to drive further gains. In her speech she reminded the country of plans already in place.

Among the biggest initiatives is a $400-million investment in technical and vocational education at high schools. Technical high schools are to receive state-of-the-art laboratories in areas including autonomous robotics, renewable energy, virtual welding, electrical engineering, industrial controls, and optoelectronics.

The Government is also retooling science laboratories, while more than 150 satellite systems have been distributed to schools to improve Internet access, with additional devices being procured, particularly for rural institutions.

Morris Dixon said the hurricane recovery programme is similarly being used as an opportunity to improve schools beyond simply repairing the damage.

“Our Melissa reconstruction programme has not only presented an opportunity to make our schools more resilient, but it has also provided an opportunity to upgrade and renovate staffrooms for educators across Jamaica. The Staffroom Renovation Programme covers 74 institutions in the first phase, with work concentrated heavily in the parishes hardest hit by Melissa,” she said.

And while buildings, equipment and technology are central to the push, the minister also highlighted the needs of students outside the classroom.

More than 160,000 students are projected to benefit from the traditional cooked lunch programme, while another 69,000 students in the most challenged schools are expected to receive both breakfast and lunch. Meanwhile, 316 school cooks were trained and received range cook certification over the summer.

Psychosocial and psychological support, including trauma-informed services and Psychological First Aid, will also continue into the new academic year, after being intensified during the previous one.

Morris Dixon said the ambition extends beyond simply getting schools reopened and students back into classrooms.

“The ministry’s commitment is to continue transforming education so that every child, regardless of where they live or their circumstances, has a fair opportunity to learn, grow and succeed,” she said.

World.title: The EU’s Israel dilemma
World.content:
Relations between the EU and Israel have been deeply strained over the war in Gaza. But the bloc is struggling to withstand the allure of Israel’s tech and missile defense prowess.

On today’s show, Zoya Sheftalovich and Ian Wishart discuss how EU capitals are looking again to Israel for cooperation on things like air defense, space and artificial intelligence. Our hosts explain why this is an awkward look for the bloc.

Then, two years after Mario Draghi’s competitiveness report, we break down how much of his plan Europe has actually delivered.

World.title: Geheimdienst-Dilemma: Der Staat und das AfD-Risiko
World.content:
Was passiert, wenn eine AfD-geführte Landesregierung Zugang zu streng geheimen Geheimdienstinformationen bekommt? Nach dem Wahlsieg in Sachsen-Anhalt wächst die Sorge vor möglichen Daten Abflüssen zum Beispiel nach Russland, sollte die AfD wirklich eine Regierung bilden und damit in Ämter kommen können . Während die Verfassungsschutzchefs in Köln über Informationssperren beraten, analysiert Rasmus Buchsteiner den sicherheitspolitischen Ernst der Lage. Mehr dazu hat Philipp Woldin von WELT dazu hier aufgeschrieben.

Im 200-Sekunden-Interview warnt Marc Henrichmann, Chef des Parlamentarischen Kontrollgremiums, vor politischem Aktionismus. Der CDU-Abgeordnete erklärt, warum er eine spezielle „Lex AfD“ beim Geheimschutz ablehnt und wie die Demokratie ihre sensibelsten Bereiche stattdessen absichern muss.

Ein falscher Klick mit fatalen Folgen: Kilian Hocke von POLITICO PRO „Technologie und KI am Morgen“ berichtet, wie ein simpler Phishing-Trick der hochsensible Daten zuerst bei Erpressern und dann im Darknet landen ließ.
