World.title: South Africa economy shrinks ahead of local elections
World.content:
Johannesburg – South Africa’s economy shrank in the second quarter of 2026, snapping a nearly two-year growth streak as the war in Iran weighed on domestic demand, the national statistics agency said Tuesday.

The contraction comes less than two months before local government elections, putting the country’s sluggish economy squarely in the political crosshairs.

Gross domestic product fell 0.2 percent from the previous quarter on a seasonally adjusted basis, StatsSA said.

Mining was the biggest drag, shrinking three percent as production of platinum-group metals, manganese, gold and iron ore fell.

Trade contracted 1.9 percent, ending six straight quarters of growth, while manufacturing posted a third consecutive decline, with seven of its 10 divisions reporting weaker output.

The weakness was compounded by rising imports and a second consecutive quarterly decline in investment, as exports grew only modestly and businesses and public corporations pulled back on capital spending.

In June, StatsSA warned that the fallout from the conflict in the Middle East, which erupted in late February and sent fuel prices soaring early in the year, could weigh on second-quarter economic activity.

The economy is expected to feature prominently in November’s local government elections, with unemployment remaining stubbornly high at more than 33 percent, among the highest rates in the world.

Years of weak growth have added to frustration with the government.

Africa’s richest economy shed 345,000 jobs in the second quarter, with most of the losses coming in the community and social services sector.

The economic malaise has deepened disillusionment with the ruling African National Congress, which lost its national majority in 2024 for the first time since the end of apartheid and was forced into an uneasy coalition government with rival parties.

World.title: Iraq advances Chevron, UCC-backed pipeline to Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq is pushing forward with a vital oil pipeline project with US energy company Chevron, TI Capital, and Qatar’s UCC, which would link Basra to Fishkhabur and branch west toward Syria’s Mediterranean port of Baniyas, Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair said Tuesday.

Khudair said at the start of the fourth Iraq Oil and Gas Projects and Licensing Rounds Exhibition that the project is critical to Baghdad’s efforts to diversify export routes and provide Iraqi petroleum more flexibility in reaching global markets.

He said that Iraq is working with a consortium of US corporations, including Chevron and TI Capital, as well as its Qatari partner UCC, to build the Basra-Fishkhabur connection and its planned branch to Baniyas.

The route would be especially important for Iraq since the majority of its petroleum exports now depart from southern Arabian Gulf terminals and go via the Strait of Hormuz.

A link between Basra and the Mediterranean would give an alternate outlet during times of difficulty.

The initiative comes as US President Donald Trump has publicly emphasized the construction of new oil pipelines in the Middle East.

Speaking at the White House last week, Trump applauded the trucking of Iraqi oil toward Syria’s Mediterranean coast and said that “many oil pipelines” were being constructed in the area.

Baghdad is also building its northern export route. Khudair said that a deal with Turkey would assist in revitalizing and developing Iraq’s northern exit, complementing the projected routes to Baniyas and providing the nation with several export possibilities.

The Minister said that Iraq’s larger goal goes beyond pipelines to increase production and exports, enhance refining capacity, develop gas resources, and reduce flaring, all while attracting foreign investment and boosting Iraqi energy firms.

According to Khudair, Iraq’s oil exports increased to over 3 million barrels per day in September, up from roughly 200,000 bpd when the present administration took office.

He also revealed that Japan’s JGC has decided to return to Iraq after discussions with the ministry to begin work on the FCC project at the southern refineries, which is part of Baghdad’s aim to enhance local refined petroleum product output.

Khudair said that the government’s ultimate goal is to achieve self-sufficiency in petroleum products, use more of its gas domestically, and eventually grow exports of higher-value refined goods.

Meanwhile, Iraq has maintained its commitment to meeting its OPEC production targets, with output not anticipated to surpass 4.2 million barrels per day.

World.title: Turkish Airlines will be new Liverpool shirt sponsor in £300 mn deal
World.content:
London – Turkish Airlines will become Liverpool’s new front-of-shirt sponsor from the start of the 2027/28 season, the Premier League giants announced on Tuesday.

No fee was disclosed by the club, but the BBC reported that the five-year deal was worth £300 million ($406 million) in total.

A contract worth more than £60 million a season, would represent an increase on the current £50 million-per-season deal with retail bank Standard Chartered, who have been the Reds’ front-of-shirt sponsor since 2010.

Liverpool’s new deal is believed to be the most lucrative purely front-of-shirt agreement in Premier League history, with Arsenal and Manchester City’s agreements with Emirates and Etihad Airways respectively also involving stadium naming rights.

By contrast, six-time European champions Liverpool’s home ground is still solely known by its original name of Anfield.

In February, Liverpool announced record revenues of more than £700 million for the most recent financial year, and were the highest-placed Premier League club in the Deloitte Football Money League.

Liverpool were the first major English professional football club to have a shirt sponsor, when Japanese electronics company Hitachi had its name displayed across the club’s strip back in 1979.

Standard Chartered will remain as the shirt sponsor this season before becoming a “global partner” of Liverpool from 2027/28 onwards.

It is understood that talks with Turkish Airlines started before 1892 Holdings — a consortium led by British-Indian millionaire businessman Amit Bhatia, the Liverpool vice-chairman, purchased a stake of around 38 percent in the club last month.

Chief commercial officer Ben Latty said that the front of the shirt “holds a special place in the history” of Liverpool, adding that the partnership will build on “strong foundations” from the club’s Champions League final win in the Turkish city of Istanbul in 2005.

Turkish Airlines chief executive Ahmet Olmustur said: “This partnership brings together two global brands united by their international reach, commitment to excellence and ability to inspire millions of people around the world.”

Turkey’s national flag carrier boasts that it flies to 356 destinations in 132 countries. A pet soft-power project of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, the company is controlled by the country’s wealth fund, which owns 49.1 percent of its shares.

The company’s network centres on Istanbul airport, which overtook London Heathrow as Europe’s busiest airport in the July summer peak with more than eight million travellers.

World.title: South Lebanon town buries its dead after Israeli strike
World.content:
Kfar Rumman – Hundreds of people in south Lebanon gathered on Tuesday to mourn two Hezbollah members and their family, among them a three-month-old infant, killed by an Israeli strike a day prior.

The two brothers’ coffins, draped in the Iran-backed group’s yellow flag, portraits of them in camouflage fatigues fixed to the front, led the procession through the village battered by repeated conflict over nearly three years.

Another 10 coffins were covered in Lebanese flags, indicating that the rest of the Farhat family killed when Monday’s strike levelled their home were civilians.

Israel has launched airstrikes and a ground invasion in south Lebanon during the Middle East war, which erupted with joint US-Israeli attacks on Iran and spread to Lebanon after Hezbollah targeted Israel in support of its backer.

The fighting in Lebanon had calmed since a US-Iran memorandum of understanding and a framework agreement between Israel and Lebanon were both agreed in June.

But Beirut still reports recurring Israeli strikes, which it says have killed more than 4,300 people in total since March, and Israeli forces continue to occupy what it calls a “security zone” in the south.

A separate strike on Kfar Rumman on Monday killed an 18-year-old rescuer with the Risala Association, linked to the Hezbollah-allied Amal movement, the organisation said, who was mourned alongside the Farhat family on Tuesday.

“We have 13 killed including grandfather and grandmother, husbands and wives, and their children including a three-months old infant,” deputy mayor Nureddine Nureddine told AFP from the funeral.

“Someone put an end to these crimes,” Nureddine said, adding that the strike that killed the Farhat family “occurred at night, while they were sleeping”.

“There was no military activity, nothing.”

An AFP correspondent saw people marching to the cemetery, waving Hezbollah flags as women dressed in black wept, holding pictures of the dead as an Israeli drone flew overhead.

“Death to America, death to Israel,” mourners yelled.

– ‘A shred of honour’ –

The Israeli military said on Monday that it had struck Hezbollah “infrastructure sites” across southern Lebanon after the launch of two explosive drones towards its troops, as well as “several terrorists” it said were transferring weapons.

“The claim that several uninvolved individuals were harmed as a result of the strikes is being reviewed,” it said, adding that the military “will continue to operate to remove threats while remaining committed to the ceasefire agreement”.

Since Friday, at least 28 people have been killed in Israeli attacks on southern Lebanon, according to Lebanon’s health ministry.

Standing next to a picture of his own son, a Hezbollah member killed by Israel, Ghaleb Baalbaki slammed the Lebanese government for continuing direct talks with Israel.

“If they have even a shred of honour, the first thing they should do would be to stop the negotiations,” he said.

The lull in violence that began in June had allowed hundreds of thousands of displaced people to return home.

“Kfar Rumman was coming back to life, there were more than 1,400 people” in the town before the latest escalation, Nureddine said,

“Now, they can be counted on your fingers.”

World.title: West Qurna-2 staff threaten strike over dues, risking 324K bpd output
World.content:
Basra (IraqiNews.com) — Dozens of technical, engineering, and administrative personnel operating at the giant West Qurna-2 oilfield in Basra Governorate demonstrated on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, demanding the regularization of their contractual status and the disbursement of overdue wages and entitlements, warning of a general strike if their demands are not addressed within one week.

Speaking a local news agency, protest representative Mashreq Abdul-Moneim declared that Basra Oil Company (BOC) and the operating consortium have been formally notified of the one-week ultimatum. Failure to reach an administrative settlement risks triggering an immediate shutdown of extraction and export infrastructure across one of the country’s most critical hydrocarbon assets.

Core Grievances and Operational Demands

Binding Employment Contracts: Protesters demand formal labor contracts that safeguard statutory benefits, matching the legal and operational standards previously established under Russian operator Lukoil.

Settlement of Financial Arrears: Demonstrators call for the immediate liquidation of all outstanding monetary arrears owed to staff by Basra Oil Company (BOC) without further administrative deferral.

One-Week Strike Ultimatum: Operating staff issued a seven-day deadline to operating partners and state managers, after which personnel intend to stage an open-ended work stoppage.

Disruption to Strategic Production: Abdul-Moneim warned that unresolved labor disputes directly threaten field logistics, where current crude extraction stands at roughly 324,000 barrels per day (bpd) and export volumes reach approximately 347,000 bpd.

West Qurna-2 Operational & Labor Risk Profile

Parameter Current Metric / Indicator Risk Scenario Field Location Northern Basra Governorate Strategic onshore super-giant reservoir Current Crude Output ~324,000 bpd Complete shutdown in case of full operational strike Current Export Volume ~347,000 bpd Severe disruption to southern maritime export streams Operator Framework Lukoil consortium / Basra Oil Company (BOC) Dispute centers on contract parity and state arrears Labor Deadline 7-day formal ultimatum (September 15, 2026) Staged escalations leading to general walkout

West Qurna-2 represents a major pillar of southern crude flows feeding into the Basra Oil Terminal for Basra Medium and Heavy grades. Any labor-induced operational halt would remove over 300,000 bpd from Iraq’s seaborne supply, directly undermining export schedules and tightening the state’s hard-currency revenue streams during a period of acute macroeconomic scrutiny.

World.title: Police clash with degree holders outside Finance Ministry in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Demonstrations organized by long-term university graduates, top-ranking achievers, and higher degree holders turned violent outside the Ministry of Finance in central Baghdad on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, marking the second straight day of confrontations over central public appointments in the draft 2027 federal budget.

Riot police and law enforcement units deployed batons, electric stun devices, tear gas canisters, and rubber rounds to repel hundreds of protestors marching toward the ministry’s perimeter gates. Demonstrators, some wearing burial shrouds to signal resolve, represented a demographic bloc estimating over 100,000 unemployed graduates from past academic cycles across Iraq’s governorates.

Demonstrator Demands and On-the-Ground Clashes

Central Employment Quotas in 2027 Budget: Demonstrators demand the statutory inclusion of centralized recruitment allocations and public service civil numbers for older graduating cohorts within the forthcoming 2027 Federal Budget Law.

Scale of the Crisis: Mobilization organizers emphasized that the national backlog of unhired graduates spans more than 100,000 degree holders across disciplines—some holding computer engineering and technical credentials dated as far back as 2014 without public sector absorption.

Security Escalation and Use of Crowd Control: Protesters reported physical assaults with clubs, electric stun guns, and tear gas. A security source confirmed that while live ammunition was strictly withheld, anti-riot police deployed smoke bombs, tear gas canisters, and rubber bullets to maintain security perimeters.

Arterial Highway Blockades: Following friction on Monday, security forces cordoned off approaches to the strategic Mohammed Al-Qasim Expressway after protesters threatened to shut down the arterial transit route.

Key Incident Parameters

Parameter Operational Detail Protest Location Ministry of Finance Headquarters, Central Baghdad Participant Profile Long-term graduates (2014+), top achievers, master’s/PhD holders Estimated Demographic 100,000+ unabsorbed graduates nationwide Core Legislative Demand Statutory civil service quotas / contractual hiring in the 2027 Budget Crowd Control Tactics Smoke grenades, tear gas, electric stun devices, rubber rounds Key Transport Disruptions Mohammed Al-Qasim Expressway approach closures

The unrest flared despite an executive directive issued on Monday by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, instructing the Ministry of Finance to audit actual ministerial staffing requirements and allocate civil or contractual appointments for older graduates in the upcoming federal budget.

However, demonstrators deemed the directive conditional and inadequate without fixed legislative quotas. The crisis underscores the chronic fiscal dilemma confronting Baghdad: while public compensation and social transfers already swallow an average of 7.438 trillion IQD monthly from the federal treasury, severe private sector employment deficits continue to channel intense popular pressure directly toward state payrolls.

World.title: Baghdad drivers queue for hours as gasoline supplies run low
World.content:
Baghdad — Drivers formed long lines outside fuel stations in Baghdad on Saturday as gasoline supplies dropped in oil-rich Iraq due to import disruptions caused by the Middle East war.

Despite being OPEC’s second largest oil producer, Iraq imports oil derivatives because its refineries do not produce enough gasoline to meet domestic demand.

In recent weeks, as regional hostilities drag on, long queues have been reappearing every few days, mostly outside government-run fuel stations in Baghdad and other provinces.

Baghdad resident Ibrahim Hashem waited for two hours outside a fuel station on Friday without any luck, only to return early the next day hoping to fill his car.

“It is unreasonable that we produce so many barrels of oil a day, yet still do not have enough gasoline to meet our daily needs,” Hashem told AFP outside a fuel station in central Baghdad.

“We already suffer from traffic congestion because of the roads and lack of services. Now, it has become worse due to the gasoline shortage,” he added.

Iraq’s average daily consumption of gasoline is 33 million liters, but demand rises to 38 million when people panic over shortages, according to authorities.

The oil ministry said Friday that “regional events and the ongoing conflict are causing logistical challenges to tanker traffic, delaying their arrival at Iraqi ports.”

It urged citizens to buy only the quantities they need and avoid crowding fuel stations for small amounts of gasoline.

Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair said on Friday that his ministry was addressing the “temporary shortage of gasoline” and that new shipments will arrive soon to help stabilize supplies.

Like other oil producers, Iraq has been greatly affected by the US-Iran conflict, which has choked off the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

Iraq is hugely dependent on oil exports, which make up about 90 percent of its budget revenues.

Before the war erupted in February, Iraq produced around four million barrels per day, and exported an average of 3.4 million bpd, mostly via Hormuz.

After a significant drop, Iraqi oil exports recovered to more than 2.2 million bpd in August, according to the oil ministry.

Last month, Iran’s state news agency IRNA said that over the past six months, Tehran has granted permission to “a number of Iraqi oil tankers” to pass through Hormuz.

World.title: Iraq rules out airspace closure, launches 9 international routes
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi Ministry of Transport ruled out any imminent closure of national airspace amid regional security tensions, announcing the successful activation of alternative air transit corridors alongside the launch of nine new international flight destinations connecting Baghdad, Kirkuk, and Basra to regional and global hubs.

Speaking to the official state newspaper reported on Tuesday, September 8, 2026, the Director General of the General Company for Airport Management and Air Navigation, Ihab Saad, affirmed that Iraq’s flight information region (FIR) remains safe, stable, and fully operational, logging over 500,000 passengers during the third quarter of 2026 alone.

Airspace Stability and Navigation Measures

Alternative Air Corridors: In technical collaboration with international civil aviation bodies (including ICAO), the ministry established flexible alternate transit routes to bypass regional friction zones, with technical evaluations underway to open additional corridors.

Continuous Open Skies: Saad stressed that Iraqi airspace did not experience any operational closures over recent months despite sharp regional escalations, maintaining uninterrupted overflight transit revenues and commercial passenger flows.

Overflight Readiness: Authorities maintain direct operational coordination with transit carriers, anticipating a return to historical direct flight paths as regional de-escalation takes hold.

Q3 2026 Passenger Milestone: Robust passenger throughput surpassed 500,000 travelers across domestic airports in Q3 2026, underscoring sustained commercial confidence in Iraqi civil aviation infrastructure.

The Ministry of Transport’s civil aviation expansion program establishes direct point-to-point connections across three key domestic gateways:

Departure Airport New International Routes Strategic Corridor Baghdad International Airport (BGW) Moscow, Tunis, Muscat Eastern Europe, North Africa & GCC integration Kirkuk International Airport (KIK) Antalya, Beirut, Dubai, Trabzon Tourism hubs, Levant link & GCC transit Basra International Airport (BSR) Baku, Delhi South Caucasus trade & South Asian commercial link

Saad noted that routing alternatives and destination additions form part of a structured civil aviation strategy to maximize sovereign revenue from overflight transit fees and airport usage charges:

World.title: Congress alleges US pressure after NIA drops UAPA charges against VanDyke
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress on Wednesday accused the Centre of being "pressurised" by the United States after the National Investigating Agency did not invoke the provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) in its chargesheet against US national Matthew Aaron VanDyke and six Ukrainian nationals.

In a social media post on X, Congress leader Jairam Ramesh questioned whether the central probing agency dropped the charges after a proper investigation or whether the decision was taken due to pressure from the Centre at the instance of US authorities.

"Did NIA drop the terror charges against the US national Matthew VanDyke after a proper investigation or was it pressurised to do so right away by the Modi Govt at the instance of the US authorities? What is pro quo that India expects for this quid?" Jairam Ramesh said.

"This appears to be bullying," he added.

Earlier on Friday, NIA filed a chargesheet against six Ukrainian nationals and US citizen VanDyke in a case registered by the agency in March 2026. The case was initially registered under the UAPA. However, the UAPA provision has not been invoked in the chargesheet filed by the agency.

The NIA's Special Public Prosecutor (SPP) said that the investigation in this regard is still ongoing and the agency may file a supplementary chargesheet if an offence under the UAPA is made out.





The NIA has invoked Sections 21 and 23 of the Foreigners Act in the chargesheet. These are compoundable offences at the level of the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO). The chargesheet was filed before Special NIA Judge Prashant Sharma, who has listed the matter for consideration on October 1.

The seven accused were arrested in connection with allegations of training ethnic armed groups in Myanmar that were allegedly inimical to India's national security.

The NIA had arrested Matthew Aaron Van Dyke (US citizen) and Ukrainian nationals Hurba Petro, Slyviak Taras, Ivan Sukmanovskyi, Stefankiv Marian, Honcharuk Maksim and Kaminskyi Viktor.

VanDyke, a self-described combat specialist and founder of the security firm Sons of Liberty International (SOLI), was arrested at Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport on March 13, around 9 pm, as part of a coordinated crackdown.

World.title: 'Crushing those who question': Rahul Gandhi demands Punjab FM's resignation over Gulzar Singh’s death
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition

on Wednesday accused Aam Aadmi Party of "crushing those who question" the Punjab government after a man died by suicide following alleged pressure to apologise for publicly questioning the state's finance minister over the drug menace in the state.

In a social media post on X, Rahul said Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann should immediately demand his minister Harpal Singh Cheema's resignation and ensure an independent and impartial investigation.

"A dangerous pattern is emerging in Punjab's AAP government - if you question government failures, the response will come in the form of threats and torture," Rahul said.

"Gulzar Singh ji, from the Dalit community, who had to watch his son fall victim to drugs, asked the finance minister just this much: why has the government failed so miserably in stopping the drug trade? For just this, he was tortured and humiliated so much, pressured so intensely to apologise, that he consumed poison.

Wandering from one hospital to another, without access to treatment, he ultimately lost the battle for his life," he added.

He said the government's job is to answer to the people, "not to crush those who ask questions".

"Last week, I also spoke with a young Mohanjeet Singh, who was tortured for protesting against chief minister Bhagwant Mann," Rahul said.

"The government's job is to answer to the people, not to crush those who ask questions.





May Gulzar Singh ji's family get justice as soon as possible. The chief minister should immediately demand the finance minister's resignation and ensure an independent and impartial investigation, with his name registered in the FIR," he added.

A controversy erupted after a 47-year-old man, Gulzar Singh, from Sangrur allegedly died by suicide, with his family claiming that he was asked to apologise and subjected to casteist slurs for questioning finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema over the "unabated" supply of 'chitta' in his area at an event on September 6.

Singh died on Monday night after allegedly consuming poison, his family members said.

A purported video of Gulzar's last moments surfaced in which he spoke about questioning the finance minister, prompting opposition parties to demand the resignations of Cheema as well as Mann.

World.title: Indians trust the classroom, see better opportunities abroad: Global survey
World.content:
Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani.

Not because the Ipsos Education Monitor survey mirrors the plot of the Shah Rukh Khan-Juhi Chawla film, but because the title neatly captures the contradiction in its India findings.

Indians may believe better opportunities for growth and prosperity lie offshore, yet they remain remarkably bullish about their education system, their degrees and, above all, the future of their youth.

More than half of Indian respondents rate the countryâs education system as good. Three-fourths believe youth will have a better life than their parents. Nearly two-thirds think even young people from lesser privileged backgrounds have a bright future.

And Indians remain strikingly convinced that a university degree still has value. However, ironically, 76% of Indian respondents say young people would have better opportunities by moving abroad.

For some parameters, TOI looked at the subset of Indiaâs position among the 16 individual G20 member countries included in the 31-country Ipsos survey. China, Russia and Saudi Arabia were not surveyed. The survey covered 23,537 online adults across the 31 countries between June and July 2026, with about 1,000 respondents in India.





Ipsos in its methodology has cautioned that its India sample is more urban, educated and/or affluent than the general population and should be interpreted as reflecting the views of the countryâs more âconnectedâ segment.The 31-country average is an unweighted average of country results; it is not adjusted for the population size of each country.

The robust belief in education, with a rider

The first question was straightforward. How do people rate the overall quality of their countryâs education system? In India, 51% called it good.

Among the G20 countries covered by the survey, only Australia was higher, at 53%. The 31-country average was 33%. But that 51% is a number in retreat. India was at 65% in 2025, 69% in 2024 and 55% in 2023. The 14-point fall from 2025 is the steepest year-on-year decline among countries with comparable 2025 data.

Education confidence chart

The contrast with several richer economies is sharp. Britain was at 43%, the US and Brazil at 32%, Italy at 29%, Japan at 24%, while France and Germany were both at 17%.

That does not mean India has a better-performing education system than advanced economies. This is a matter of perception. And on that measure, Indians appear unusually confident. Just less than before.

Optimism about Yuva Shakti

The gap becomes even more striking when the question shifts from institutions to the people coming out of them. Asked whether young people in their country have a bright future, 72% of Indian respondents agreed. That was not merely the highest figure among the G20 countries covered.

It was the highest among all 31 countries surveyed. The 31-country average was 45%.

Highest youth optimism score

Within the surveyed G20 set, Australia and South Africa were next at 54%, followed by Mexico at 52% and Canada at 50%. France was at 22%. It is perhaps one of the strongest votes of confidence in the survey. Indians appear to have placed enormous hope in their youth to put the country on the right track and take it forward.

The Indian dream remains intergenerational

One of the hallmarks of an aspirational society like India is the belief in accumulating wealth and opportunity across generations.

People believe that the hard work of one generation will make the lives of those that follow smoother. That belief gets backed in this survey. Three-fourths of Indian respondents, 75%, believe young people today will have a better life than their parents. The 31-country average is 48%.

India's faith on future

Indians are also optimistic about people escaping the poverty trap. 64% believe young people from poorer backgrounds have a bright future, compared with a 31-country average of 40%.

India is the highest among the G20 countries covered on both measures. And 69% of Indian respondents believe the education system contributes to reducing social inequalities, again the highest among the surveyed G20 countries. That figure is also below earlier readings, 72% in 2024 and 79% in 2023.

Together, these numbers suggest that Indian respondents continue to see education as a vehicle for upward social mobility.

That belief becomes even clearer when the survey turns to higher education.

In India, the college degree has not lost its promise

âs recent

Reimagining Skilling

for Viksit Bharat@2047

also points to the continuing pull of degree programmes, noting that vocational pathways are often not seen as credible, growth-oriented alternatives and that degrees can become the safer choice amid limited counselling, social bias and low trust in existing skill systems. The Ipsos survey, albeit with a more urban and connected Indian sample, points in a similar direction.

75% of Indian respondents say a college or university degree is very important to succeed in life.

78% believe it helps people go further in their careers. And 70% say degrees in their country offer good value for money.

Bullish on college degree

On the first measure, India is the highest among the G20 countries surveyed. On both the other measures, it ranks second. The contrast with several advanced economies is large. On whether a degree is good value for money, Indiaâs 70% compares with 38% in the US, 41% in Germany, 30% in Japan and 28% in Britain.

Ipsos itself finds a strong positive relationship across countries between believing that a degree helps a career and believing that it offers value for money.

India trusts the curriculum, yet worries about the jobs connection

Here again, the Ipsos study broadly aligns with a concern flagged in

that education and credentials do not automatically translate into the skills and pathways that the labour market demands. The Ipsos survey shows a deep-seated faith in formal education and yet a growing realisation that job-market demands are at times different from what is being taught in the classroom.

Asked whether the school curriculum adequately prepares students for future careers, 67% of Indians agree, the highest share among the G20 countries covered by the survey. Even here, the direction has been downward: 74% agreed in 2024, 72% in 2025 and 67% now.

Education-Jobs paradox

Yet in another question on the greatest challenges facing young people, 36% of Indian respondents select âeducation and training systems not matching labour market demandsâ.

That too is the highest among the G20 countries in the survey.

A bright future. Somewhere else?

India again falls on one extreme of a scatter plot for its two seemingly contradictory sets of beliefs. On one hand, 72% say young people have a bright future. On the other hand, 76% say young people would have better opportunities by moving abroad. The 31-country average on that question is 62%.

Indonesia and South Africa are even more likely to say opportunities are better overseas, at 87% and 80% respectively.

Italy is at 79%. Romania matches India at 76%. But none combines that level of outward-looking aspiration with Indiaâs exceptional optimism about the future of its young.

Hope at home, opportunity abroad

This is perhaps the central finding of the entire report for India. Respondents may be optimistic about Indiaâs young people precisely because they believe those young people possess education and skills that give them more options, including the option of leaving.

The optimism may be about the people. The doubt may be about the location of opportunity.

Social media? Restrict it. AI? Not necessarily

The dichotomy in the approach of Indians extends to technology too. 78% support banning social media for children under 14, both inside and outside school. The 31-country average is 73%.Support has climbed 10 points in a year. India was at 68% in 2025 and 73% in 2024.

On smartphones, 57% of Indian respondents favour a ban in schools, exactly matching the 31-country average.

That is up from 50% last year and 52% in 2024. But attitudes to AI are different.

On use of AI

Only 26% of Indian respondents say AI, including ChatGPT, should be banned in schools, compared with 39% across the 31 countries. Indian opinion on AI has moved sharply over the four editions of the survey. 39% wanted AI banned in schools in both 2025 and 2024, compared with just 16% in 2023. The 13-point drop from 2025 to 2026 is the largest year-on-year fall among countries with comparable 2025 data.

Britain, the US and Poland moved in the other direction, rising to 52%, 56% and 46%, respectively.

To sum up, Indiaâs âconnectedâ population has not lost faith in education. Quite the opposite. It remains unusually convinced that education matters, degrees pay, children can surpass their parents and those from poorer homes can climb. What appears less certain is where that promise will ultimately be realised.

Karmabhoomi

and

janmabhoomi

may finally be different. That is the sobering realisation one can derive from this survey.

World.title: Delhi HC raps Centre for outing survivor's name in its POSH handbook
World.content:

Handbook is âeverywhere and anywhereâ on internet: Lawyer

NEW DELHI: Delhi HC rapped Centre for naming a workplace sexual harassment survivor in a handbook it published on preventing such harassment and dealing with complaints.âHow is the name of the victim disclosed in this? How can you do that? You are the govt of India. You yourself are publishing (handbooks) revealing the name of the victim and you are circulating it. It is on your official website,â Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma said, listing the matter for the next hearing on Wednesday.Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) handbook was published by Ministry of Women and Child Development. Law prohibits revealing the identity of the survivor of a sexual offence, and doing so is a punishable offence.HC asked Union govtâs lawyer to come back with the names of officials âresponsible for this contentâ while hearing a petition by the alleged perpetrator, who submitted that the matter has since been settled and therefore, sought directions for removal of his name from the handbook.The petitionerâs counsel submitted that a labour tribunal order arising from the alleged incident has been included in the handbook as an anecdote, revealing the details of not only his identity but the womanâs name as well.The handbook is âeverywhere and anywhereâ on the internet, the lawyer said. that the Centreâs counsel submitted that the handbook was published in Nov 2015 for educational purposes, and the parties settled the matter only recently.âSo will it reveal the name of the victim? Even a judgement cannot,â Justice Sharma responded. âFor educational purposes you donât need the victimâs name, right? Even the judges write âXâ. There are directions of high court. You canât disclose the name. Now it is punishable,âHC reminded the counsel as it added that judicial directions to protect a survivorâs identity were in place even before 2015 and the authorities cannot be absolved of their responsibility to follow the law even if a party was acting on it now. The petitioner also sought directions to Google for de-linking and de-indexing the content.

MUMBAI: PM Narendra Modi Tuesday called for India to set its own standards and protocols for cross-border payments and directly integrate its payment system with countries where Indian diaspora populations are large and trade volumes significant.He said India now had a sovereign alternative to the foreign standards under-pinning the existing card-payment architecture and could connect it with the global financial system.Modi said the move could also reduce the cost of remittances, noting that Indians abroad send the largest volume of money home globally but lose a notable portion to transaction fees. âUPI can deliver substantial savings here as well, allowing funds to reach Indian families far more rapidly,â he said.His remarks came ahead of the Brics summit, where expanding national and local currency trade is a priority. A proposal seeks to enable retail and trade-settlement interoperability between fast-payment systems by linking UPI with similar networks in other countries. India has been looking at ways to reduce reliance on the dollar for cross-currency trade while Brics has stopped short of referring to the dollar, with the 2025 declaration calling for finding âacceptable mechanisms of financing in local currenciesâ.âWe have already accomplished this with Singapore. As a result, cross-border transactions between India and Singapore occur as seamlessly as transfers between two neighbourhoods of the same city. We must replicate these integrations across other countries and international markets,â the PM said.Addressing Global Fintech Fest for the third consecutive year, Modi said India had gr-own 7.8% despite pressure on energy and commodity supply chains and escalating trade tensions. He also cited a Japanese ratings agency upgrading India to the A category, a milestone achieved after three decades. âThis reflects how confident the world has become in the structural reforms implemented over the past years. And I reiterate: Indiaâs âReform Expressâ will advance at an even faster pace,â he said.The PM called for stronger cybersecurity, industry-led ethical data-protection stand-ards, a regulatory-industry innovation ecosystem and a fintech consumer-protection index with clear and transparent ratings. He also said the sector needed to diversify beyond payments by expanding credit, insurance, savings, investments and pension products.Noting that Global Fintech Fest coincided with UPIâs 10th anniversary, Modi said those excluded from formal banking for generations were now driving fintech growth.He said SVANidhi credit cards had brought street vendors into the formal credit system by giving them a verifiable tool for access. Studies, he said, showed average annual income among PM SVANidhi beneficiaries had risen by over 20%.Noting that besides fintech energy, Mumbaiâs cultural energy was also at its peak thanks to Ganeshotsav festivities around the corner, Modi extended warm wishes. Attending the annual fest for the third consecutive time, Modi said, would be his second âhat trickâ â the first being in 2024 when NDA formed govt for a third time.

World.title: Eiffel Tower shuts after staff strike over BAPS visit
World.content:
Eiffel Tower in Paris was closed to visitors Monday after staff suddenly went on strike, alleging that female employees were moved from their stations during a visit by a delegation from a Gujarat-based Hindu religious group.

A 100-strong delegation linked to Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) had visited Eiffel Tower ahead of Festival of Cultures, marking the consecration of a Swaminarayan Temple in Paris over the weekend.

PTI quoted workers' union representative Diane Davoine as saying women members of the staff were asked to leave their stations as the delegation arrived at the tourism landmark. Confederation Generale du Travail, a national forum of trade unions, alleged that in some cases, women employees were temporarily replaced by male colleagues and told to avoid particular areas till the religious delegation left.

The operating company, Societe d'Exploitation de la tour Eiffel (SETE), said the tower reopened as usual on Tuesday, acknowledging that a BAPS delegation had requested "limited interactions with women" and that the condition "should not have been accepted".

BAPS issued a detailed statement insisting the arrangements were never gender-based. It said the visit was coordinated in advance purely for logistical reasons.





"Given the size of the group, this visit was coordinated in advance with the Eiffel Tower's management team and was scheduled at the start of normal operating hours specifically to minimise any disruption to staff, other visitors, and the site's regular functioning.

" MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the matter was purely between the entities concerned.

BAPS regretted any inconvenience caused to employees by the arrangements.

"We take seriously the concerns expressed by the Eiffel Tower's employees, and we sincerely regret any inconvenience or discomfort caused to them as a result of the arrangements made for our group's visit."

Paris mayor Emmanuel Gregoire called the employees' anger legitimate. National Assembly President Yael Braun-Pivet said women in France fully occupy public spaces and cannot be told to make themselves invisible. Gender equality minister Aurore Berge called the episode unacceptable, saying no religion is above the Republic's laws. Former PM Gabriel Attal backed Tower's staff, saying no culture or belief can dictate a woman's place.

NEW DELHI: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has summoned Meta India's managing director and country head to appear before it on Wednesday over s allegedly linked to child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) on Instagram.NCPCR commission took suo motu cognisance of a BBC Eye report and issued a notice to Meta Platforms Inc on July 3, seeking an explanation and documents. Meta replied a week later, following which the NCPCR instituted a formal inquiry to establish the facts.Commission officials remained tight-lipped about Meta's response. However, they said the inquiry would examine Meta India's role in the appearance of the s, how they cleared Instagram's systems and why the situation arose.The scrutiny would consider the stringent provisions relating to such material under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, they added.Last week, NHRC issued notices to the ministry of electronics and information technology and ministry of information and broadcasting as part of its scrutiny of alleged CSAM on Instagram. An NHRC member Priyank Kanoongo, whose bench issued the notices Sept 2, said the inquiry was no longer only identifying who uploaded the content. "It also examines the extent to which the platform's own editorial and publishing systems participate in the generation, selection, circulation, amplification or monetisation of content," he said. The company denied knowingly targeting such s at people.Queries to Meta did not elicit a response.

World.title: India’s cleanest city Indore slips from top spot in clean air survey; Mayor assures anti-pollution steps
World.content:
The local administration has blamed PM10 particles — dangerous airborne particles — for vehicle-heavy Indore’s slide from first place to second in the 2026 Clean Air Survey and has announced intensified measures to reduce air pollution in India’s cleanest city.

In the survey, Indore, Madhya Pradesh’s commercial capital, scored 197 out of 200 in the category of cities with a population of over 1 million, while Lucknow ranked first with 198 points.

Jabalpur ranked third with 195 points, while Bhopal and Agra tied for fourth with 192 points each.

Indore, which topped the list with a score of 200 out of 200 in the 2025 survey, fell just one point short of Lucknow and failed to retain its position.

The Uttar Pradesh capital, besides Odisha’s Rourkela and Kalinga Nagar, emerged as a top performer under the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), with the Union Environment Ministry honouring their efforts at the fifth edition of the Swachh Vayu Sarvekshan Awards on Monday (September 7, 2026).

Cities and towns nationwide were ranked based on the Swachh Vayu Survekshan Framework released in 2022-23, which laid down measures to tackle road dust, vehicular emissions, and industrial pollution, among others.

Indore Mayor Pushyamitra Bhargava told PTI on Tuesday (September 8, 2026), “We scored one point lower than Lucknow in the survey due to (the city) lagging behind in PM10 particle standards.” Indore is the city with the highest vehicle density in Madhya Pradesh.

Mr. Bhargava assured steps will be taken throughout the year to reduce pollution from traffic and industries in the city, including PM10 particles.

He said public awareness initiatives like “Red Light On, Engine Off” at traffic signals, promotion of electric vehicles, and operation of e-buses will be accelerated to curb vehicular pollution.

Mr. Bhargava maintained concrete efforts will also be made to convert all vehicles collecting garbage from door-to-door to electric ones and to shift factories from diesel to green fuels like CNG.

PM10 (Particulate Matter-10) are ultra-fine particles present in the air with a diameter of 10 micrometres or less. These particles are produced by vehicle exhaust, road dust, and industrial emissions and enter the human respiratory system through breathing.

The key parameters of the Clean Air Survey include measures taken by urban bodies to reduce PM10 levels.

Officials said despite lagging behind Lucknow by just one point in the Clean Air Survey, Indore’s overall air quality record remains strong.

According to Indore Municipal Corporation data, the city recorded a decline of more than 15% in PM10 levels compared to previous years, with the annual average PM10 level this year being around 81 micrograms per cubic metre.

The National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) set the annual average level of PM10 in air at 60 micrograms per cubic metre for residential, industrial, and rural areas.

According to municipal corporation data, the Air Quality Index (AQI) in Indore remained below 200 on average on more than 98% of the days during the Clean Air Survey evaluation period.

An AQI between 0 and 50 is considered ‘Good’, 51 to 100 ‘Satisfactory’, 101 to 200 ‘Moderate’, 201 to 300 ‘Poor’, 301 to 400 ‘Very Poor’, and 401 to 500 ‘Severe’.

Municipal corporation officials said to control dust, approximately 700 kilometres of roads in the city are being swept daily with machines, and various measures are being taken to dispose of construction waste.

Indore has topped the National Sanitation Survey, a separate ranking competition of cities conducted by the central government, for eight consecutive times.

World.title: Justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge sworn-in as Chief Justice of Calcutta High Court
World.content:
Justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge was sworn in as the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court on Wednesday (September 9, 2026) by West Bengal Governor R.N. Ravi.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and Assembly Speaker Rathindra Bose were among the dignitaries present at the ceremony.

The event took place in Court Room 1, the Chief Justice's seat.

Chief Justice Ghuge was a judge at the Bombay High Court before his present appointment.

World.title: U.S. military says it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers; Tehran hits back at American targets in Jordan
World.content:
The U.S. military said it destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) in response to the latest attacks on its warships, and Tehran hit back at American targets in Jordan, the latest burst of back-and-forth strikes that have lurched the sides back toward open hostilities in a more than six-month-old war.

Following the American strikes, Iran launched missiles toward U.S. targets in Jordan, Iranian state-run media said.

Jordan's military said its air defence systems intercepted 18 ballistic missiles launched toward its territory and two others fell in places where no one lives.

It said it has no reports of casualties. Jordan is a staunch U.S. ally that hosts American forces, making the kingdom's military bases a target of repeated Iranian strikes. U.S. Central Command said it had no information to offer.

The latest strikes are part of a dual economic and military approach by President Donald Trump as he struggles to bring an end to the war.

The Trump administration on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) also imposed sanctions on additional elements of Iran's aviation industry, targeting more than two dozen commercial and private airlines as well as foreign cargo service providers, in its new push to isolate Tehran from its remaining trading partners.

Both the U.S. and Iran are seeking to exert control over the Strait of Hormuz, where about one-fifth of the world's oil passed before the war began. Rising energy prices are posing political problems for Mr. Trump and his Republican Party ahead of the November midterm elections. A barrel of international standard Brent crude briefly climbed as high as $99.46 on Tuesday (September 8, 2026).

The U.S. forces also destroyed three Iranian oil tankers on Saturday (September 5, 2026) after Iran's Revolutionary Guards tried to attack a U.S. aircraft carrier and destroyer with ballistic missiles, warning that it would, “if necessary, destroy Iran's limited and exposed oil fleet”.

Iran later said it planned to announce a new “exclusion zone” near the Strait of Hormuz aimed at vessels intending to transit.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the U.S. will not allow Iran's attacks to go unanswered.

“Iran continues to try to hit U.S. naval ships. And for every time they do that or try to do that, they're going to lose tankers. And I think you'll see that again today,” Mr. Rubio told reporters on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) when asked about the latest attacks in Iran while on a trip to Colombia.

Danny Citrinowicz, an Iran expert at Israel's Institute for National Security Studies, warned that such back-and-forth strikes can only risk more retaliation and further impact on the global economy.

“There is no kinetic solution to the Strait of Hormuz problem,” he said on social media. “Every attempt to impose one only brings Washington and Tehran closer to an escalation that may become increasingly difficult to control.” U.S. Central Command said the military struck the tankers on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) after the Revolutionary Guards targeted a Navy warship with ballistic missiles twice over the past two days.

“The U.S. warship successfully evaded the attempted Iranian attacks and continued to patrol regional waters. No American personnel were harmed,” it said in a statement.

It said the Iranian tankers destroyed on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) were the Kivik, Charminar, Horizon 1 and the Riesco in the Gulf of Oman. The U.S. military also destroyed the vessel Derya, which was located near Kharg Island in the Strait of Hormuz. The statement said the crews of the five vessels were told to abandon ship before the attacks.

Iranian state television also reported the U.S. strikes, saying U.S. forces attacked Iranian oil tankers near the southern port of Jask and near Kharg Island in the Persian Gulf. It said the crews were evacuated.

An Iranian state TV reporter in Jask said an Iranian tanker was struck near the coast of Yekbeni. State TV later reported that the U.S. military attacked a second tanker near waters off Jask. Separately, state television reported that another Iranian tanker was attacked in the Kharg Island anchorage area.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) warned crews of oil tankers near ports in Kuwait and Bahrain to immediately leave their vessels, saying the ships could be targeted in retaliation for US attacks on Iranian tankers. It accused Kuwait and Bahrain of hosting US forces and assisting in the attacks.

A U.S. blockade of Iranian ports has squeezed the country's economy by limiting its oil exports, while the American military has been helping a limited number of ships transit on a route through the Strait of Hormuz off Oman. Tehran wants ships to follow a route that it chooses through the strait, which was considered an international waterway before the war.

Iran's Guards attacks 2 US vessels, 8 tankers, 10 ships in Gulf, Strait of Hormuz
